seeker_flawed_plan: Tatiana plans to use the same chemical indicator strips she uses for her autoclave pouches to verify the sterilizer itself, because she assumes any strip that changes color proves the cycle ran correctly.
flaw_explanation: Chemical indicator strips on pouches are external indicators that only show exposure to sterilization conditions, not whether the autoclave's internal parameters were met; verifying the machine itself calls for a different class of indicator placed inside a test load. Using the wrong type could give her a false sense of the machine's performance, so she would need to redo the check with the proper indicator, wasting time.

judge_notes.deepseek: Using pouch external indicators to verify the sterilizer itself is a real error that could mask machine failure and pose infection-control risk, not just wasted time.
judge_notes.glm: The plan is plausible in a tattoo studio sterilization discussion, the flaw (using external pouch indicators instead of an in-load biological/chemical indicator to verify the autoclave) is a real, verifiable error, and acting on it only wastes time with no health or safety risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Ephraim plans to apply the blur effect to only a few sample frames throughout each clip and rely on the editing software to automatically extend the effect across the whole timeline, saving him from manually tracking the blur over every frame.
flaw_explanation: Most editing programs do not propagate a static effect to neighboring frames on their own; Ephraim needs to either keyframe the blur or use an automatic tracking/masking tool. Otherwise the blur will only appear on the frames he touched, leaving the rest of the clip unedited and requiring a redo.

judge_notes.deepseek: The plan is a plausible editing shortcut whose flaw is a concrete, verifiable limitation of most editing software regarding effect propagation.
judge_notes.glm: The plan is a plausible but mistaken assumption about video editing software that would only cause wasted time redoing the blur work, fits naturally into the footage-anonymization conversation, and describes a specific, verifiable technical error about effect propagation.

seeker_flawed_plan: Samson plans to order the anti-slip coating for the ferry ramp in a single large batch sized from the ramp's flat surface area, figuring that measuring length times width gives the full quantity needed.
flaw_explanation: A ramp's actual coated area is larger than its flat footprint because the sloped surface is longer than its horizontal projection, and the measurement also ignores edge returns and any overlap or waste, so a batch sized from the flat area alone will come up short.

judge_notes.glm: Underestimating coating quantity from flat footprint is a real, verifiable error that fits the shipyard coating topic, and the worst case is a short order causing delay and modest extra cost.
judge_notes.deepseek: Under-ordering anti-slip coating for a ferry ramp could leave a safety-critical surface untreated, so the flaw carries real safety and cost consequences.

seeker_flawed_plan: Abigail plans to check each calibration sticker by looking only at its printed expiration date and treating any instrument with a current sticker as verified, skipping the tolerance class or accuracy grade shown elsewhere on the lab's records.
flaw_explanation: A sticker's expiration date only confirms when calibration was last performed, not which accuracy class the instrument was calibrated to; two instruments can both have valid dates while belonging to different tolerance grades. By ignoring the class, Abigail may log an instrument as fully verified when it is only suitable for a coarser measurement, wasting time on a recheck later.

judge_notes.glm: Ignoring tolerance class while trusting sticker dates is a plausible, verifiable procedural error with only minor consequences like wasted time or a later recheck.
judge_notes.deepseek: Ignoring tolerance class is a real, verifiable error that could cause mislabeled verification and rework, but only minor inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Youssef plans to model the sprinkler water demand by multiplying the flow rate of a single most-remote sprinkler head by the total number of heads in the system to get the overall demand figure.
flaw_explanation: Only a small design area of sprinklers operates at once, not all heads simultaneously, so the demand is calculated from the flow of the heads within that design area plus a hose allowance. Multiplying by every head vastly overestimates demand, leading to wasted time redoing calculations and an oversized model.

judge_notes.glm: The plan plausibly arises in a sprinkler design conversation, and its flaw—ignoring the hydraulic design area and hose allowance—is a clear, verifiable error with only wasted-effort consequences.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan fits the sprinkler-design topic, and the flaw is a specific, verifiable hydraulic error that would mainly cause wasted effort and an oversized model.

seeker_flawed_plan: Ari plans to mount the smoke detectors on the ceiling near the corners of the studio, reasoning that corners are the most structurally solid spots and will keep the wiring runs short and tidy.
flaw_explanation: Smoke tends to pool and travel along the flat ceiling surface before reaching wall corners, and corner placement can leave a dead-air pocket that delays detection; detectors perform better out in the open field of the ceiling, well away from corners and walls.

judge_notes.glm: Corner placement creates dead-air pockets that delay smoke detection, which is a genuine fire-safety risk rather than a mere inconvenience, but the belief fits the renovation topic and the flaw is a well-documented, verifiable placement error.
judge_notes.deepseek: Corner-mounted detectors can delay smoke detection due to dead-air pockets, a genuine safety flaw.

seeker_flawed_plan: Aditya plans to specify the sub-slab vapor extraction piping's pressure-field test by capping the riser, pulling a vacuum with a shop vacuum, and recording the vacuum reading at the riser as the indicator of communication across the slab footprint.
flaw_explanation: A shop vacuum's airflow and vacuum are unregulated and far too weak and variable to establish a meaningful pressure field or communication radius; the readout reflects the vacuum at the riser rather than the sub-slab pressure distribution being mapped, so the test result would be uninterpretable and the field work would need to be redone with a proper blower and monitoring points.

judge_notes.glm: Using a shop vacuum for a sub-slab pressure-field test is a plausible but technically flawed approach that would only waste time and require redoing the test with proper equipment.
judge_notes.deepseek: A shop vacuum cannot establish a meaningful sub-slab pressure field, so the test would be uninterpretable and require redoing with proper equipment—costly but not a health/safety/legal risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Greta plans to use a free consumer file-sharing account with a simple shared password for the sign-in spreadsheet, since that will let her and the front-desk volunteer access it from any device without paying for anything.
flaw_explanation: Free consumer accounts typically don't offer per-user accounts or audit logs, so the shared password means changes can't be attributed to anyone and the login isn't protected adequately. Greta will likely have to redo the setup with proper accounts later, wasting time she's already spent configuring the free option.

judge_notes.deepseek: Shared-password consumer file sharing for patient sign-in data creates real privacy/security risk, not just minor inconvenience.
judge_notes.glm: The plan involves patient sign-in data on an insecure shared consumer account, which risks privacy/HIPAA compliance, not just wasted time, though the flaw itself is relevant and clearly verifiable.

seeker_flawed_plan: Morgan plans to order cryogenic gloves in a snug, well-tailored fit like ordinary work gloves, reasoning that a close fit will give better grip and dexterity when handling transfer lines and vials.
flaw_explanation: Cryogenic gloves are meant to fit loosely so they can be pulled off instantly, and so that a layer of trapped air inside can act as insulation. A snug glove removes that air gap and takes longer to remove, giving a worse result rather than better protection.

judge_notes.glm: Snug cryogenic gloves can trap spilled cryogen against skin and delay removal, creating a real frostbite risk rather than mere inconvenience.
judge_notes.deepseek: A snug cryogenic glove fit is a genuine safety hazard because it removes the insulating air gap and impedes rapid removal, risking cold burns.

seeker_flawed_plan: Nikola plans to put the checklist items in alphabetical order so it's easy to find a given item, and to print it on a single double-sided sheet with the date and inspector name at the bottom.
flaw_explanation: Alphabetical ordering separates steps that belong together in a functional sequence, so an inspector working down the list would jump between unrelated checks and could skip a dependent step, making the inspection slower and less reliable; a logical grouping by assembly or inspection stage would work better.

judge_notes.deepseek: Alphabetizing a procedural checklist is a plausible but flawed organizational choice that mainly causes inefficiency and possible skipped steps, not serious harm.
judge_notes.glm: Alphabetical ordering of an inspection checklist is a plausible but flawed plan that would only cause wasted time and a less reliable inspection, and the flaw is specific and verifiable.

seeker_flawed_plan: Hira plans to evaluate the privacy impact assessment by comparing it against the district's general data governance checklist first, then reading the tracking-specific sections afterward to see how they line up.
flaw_explanation: The general checklist is organized around enterprise data systems rather than location tracking, so working through it first will flag items that don't apply and bury the tracking-specific questions; reading the tracking sections first would give the right frame and make the general checklist a quick cross-check instead of a long detour.

judge_notes.glm: The plan is a plausible, low-stakes approach to reviewing a privacy assessment, and the flaw—that a generic enterprise checklist is the wrong starting frame for location tracking—is a specific, verifiable practical error.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan is a low-stakes ordering choice, fits the privacy-assessment topic, and the flaw about checklist mismatch is a concrete, verifiable practical error.

seeker_flawed_plan: Kofi plans to fire his matte test tiles on the same shelf and in the same firing as his finished bowls, so he can judge the matte surface and confirm the look of each combination in one load.
flaw_explanation: Test tiles should be fired separately from finished work: glaze behavior and matte development can differ with placement and firing conditions, and if a combination runs or pinholes, it can damage the bowls in the same load. Firing separately costs only an extra firing and some time, but it gives a truer read on the glaze before committing the bowls.

judge_notes.deepseek: Firing test tiles with finished bowls risks glaze runs or pinholes damaging the bowls, a real practical error beyond mere inconvenience.
judge_notes.glm: Firing test tiles with finished bowls is a common but flawed practice that risks ruining the bowls if a glaze runs, and it fits naturally into this glaze-selection conversation.

seeker_flawed_plan: Thiago plans to document the sanitary weld inspection by taking a few photos of the weld with his phone's camera flash pointed straight at the joint, believing the bright flash will highlight any surface irregularities well enough for the inspection record.
flaw_explanation: A head-on flash washes out the very surface detail he is trying to capture, since shadows are what reveal pits, ridges, and misalignment in a weld. Raking the light at a shallow angle from the side is what makes such features visible, so his photos will likely come out flat and need to be retaken.

judge_notes.glm: Head-on flash washing out weld detail is a real, verifiable photography error, fits the sanitary weld inspection topic, and worst case is only retaking photos.
judge_notes.deepseek: Head-on flash would wash out weld surface detail, so the photos would be flat and need retaking—a minor inconvenience with no safety or legal risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Becca plans to schedule the firmware rollout for the parcel lockers at the end of the business day, reasoning that overnight downtime will be invisible to users and the update will be finished by morning.
flaw_explanation: The lockers' update process requires each unit to stay powered and connected for a validation handshake that only completes when the staging server is actively syncing, and that sync is paused outside business hours, so the updates would stall overnight and need to be restarted the next day.

judge_notes.glm: The plan is plausible for the scene, and the flaw—that overnight updates stall because the staging server sync pauses after hours—is a specific, verifiable practical error with only minor consequences like wasted time and a delayed rollout.
judge_notes.deepseek: The overnight rollout would stall because the validation sync is paused outside business hours, causing delays but no serious harm.

seeker_flawed_plan: Roland plans to buy four rigid (fixed-direction) casters for the lab bench because they are cheaper than swivel models and he only needs to roll the bench straight down the hallway to its new spot.
flaw_explanation: With all four casters fixed, the bench can only move in straight lines and cannot be steered around corners or through doorways, so Roland will likely have to return the rigid casters and order swivel ones (or a swivel-rigid mix), wasting time and shipping costs.

judge_notes.glm: Buying four rigid casters is a benign, topic-relevant plan whose clear main flaw—that fixed casters cannot steer around corners or through doorways—is easily verified.
judge_notes.deepseek: Rigid casters on all four corners prevent steering, a clear practical flaw causing only minor cost/time inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Naima plans to skip the warm-up period and start the calibration routine immediately after switching the breathalyzer on, since the unit powers up in seconds and she wants to finish before the equipment room closes.
flaw_explanation: Breathalyzer sensors need a warm-up period (often 10-30 minutes) after power-on before their readings stabilize. Calibrating against an unstable sensor will produce an offset that fails verification, so she will have to wait for warm-up anyway and redo the whole procedure.

judge_notes.deepseek: Skipping warm-up just wastes time and forces a redo, which fits the calibration topic and is a clear, verifiable procedural error.
judge_notes.glm: Skipping the warm-up would only waste time and require redoing the calibration, fits naturally into the breathalyzer calibration conversation, and the warm-up requirement is a clear, verifiable technical fact.

seeker_flawed_plan: Lisette plans to interpret the motor specs by assuming that the 'duty cycle' percentage listed on each vendor sheet means the percentage of a full day the motor can run, so she'll rule out any motor rated below 50% for an acute-care ward bed.
flaw_explanation: Duty cycle in motor specs is expressed as a percentage of a short standardized operating interval (e.g., on for X minutes out of every 10-minute cycle), not a share of the day. Comparing it to a daily usage figure will cause her to wrongly eliminate suitable motors and have to redo the comparison.

judge_notes.glm: Misreading duty cycle as a daily percentage is a clear, verifiable spec-interpretation error that fits the procurement conversation and only wastes time.
judge_notes.deepseek: Misreading duty cycle as a daily percentage is a plausible, verifiable spec error that would mainly cause wasted time and a worse comparison, not real harm.

seeker_flawed_plan: Nayeli plans to label each suspension cable in the rigging plan by the color of its protective sleeve (red, blue, green) rather than by its ceiling anchor point number, so the install crew can match cables to positions at a glance.
flaw_explanation: The sleeves' colors were assigned per shipment batch, not per position, so two cables destined for different anchor points share a color while one anchor has no matching color at all. Following her labels will send the crew back to re-measure and re-sort every cable, costing time but nothing else.

judge_notes.glm: Labeling cables by shipment-batch sleeve color rather than anchor point is a clear, verifiable practical error that only wastes the crew's time, and it fits naturally into a rigging plan review.
judge_notes.deepseek: Color-based cable labeling is a plausible rigging-plan shortcut, and the batch-color mismatch is a concrete, verifiable flaw causing only rework.

seeker_flawed_plan: Noemi plans to take her noise measurements only while the press is running its normal stamping cycle, assuming the readings during idle moments between strokes are quiet enough that they can be ignored entirely.
flaw_explanation: The press's idle periods still contribute sound to the worker's overall dose, so ignoring them will underestimate the average exposure and make the readings slightly inaccurate. She would need to sample across the full operating pattern, including pauses, to get a representative average.

judge_notes.glm: Ignoring idle-period noise would only slightly skew the average exposure reading, a minor accuracy issue that fits naturally with measuring noise near a stamping press and is a clear, verifiable sampling error.
judge_notes.deepseek: Ignoring idle periods underestimates noise dose, but the error is a minor measurement inaccuracy rather than a serious safety or legal risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Yarael plans to store each audit log entry as a separate plain-text file named with a timestamp, believing that one file per event will make it easy to trace individual actions later.
flaw_explanation: Plain-text files have no tamper-evident structure, so any edit or deletion goes unnoticed and the logs cannot be reliably trusted for audit purposes; a hash-chained or append-only format is needed to detect changes.

judge_notes.glm: The one-file-per-event plan fits the audit-log topic, its main flaw (no tamper-evidence without hash chaining or append-only storage) is a verifiable technical error, and acting on it would mainly cause rework and weaker audit integrity rather than serious harm.
judge_notes.deepseek: Plain-text per-event logs lack tamper-evidence, a real audit-integrity flaw that fits the scene.

seeker_flawed_plan: Vivian plans to protect her source by keeping all identifying details in a single password-protected spreadsheet on the newsroom's shared drive, believing that a locked file with restricted access will satisfy her editor's demand to see who the source is without actually revealing the name in the story.
flaw_explanation: A shared-drive file, even password-protected, is visible as an existing file to anyone with drive access, and editors with admin rights can typically see or reset permissions, so the file's presence invites the very scrutiny she wants to avoid. Keeping the name out of the draft does nothing to answer the editor's demand, and the locked spreadsheet becomes an obvious target rather than a safeguard.

judge_notes.glm: The password-protected shared-drive plan fits the confidentiality conversation, its flaw (visible file and admin-accessible permissions inviting editor scrutiny) is concrete and verifiable, and the worst realistic outcome is professional embarrassment or a worse result rather than serious harm.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan risks exposing the source through shared-drive visibility and admin access, so it carries real confidentiality and safety stakes rather than mere inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Celina plans to log the cracked training extinguisher gauges as unusable only if the needle sits outside the green zone, assuming that as long as the reading is in the green, a crack in the gauge face is just cosmetic and the unit can stay in rotation.
flaw_explanation: A crack in the gauge face or lens can let dust and moisture in and makes the reading itself unreliable, so the needle position alone is not a valid test of usability. Training extinguishers with cracked gauges should be pulled from rotation and tagged for gauge replacement regardless of where the needle points.

judge_notes.glm: The needle-position-only rule is a clear, verifiable error, and since these are training extinguishers the worst realistic outcome is a practice unit failing or being wasted, not real danger.
judge_notes.deepseek: A cracked gauge lens can admit moisture and dust, making the reading unreliable, so keeping the unit in rotation based on needle position alone is a genuine safety error.

seeker_flawed_plan: Celine plans to label each soil sample jar using a regular ballpoint pen on ordinary adhesive labels, since that is what she has on hand and it seems quicker than preparing anything special before the sampling.
flaw_explanation: Damp or muddy jars from a creek-side site will make ordinary ink and adhesive labels smear or peel off, so the markings may become unreadable before the samples are logged. Field documentation typically uses waterproof ink and weatherproof labels to keep identifiers intact.

judge_notes.glm: Unreadable sample labels could break chain of custody, invalidating legally significant spill evidence, so the outcome goes beyond minor inconvenience; the flaw is relevant to the scene and is a specific, verifiable field-practice error.
judge_notes.deepseek: Unreadable sample labels could compromise chain-of-custody documentation and legal defensibility, so the flaw is a real, specific, and consequential error.

seeker_flawed_plan: Dita plans to scoop fine dry sand from a dune behind the beach for the ring mold, believing that the finer, more uniform grains will capture sharper detail on the ring's surface than coarser beach sand.
flaw_explanation: Fine dry dune sand lacks the binder and clay content that casting sand needs, so it will not hold together or pack firmly around the pattern. Dita will likely end up with a crumbly mold and a rough or failed casting, and will need to redo it with proper casting sand.

judge_notes.glm: Using dry dune sand without clay binder would only waste time and yield a failed mold, it fits naturally into a sand-casting conversation, and the flaw is a verifiable, specific error about casting sand needing clay binder.
judge_notes.deepseek: Fine dry dune sand lacks binder/clay so it won't hold a mold, a clear practical flaw fitting the casting topic.

seeker_flawed_plan: Nadim plans to read and record the color-based swab test results immediately after swabbing each surface, within about a minute, since he believes the indicator changes color as soon as allergen residue is present.
flaw_explanation: These swab kits require a fixed incubation period (often several minutes) for the color reaction to fully develop, so reading them right away can show a false negative or pale color. He would need to repeat the swabs or wait and re-read them, wasting time.

judge_notes.glm: Reading allergen swabs before the incubation completes could yield false negatives that let contaminated product pass, a real health/safety risk, not just wasted time.
judge_notes.deepseek: Reading swab results before the required incubation period is a clear, verifiable procedural error that mainly wastes time and yields unreliable readings.

seeker_flawed_plan: Sabine plans to estimate each returned lithium battery's stored energy by multiplying its labeled voltage by its labeled capacity in amp-hours and then summing those watt-hour figures to set the bin's storage density. She believes that comparing this total against a watt-hour limit per bin will give her a straightforward, uniform measure of how full the bin is.
flaw_explanation: Multiplying voltage by amp-hours gives watt-hours, but the labeled capacity is measured at the cell's nominal voltage, so the resulting figure is nominal energy, not the actual stored energy that matters for storage limits; the calculation also ignores that packs mix different chemistries and states of charge, so the sum will not correspond to a consistent density measure.

judge_notes.glm: The watt-hour summation fits the conversation naturally and the flaw is verifiable, but misjudging lithium battery storage density in a shared bin setting carries real fire-safety risk, so the worst outcome is not merely minor inconvenience.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan concerns lithium battery storage safety, so errors could cause fire risk, and the stated flaw correctly identifies that nominal watt-hours ignore chemistry and state of charge.

seeker_flawed_plan: Lars plans to start by thoroughly cleaning the dishwasher's filter and drain sump before anything else, since he believes a partially clogged drain is making the machine work harder during the rinse cycle and that this extra strain is what trips the breaker.
flaw_explanation: A clogged drain affects water flow, not electrical draw, so cleaning it will not address an overcurrent condition that trips a breaker. He will waste time on a cleaning task while the real cause—likely a component drawing excess current during rinse—go unexamined.

judge_notes.glm: The plan fits the dish-pit conversation, worst case is wasted cleaning time, and the flaw is a specific, verifiable diagnostic error since a restricted drain mainly affects flow and cycle timing rather than causing the overcurrent that trips a breaker.
judge_notes.deepseek: Cleaning a clogged drain won't fix an overcurrent breaker trip, so the plan wastes time while the real electrical fault goes unaddressed.

seeker_flawed_plan: Umi plans to store all her opened baking supplies in glass jars with lids that rest on top but don't seal tightly, believing that as long as the lids are on, the contents will be protected.
flaw_explanation: A loosely fitted lid without a gasket or screw seal leaves small gaps around the rim, so it will not actually keep anything out of the jar. The supplies need airtight containers with properly sealing lids to be protected.

judge_notes.glm: Loosely fitted lids failing to keep pantry moths out is a minor, verifiable practical error that fits naturally into a conversation about storing flour.
judge_notes.deepseek: Loose lids won't keep pantry moths out, but the consequence is only spoiled flour, a minor inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Evelina plans to judge the adequacy of the tower's lightning protection by checking whether the air terminal at the top is the tallest point on the structure, reasoning that a rod that clears everything else by a foot or two must be protecting the tank beneath it.
flaw_explanation: Height alone does not establish a protected zone; the air terminal's placement relative to the tank and its connections to the down conductors and grounding system matter more, so a tall rod can still leave parts of the structure outside the intended protection area.

judge_notes.deepseek: Judging lightning protection by rod height alone is a real safety error, since protection depends on placement, down conductors, and grounding.
judge_notes.glm: The height-only heuristic is a plausible but flawed assessment approach that fits the scene, and the flaw about protection zones and grounding is a real, verifiable error with only minor practical consequences.

seeker_flawed_plan: Meghana plans to round all GPS coordinates to three decimal places before starting any processing, assuming this level of precision is enough to shrink the dataset and that it won't affect her analysis.
flaw_explanation: Three decimal places corresponds to roughly 100 meters of position error, which is far coarser than the raw GPS data and will blur short trips and turns. This will degrade map-matching and stay-point detection results, forcing her to re-download the raw traces and redo the work.

judge_notes.glm: Rounding GPS coordinates to three decimals (~100 m error) is a plausible, verifiable mistake that would degrade analysis but only cause wasted work, fitting naturally into a GPS anonymization discussion.
judge_notes.deepseek: Rounding to three decimals (~100 m error) is a real, verifiable flaw that would degrade map-matching and stay-point detection, but the consequence is only wasted time and rework.

seeker_flawed_plan: Uri plans to measure his tire tread depth with a standard ruler by inserting it into the grooves at the center of the tread and treating any reading above 2/32 of an inch as proof the tires are fine for winter.
flaw_explanation: A standard ruler is hard to read accurately inside a narrow groove, and winter driving generally calls for much more tread (around 4/32 to 6/32) than the 2/32 legal minimum. Using the wrong threshold and tool would lead him to keep tires that are inadequate for snow, giving a worse result rather than a safety-critical one in this framing.

judge_notes.deepseek: The plan uses an unreadable tool and a too-low 2/32 threshold, so it could keep unsafe winter tires, making the outcome safety-critical rather than merely inconvenient.
judge_notes.glm: The plan fits the tire-shop conversation naturally, and its flaw—using a hard-to-read ruler with the 2/32 legal minimum instead of the 4/32–6/32 winter threshold—leads only to a worse tire-replacement decision, not a safety-critical outcome in this framing.

seeker_flawed_plan: Alvaro plans to evaluate the roof membrane seams by pressing his palm flat against each seam for about thirty seconds and judging its condition from how warm it feels, treating warmer spots as better-adhered seams, and he will base his survey notes entirely on that warmth test.
flaw_explanation: Seam temperature mostly reflects sun exposure, shading, and the material underneath rather than the quality of the weld, so warm spots are often just areas getting more direct sunlight. This means the warmth test would misclassify many perfectly good seams as weak and vice versa, wasting Alvaro's survey time and producing misleading notes.

judge_notes.glm: The warmth-based seam test is plausible to raise in this roof-survey conversation, its flaw (temperature reflecting sun exposure rather than weld quality) is a clear, verifiable error, and the worst outcome is wasted time and misleading notes rather than any safety or legal risk.
judge_notes.deepseek: The warmth test is a plausible but flawed proxy for seam adhesion, and its worst consequence is wasted time and misleading survey notes rather than safety or legal harm.

seeker_flawed_plan: Bram plans to check the chimney's crack pattern by looking only at the inside faces of the flue from the rooftop opening, since that is where the liner will sit, and to judge the outside brickwork afterward from the ground.
flaw_explanation: Cracks that matter often show on the exterior faces of the stack while the flue interior looks sound, so inspecting only the flue from above can miss the pattern he needs; the outside should be checked closely at the same time, not from the ground.

judge_notes.glm: Skipping a close exterior inspection could mean installing a liner in a structurally compromised chimney, risking fire, CO exposure, or costly rework, so the outcome is not merely minor inconvenience.
judge_notes.deepseek: Missing exterior crack patterns could lead to unsafe liner installation, so the flaw carries real safety risk and is a specific, verifiable inspection error.

seeker_flawed_plan: Boris plans to draw the smoke-control zone boundaries on the charrette floor plans first and only afterward check where the existing corridor doors and rated walls actually fall, treating the zoning as a purely geometric exercise.
flaw_explanation: Smoke-control zones have to align with physical barriers such as rated walls and door assemblies, so drawing the boundaries before checking those conditions usually produces zones that cross open corridors or unrated partitions and have to be redrawn.

judge_notes.glm: Drawing zone boundaries before checking rated walls and doors is a plausible but flawed approach that would only cause redraws and wasted effort in a design charrette.
judge_notes.deepseek: Drawing smoke-control zones before checking rated walls and doors is a real, verifiable design error that can compromise life safety, so it is not merely a minor inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Kelechi plans to buy all the snacks for the classroom party a full week ahead of time, believing that shopping early will make the planning less stressful and guarantee nothing is forgotten.
flaw_explanation: The flaw is that many allergy-friendly snacks, like fresh fruit or certain bakery items, go stale or spoil within a few days, so buying a week early means some items will be past their best by party day. Kelechi would need to re-shop for the perishables, wasting time and money.

judge_notes.glm: Buying perishable allergy-safe snacks a week early would only cause wasted time and money from spoilage, fits naturally into the party-snack planning conversation, and the flaw is a clear, verifiable practical error.
judge_notes.deepseek: Buying perishable allergy-friendly snacks a week early is a real, verifiable practical error causing spoilage and wasted money, but only minor ordinary inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Orlandoe plans to inspect the water-damaged routers by opening each case and photographing the circuit boards with a phone camera under the closet's normal overhead lighting, treating clear photos as sufficient to spot any water damage or corrosion.
flaw_explanation: Corrosion and water residue on circuit boards are often faint, discolored patches tucked under chips and connectors, and ordinary overhead lighting plus a phone camera can easily wash them out or leave them in shadow. A bright directed light or magnification is usually needed, so this method risks missing damage and giving a false all-clear.

judge_notes.glm: The plan fits the scene naturally, and its flaw—faint corrosion being missed under ordinary overhead lighting—is a specific, verifiable practical error whose worst outcome is only wasted time or a false all-clear on equipment.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan fits the router-inspection scene, and the flaw is a concrete, verifiable practical error about lighting and camera limits for spotting corrosion.

seeker_flawed_plan: Nefeli plans to set the alert thresholds by watching the sensor readings at the height of tonight's storm and picking a level just above whatever the drains peak at, so the alarms only trigger in genuinely extreme conditions.
flaw_explanation: Calibrating thresholds against a single storm's peak bakes that storm's idiosyncrasies into the baseline; a heavier or lighter rain event would produce constant false alarms or missed alerts, forcing her to redo the calibration later. Thresholds should be derived from normal operating levels plus a defined margin, not from one peak observation.

judge_notes.glm: The plan fits the scene and the flaw is a real, verifiable calibration error, but a threshold set too high could cause missed flood alerts in an underpass, which carries genuine safety risk rather than mere inconvenience.
judge_notes.deepseek: Calibrating flood alert thresholds to a single storm's peak risks missed alerts or false alarms in other conditions, a genuine safety-relevant flaw.

seeker_flawed_plan: Ruth plans to wait until her husband's registered donor status is confirmed before saying anything to the donation coordinator, believing that if he isn't registered, she isn't allowed to bring up the topic at all.
flaw_explanation: Ruth assumes the conversation can only happen after registry status is verified, but the coordinator can and typically does discuss the process and answer questions regardless of registration status. Waiting just delays her getting guidance and support, costing her time during an already stressful day.

judge_notes.glm: Ruth's mistaken belief that she can't approach the donation coordinator before registry verification is plausible in this scene, verifiable, and only costs her delayed guidance and support.
judge_notes.deepseek: Waiting for registry confirmation only delays guidance and support, a minor inconvenience with no real risk, and the flaw is a clear, verifiable misconception about when the coordinator can discuss donation.

seeker_flawed_plan: Ainhoa plans to build her exposure spreadsheet using each tool's vibration magnitude figure taken straight from the manufacturer's specification sheet, since that number seems like the official value to use for daily total calculations.
flaw_explanation: Manufacturer vibration figures come from standardized laboratory test conditions, not real-world use, and actual tool vibration on site often differs substantially depending on materials, tool wear, and grip. Using the spec-sheet number will produce totals that do not reflect the crews' real exposure, requiring the data to be gathered again.

judge_notes.glm: Using spec-sheet vibration figures is a plausible but mistaken approach that yields inaccurate spreadsheet totals requiring re-measurement, a clear, verifiable error with only wasted-effort consequences as framed.
judge_notes.deepseek: Using spec-sheet vibration values instead of real-world measurements understates exposure and risks health, so the flaw is real and central.

seeker_flawed_plan: Hussein believes that a label dilution ratio of 1:64 means 1 part concentrate plus 64 parts water, so he plans to mix one cup of concentrate with 64 cups of water and record that as the correct dilution.
flaw_explanation: The flaw is in how he interprets the ratio: on most disinfectant labels, 1:64 refers to the final dilution, meaning 1 part concentrate in 64 parts total solution, i.e., 63 parts water. His version makes the mixture slightly weaker than intended, which could just mean redoing the batch if he notices the mismatch.

judge_notes.deepseek: Under-diluting disinfectant in a childcare kitchen could leave pathogens active, posing a real health risk rather than mere inconvenience.
judge_notes.glm: The ratio misreading is a plausible, verifiable label-interpretation error that fits the daycare disinfectant topic, and per the stated flaw the worst case is a slightly weak batch needing a redo.

seeker_flawed_plan: Stellan plans to rank the low-bid parking garage repair proposals by adding up each bidder's itemized unit prices and comparing those sums directly, treating the lowest arithmetic total as the best value.
flaw_explanation: The itemized unit prices are estimated quantities multiplied by rates, and bidders often omit or reword line items differently, so the summed totals are not comparable across bids; the official bid total and the scope each line covers must be reconciled before any ranking is meaningful.

judge_notes.deepseek: Summing incomparable itemized unit prices could misrank bids and lead to awarding a contract that is not actually the best value, a real procurement error.
judge_notes.glm: The plan is a plausible but flawed bid-evaluation approach for this procurement scene, its flaw (non-comparable itemized sums) is specific and verifiable, and the worst case is a poor ranking or wasted effort rather than safety, legal, or major harm.

seeker_flawed_plan: Bianca plans to test the scanner integration by using a phone photo of a barcode displayed on a laptop screen, assuming the robot's scanner will read it the same way it reads printed labels on packages.
flaw_explanation: Screen-displayed barcodes often fail to scan reliably because of glare, refresh-rate flicker, and contrast differences, and even when a scanner does read one, that result may not reflect how it performs on actual curved, glossy medication packaging. So the test could produce misleading failures or false confidence, wasting time.

judge_notes.glm: Testing with a screen-displayed barcode is a plausible but flawed method whose main problem—unreliable scanning due to glare, flicker, and unrepresentative packaging—is a verifiable practical error with only wasted-time consequences.
judge_notes.deepseek: Testing with a screen-displayed barcode is a plausible but flawed verification method whose worst outcome is wasted time and misleading results, not real harm.

seeker_flawed_plan: Harriet plans to draft the validation plan by testing every feature of the new system with a single set of test data, assuming one standard specimen dataset will exercise all the workflows, from accessioning to result reporting.
flaw_explanation: A single dataset will only follow one path through the system, so it won't reveal how the software behaves with variations like different specimen types, edge-case inputs, or alternate order configurations. She'll need several distinct test datasets covering the main workflow variations, which means rework when her single-dataset testing misses whole branches.

judge_notes.glm: The single-dataset testing plan fits the LIS validation topic naturally, its flaw (one dataset can't cover workflow variations) is specific and verifiable, and the worst outcome is rework and wasted effort rather than direct harm.
judge_notes.deepseek: Single-dataset testing misses workflow branches, a clear practical flaw, but the consequence is rework rather than safety or legal harm.

seeker_flawed_plan: Thiago plans to inspect the sanitary weld by first polishing the weld bead and surrounding metal to a bright mirror finish with a handheld abrasive pad, then checking for pits or crevices, reasoning that a clean, shiny surface will make any defect easier to see.
flaw_explanation: Polishing with an abrasive pad can smear and blur the weld's surface and round over the very crevice edges he needs to see, so the weld looks smoother and hides small defects rather than revealing them; inspection is better done on the undisturbed weld surface before any cosmetic polishing.

judge_notes.deepseek: Polishing before inspection can smear metal and hide crevices, a real and verifiable flaw, but the consequence is mainly a worse inspection result rather than serious harm.
judge_notes.glm: Polishing before inspection is a plausible but flawed inspection approach that fits the sanitary weld topic, and the error—that abrasion smears and rounds over defect edges—is specific and verifiable, with the worst case being a missed defect or wasted effort rather than immediate harm.

seeker_flawed_plan: Maliha plans to grind each sample of imported spice in a standard kitchen-style blender before running her tests, assuming a single quick grind is enough to make every jar's contents homogeneous.
flaw_explanation: A single short grind usually leaves spice particles unevenly mixed, so a subsample taken afterward may not represent the whole jar and her test results could be slightly off. She would need a longer, multi-stage grinding and mixing step to get a properly representative sample.

judge_notes.glm: The single-grind assumption is a plausible, verifiable sampling error with only minor consequences like inaccurate test results and wasted effort.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan fits the sampling-plan topic, and the homogeneity flaw is a real, verifiable practical error with only minor consequences.

seeker_flawed_plan: Morgan plans to select the thinnest, most dexterous cryogenic gloves available for every task in the bay, reasoning that better finger feel will make all the fittings and valve work quicker and more precise.
flaw_explanation: Thin gloves give poor thermal insulation and can stiffen or crack when chilled, so they are the wrong choice for tasks with prolonged contact or splashes; dexterity alone does not make a glove suitable for cryogenic handling.

judge_notes.glm: Choosing thin gloves for cryogenic work risks frostbite from splashes or prolonged contact, so the outcome is a real safety hazard, not mere inconvenience.
judge_notes.deepseek: Thin cryogenic gloves lack insulation and can stiffen or crack, posing real safety risks for prolonged contact or splashes, so the plan is not benign.

seeker_flawed_plan: Jun plans to validate the floodplain model's terrain inputs by comparing the simulated water surface elevations against the surveyed cross-section elevations at the channel's centerline, reasoning that a good match there confirms the whole floodplain is represented correctly.
flaw_explanation: Matching only at the channel centerline does not validate the floodplain terrain, because the centerline is the deepest part of the channel and is insensitive to errors in the overbank and floodplain elevations that actually drive flood extent.

judge_notes.glm: The centerline-only validation flaw is a real, specific modeling error that fits naturally into a floodplain model review, and acting on it risks only a flawed analysis, not safety or significant money.
judge_notes.deepseek: Relying on centerline-only validation could misrepresent flood extent and endanger people through flawed floodplain mapping.

seeker_flawed_plan: Anaya plans to space the temperature sensors evenly across the shelves, assuming uniform spacing gives uniform coverage regardless of where the cooling vents are located.
flaw_explanation: Refrigerator temperature is not uniform; the distribution depends on airflow patterns and proximity to cooling vents or the compressor, so sensors should be placed based on expected warm and cold zones rather than at even intervals. Evenly spaced sensors can cluster all readings in middling zones while missing the warmest and coldest spots.

judge_notes.glm: Misplaced sensors could miss warm/cold zones, risking undetected temperature excursions that spoil medications—a health, safety, and financial hazard, not a minor inconvenience.
judge_notes.deepseek: Evenly spacing sensors ignores airflow and vent proximity, risking missed hot/cold spots that could compromise pharmacy temperature monitoring and drug safety.

seeker_flawed_plan: Jorge plans to buy one single charger model for the entire fleet by picking the chair that has the largest battery capacity and matching a charger to that one, assuming it will then work fine for all the other chairs as well.
flaw_explanation: The flaw is that chairs in a fleet often have different battery voltages (for example 12V versus 24V systems), so a charger matched to the biggest chair may not be compatible with the smaller ones. Elspeth would point out that he needs to check each chair's battery voltage and chemistry, not just capacity, before choosing a single model.

judge_notes.glm: Mismatched chargers would mainly cause wasted money and returns, the plan fits the charger-selection conversation naturally, and the voltage/chemistry mismatch is a specific, verifiable flaw.
judge_notes.deepseek: Mismatched chargers can damage batteries or create fire/safety hazards, so the flaw is not merely a minor inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Lorena plans to measure the bottler's gasket grooves while the machine is hot from a morning run, figuring that warm measurements will better reflect the conditions the gasket will actually work in.
flaw_explanation: Metal components expand slightly when heated, so measurements taken while hot will read a bit larger than the cold dimensions the gasket is actually cut and installed to. This would lead to gaskets cut slightly too large, causing some refitting and wasted material.

judge_notes.glm: Measuring hot gasket grooves is a plausible on-topic mistake whose flaw (thermal expansion inflating hot measurements) is a clear, verifiable error with only minor cost consequences.
judge_notes.deepseek: Measuring hot grooves overstates dimensions due to thermal expansion, leading to oversized gaskets and minor waste, but no serious harm.

seeker_flawed_plan: Coralie plans to sort the turbidity readings into two groups by whether the spike happened on a weekday or a weekend, then compare the averages to see if the plant's raw water is more variable on weekends.
flaw_explanation: Splitting readings by day of week mixes up unrelated causes, because a spike's size depends on rainfall and runoff timing rather than the calendar; grouping that way scatters the same events across both buckets and makes any comparison meaningless.

judge_notes.glm: The plan is a harmless exploratory analysis, but the stated flaw mischaracterizes it—each spike falls into exactly one bucket, and comparing weekday vs. weekend averages is a legitimate (if weak) hypothesis test, not a meaningless error.
judge_notes.deepseek: Grouping turbidity spikes by weekday vs weekend is a plausible but flawed analysis whose main error is confounding calendar grouping with rainfall/runoff causes, with only minor consequences.

seeker_flawed_plan: Naveed plans to assess the swelling by measuring the pack's overall thickness with a ruler and comparing it to the manufacturer's listed dimensions, expecting that any puffing will show up as a uniform increase across the whole pack.
flaw_explanation: Swelling in LiPo packs is often localized to one cell or one spot in a pouch, so a single overall thickness measurement can read as normal even when a section is noticeably puffed. He would need to check each cell's width and look for uneven contours rather than rely on one number.

judge_notes.glm: A single overall thickness reading could falsely clear a locally puffed pack, leading him to charge or fly a fire-hazard battery, so the worst outcome is a real safety risk rather than mere inconvenience.
judge_notes.deepseek: A swollen LiPo battery poses real fire/safety risk, so relying on a single overall thickness measurement could miss localized puffing and lead to unsafe use.

seeker_flawed_plan: Ivan plans to pay off his highest-balance credit card first, reasoning that clearing the largest debt will reduce his monthly stress the most, and only after that card is at zero will he start putting anything into emergency savings.
flaw_explanation: Prioritizing the highest balance instead of the highest interest rate (the avalanche method) means Ivan will likely pay more interest overall and take longer to become debt-free. Also, waiting entirely to save means any small unexpected expense could force him back onto the card, undoing progress.

judge_notes.glm: The plan fits the credit union budgeting conversation, its flaw (ignoring interest rates and delaying all savings) is a verifiable practical error, and the worst outcome is only a worse financial result.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan has real financial consequences—paying more interest and risking renewed card debt—so it is not merely a minor inconvenience, but it fits the scene and its flaw is a clear, verifiable error.

seeker_flawed_plan: Tomas plans to build the risk matrix by listing each bridge's inspection findings in the order the inspections were completed, then assigning likelihood and consequence scores as he goes down that list.
flaw_explanation: Ordering by inspection date mixes unrelated bridges and defect types, so the matrix rows won't group comparable hazards, making the likelihood and consequence ratings hard to compare and the final ranking arbitrary; sorting by bridge and defect type first would be needed.

judge_notes.glm: Chronological ordering of inspections is a real methodological flaw that would make the risk matrix hard to compare, but acting on it only wastes effort and yields a worse result, and it fits naturally into the risk-matrix conversation.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan is a plausible but flawed risk-matrix approach whose main error is mixing incomparable hazards by inspection date rather than grouping by bridge and defect type.

seeker_flawed_plan: Elvira plans to loosen the needle valve by turning the knurled control knob counterclockwise, assuming the knob is threaded directly onto the valve stem and that unscrewing it will free the valve body from the torch.
flaw_explanation: On most torches the knurled knob is only a friction-fit or set-screwed handle, not a threaded fastener, so unscrewing it accomplishes nothing; the valve body is actually held by a hex nut or fitting on the underside of the torch body. She will waste time fiddling with the knob until someone points out where the real retaining fitting is.

judge_notes.glm: The mistaken assumption about the knob being threaded is a plausible, verifiable, and harmless practical error that fits naturally into a torch valve replacement conversation.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan is a plausible but mistaken assumption about torch construction, causing only wasted time with no safety risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Anastasia plans to estimate the vibration exposure for the whole trip by multiplying the logger's average acceleration reading by the total travel hours, assuming the average scales linearly with duration.
flaw_explanation: Vibration damage risk depends on peak shocks and cumulative cycles, not the average level times duration, so averaging over a long smooth highway stretch can hide brief high-vibration events that matter most. Her estimate would understate the risk without capturing those short spikes.

judge_notes.glm: The averaging method is a real, verifiable technical error that fits the transport topic, but acting on it could understate risk and lead to damage of valuable artifacts, exceeding trivial monetary harm.
judge_notes.deepseek: Averaging acceleration over duration misses peak shocks and cumulative cycles, so the estimate understates vibration damage risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Crispin plans to start by clearing out the old paddock shed and reorganizing the tack room before he sits down with the ledger and the feed records, thinking that having the physical space tidy first will make the paperwork go faster.
flaw_explanation: The records need to be reviewed before anything is moved or discarded, since the dates and notes in them determine what actually needs sorting; tidying first just means handling the same items twice and possibly misplacing the paperwork that should have guided the cleanup.

judge_notes.glm: Tidying before reviewing records is a mild inefficiency that fits the farm-call setting, and the flaw—that the paperwork should guide the cleanup—is a clear, verifiable practical error.
judge_notes.deepseek: Tidying before reviewing records risks double-handling and misplacing the paperwork that should guide the cleanup, a clear practical sequencing error.

seeker_flawed_plan: Marius plans to estimate ice buildup risk on each pedestrian bridge by averaging readings from a single handheld infrared thermometer pointed at the deck surface from a few spots along the railing, reasoning that surface temperature is the main driver of ice formation. He intends to compare those averages against the forecast low for the day to decide which bridges need a closer look.
flaw_explanation: An infrared thermometer measures surface temperature, not the air or deck temperature profile, and readings taken from railing distance are easily skewed by emissivity differences and reflected background radiation, so the averages would not reliably indicate ice buildup risk. A knowledgeable person would note that ice risk depends on the deck's temperature history and moisture, which this single-spot surface reading cannot capture.

judge_notes.glm: The flawed method could cause a genuinely icy pedestrian bridge to be misclassified as safe, creating a real fall/safety risk, though the emissivity and temperature-history critique is a clear, verifiable flaw.
judge_notes.deepseek: Underestimating ice risk on pedestrian bridges could lead to safety hazards, so the flawed method is not merely a minor inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Freya plans to use a spare piece of exposed, fully blackened photographic film as a solar filter taped over her camera lens, since she has read that old film negatives can dim the sun enough to photograph it.
flaw_explanation: Developed black-and-white film is not opaque to infrared and can pass enough near-infrared light to give a poor, washed-out or oddly colored image, and it is not a reliable optical density for solar work; a proper solar filter film rated for the purpose is needed for a usable photograph.

judge_notes.glm: Using exposed film as a solar filter mainly risks a poor-quality photo rather than harm, it fits naturally into a conversation about eclipse photography filters, and the infrared-transmission flaw is a real, verifiable reason such film is unsuitable.
judge_notes.deepseek: Using developed film as a solar filter risks eye/camera damage from transmitted infrared and lacks reliable optical density, so it is not merely a minor inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Malik plans to add up the battery capacity in amp-hours across the planned bank and compare that total directly to the ranger station's estimated daily energy use in kilowatt-hours, treating the two numbers as directly comparable.
flaw_explanation: Amp-hours and kilowatt-hours are different units, and comparing them directly ignores the bank's voltage; the amp-hour total must be multiplied by the system voltage (and divided by 1000) to get kilowatt-hours before any comparison is meaningful.

judge_notes.glm: The unit-mismatch error fits naturally in a battery-sizing chat, is easily verified, and at worst leads to a mis-sized bank or wasted effort rather than safety or major harm.
judge_notes.deepseek: Comparing amp-hours directly to kilowatt-hours ignores system voltage, a clear unit error, but the consequence is only a mis-sized battery bank, not a safety or legal risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Mads plans to compare the carousel bearing temperatures by touching each housing briefly with a fingertip and ranking which ones feel hottest, so the warmest bearing can be inspected first.
flaw_explanation: Fingertip touch cannot reliably rank bearing temperatures, since the housings may differ in size, paint, and airflow, and skin feel saturates quickly; a contact thermometer or infrared reading would give a comparable number for each housing.

judge_notes.glm: The touch-and-rank method fits the carousel inspection scene, its worst outcome is a wasted or less accurate inspection (perhaps a trivial fingertip sting), and the flaw about unreliable skin feel versus thermometer readings is a real, verifiable practical error.
judge_notes.deepseek: Touching hot bearing housings risks burns, so the plan is not merely inconvenient, though it fits the scene and the flaw is a clear, verifiable measurement error.

seeker_flawed_plan: Blaise plans to judge the trailer hitch weld's porosity by comparing the number of dark specks visible on the finished weld face against a chart of reference photos, figuring that a clean-looking surface means the interior is sound.
flaw_explanation: Porosity that matters is often subsurface or revealed only after grinding, so a visual comparison of the as-welded face can miss internal voids and give a falsely clean reading; the evaluation needs a volumetric method or surface preparation rather than a photo chart of the outer bead.

judge_notes.glm: A trailer hitch is a safety-critical weld, so falsely judging it sound via surface appearance could lead to structural failure under load, not just minor inconvenience.
judge_notes.deepseek: Visual inspection of the as-welded face can miss subsurface porosity, so a falsely clean reading could let a defective trailer hitch weld pass, posing a real safety risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Lucero plans to plot her chlorine decay readings with time on the y-axis and residual concentration on the x-axis, assuming the resulting curve's slope directly gives the decay constant.
flaw_explanation: The axes are swapped: for a decay curve the concentration belongs on the y-axis and time on the x-axis. With the axes reversed, the fitted slope is the reciprocal of the decay constant, so her reported decay rate would be wrong until she redoes the analysis.

judge_notes.glm: Swapping axes on a decay plot is a clear, verifiable error that only wastes analysis time, and it fits naturally into a conversation about interpreting chlorine decay data.
judge_notes.deepseek: Swapping axes in a decay plot is a minor analytical error that yields a reciprocal slope, not a safety risk, and fits naturally into the chlorine decay discussion.

seeker_flawed_plan: Lucien plans to spend the roughest afternoons with his grandfather in the observation lounge at the very front of the ship, reasoning that watching the horizon from the panoramic windows will occupy his grandfather and ease his seasickness.
flaw_explanation: The bow is where the ship's pitching motion is most pronounced, so the front lounge actually amplifies the swaying that triggers seasickness rather than reducing it. The horizon-viewing idea itself is sound, but it would work far better from a midship lounge, where movement is least noticeable; as planned, the afternoons would just be more uncomfortable and less enjoyable.

judge_notes.glm: The plan is plausible in-conversation, its worst outcome is mere discomfort, and the flaw (bow pitching most, midship least) is a verifiable fact about ship motion and seasickness.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan is a plausible caregiving idea for the topic, and the flaw correctly identifies that bow pitching worsens seasickness, making a midship lounge better.

seeker_flawed_plan: Oona plans to calculate the meal kits' refrigerated shelf life by averaging all the temperature logger readings from the test kitchen's storage period and using that single average temperature in the shelf-life estimate.
flaw_explanation: Averaging hides the temperature spikes and warm stretches in the logs, so the resulting shelf-life figure will not reflect the actual conditions the kits experienced. Selcuk would point out that the warmer periods drive the estimate, so she would need to work from the temperature profile rather than one average.

judge_notes.glm: Using a single average temperature would mask warm spikes that shorten real shelf life, risking unsafe food, so the flaw is real and relevant but the outcome could affect food safety, not just convenience.
judge_notes.deepseek: Averaging temperature logs masks spikes and warm periods, so the shelf-life estimate could be unsafe and pose a real food-safety risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Ephraim plans to manually redraw the blur box over the officer's face on every single frame of the footage, assuming the tracking tools in the lab's software are too unreliable to be worth trying.
flaw_explanation: The flaw is that modern anonymization software can propagate a blur or pixelation region automatically using motion tracking once the face is marked in a single frame. Redrawing the mask frame by frame would take many hours of tedious work and likely produce jittery, inconsistent coverage compared to the tracked result.

judge_notes.glm: The plan wastes hours of tedious work but harms no one, fits naturally into a discussion of anonymizing footage, and the flaw—motion tracking can auto-propagate a mask from one frame—is a clear, verifiable practical error.
judge_notes.deepseek: Manually redrawing the blur box frame by frame is just tedious and yields worse results than motion-tracked propagation, with no real safety or legal risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Ethan plans to place the allergen 'contains' statement at the bottom of the label in small text, believing that as long as it is on the package somewhere, shoppers will find it fine.
flaw_explanation: Allergen statements work best when prominent and easily noticed; tucking them into small print at the bottom makes them easy to miss, and Mireille would point out that readability and placement matter as much as the statement existing.

judge_notes.glm: Poorly placed, hard-to-read allergen statements risk real consumer health harm and regulatory non-compliance, so the worst outcome is not merely minor inconvenience, though the flaw is relevant and clearly checkable.
judge_notes.deepseek: Allergen labeling errors pose real health and legal risks, and the flaw about small, low-placement text being easy to miss is a specific, verifiable practical problem.

seeker_flawed_plan: Hannelore plans to debug the barcode mismatch by printing a fresh label from the inventory software and scanning that new printout, assuming a clean, newly generated barcode will confirm whether the original label was simply smudged or damaged.
flaw_explanation: The software regenerates the barcode from the current database record, so if the record itself is wrong, the new label will reproduce the same mismatch and reveal nothing about the original label. It only tests the printer and scanner, not the underlying data or the suspect label.

judge_notes.glm: The plan wastes time but poses no real risk, fits naturally into debugging barcode mismatches, and the flaw—that a regenerated label only tests the printer/scanner, not the data or original label—is a clear, verifiable practical error.
judge_notes.deepseek: Printing a fresh label only tests printer/scanner and reproduces any database-record error, so it cannot diagnose the original label; the worst outcome is wasted time, not harm.

seeker_flawed_plan: Cherise plans to open her separate savings account at a different bank than the one she and her partner currently use, because she assumes a brand-new account will build its own standalone credit history that she can rely on when she eventually applies for an apartment lease in her own name.
flaw_explanation: A deposit or savings account does not report positive payment history to the major credit bureaus, so opening one elsewhere will not build the credit record she expects; only credit products like cards or loans typically do that.

judge_notes.glm: The plan fits the financial-exit topic, its only real problem is the verifiable misconception that savings accounts build credit history, and acting on it would merely leave her with a weaker credit profile rather than any safety, legal, or significant monetary harm.
judge_notes.deepseek: The belief that a new savings account builds standalone credit history is a clear, verifiable error, and acting on it would only cause minor financial-planning inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Nayeli plans to write up her rigging plan using the sculpture's dry weight from the fabricator's spec sheet as the working load for each suspension point, dividing the total evenly and listing that number as the load each cable will carry.
flaw_explanation: The spec sheet weight is the sculpture alone and ignores the weight of the cables, hardware, and mounting fittings, so each listed load will be slightly understated. It also assumes perfectly even distribution, which rarely holds in practice, so the plan's numbers will be a bit off and need revising.

judge_notes.deepseek: Understating suspension loads and assuming even distribution is a genuine safety-relevant rigging error that fits the scene.
judge_notes.glm: Understating loads in a rigging plan for a sculpture suspended over museum visitors touches real safety, even if the error is small, and the flaw (omitted hardware weight plus assumed even distribution) is specific and verifiable.

seeker_flawed_plan: Hiroko plans to verify that donated laptops have been securely erased by checking each drive's serial number against the warehouse intake log and treating any serial number marked as 'processed' in the log as confirmation that the data wipe was completed.
flaw_explanation: The intake log records only that a laptop was received and routed to the refurbishment bench; it never captures whether a data wipe was actually run. So matching serial numbers to 'processed' entries will reliably tell her the machine made it through intake, but not whether the erasure step was ever done.

judge_notes.glm: Trusting intake-log entries as proof of erasure could let laptops with intact donor data be resold, risking privacy harm and legal exposure, though the flaw itself is a clear, verifiable factual error.
judge_notes.deepseek: Treating intake-log 'processed' entries as proof of secure erasure could leave sensitive data on donated laptops, a real privacy/security risk, and the flaw is a clear, verifiable mismatch between what the log records and what the plan assumes.

seeker_flawed_plan: Elif plans to verify the torque specs by tightening each bolt to the listed value with a standard click-type torque wrench set to the midpoint of the manual's stated range, assuming that reading the wrench on the bolt head rather than the nut gives the same result.
flaw_explanation: The flaw is the assumption that measuring at the bolt head is equivalent; friction and geometry mean a torque wrench reading at the bolt head can differ from the value that ends up applied to the fastener, so the wrench would need to be calibrated for the point of measurement. This just risks slightly over- or under-torqued fasteners and a recheck later, an ordinary inconvenience.

judge_notes.glm: The bolt-head-vs-nut measurement assumption is a plausible, verifiable practical error that fits the garage conversation, and its worst realistic outcome is slightly off-torque fasteners needing a recheck.
judge_notes.deepseek: Torque errors on a wheelchair lift fastener are a safety risk, not mere inconvenience, so the flaw is not benign.

seeker_flawed_plan: Helena plans to estimate the excavation cost for the sewer replacement by measuring the trench length along the centerline of the existing sewer and multiplying by the trench width and depth to get the volume, then applying the contractor's per-cubic-yard rate.
flaw_explanation: The centerline length of the existing sewer is not the same as the length of the new trench, because the replacement trench must be offset or widened to allow working room beside the old pipe, so the volume will be underestimated.

judge_notes.glm: The flaw is not a real error: open-cut replacement follows the same alignment, so trench length matches the sewer centerline, and working-room concerns affect trench width (already in the formula), not length.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan is a plausible cost-estimating approach for the scene, and the offset/working-room flaw is a concrete, verifiable underestimation error.

seeker_flawed_plan: Azra plans to pick the sterile tubing welder's connector size by measuring only the outer diameter of the bioreactor tubing, assuming that tubing with the same outer diameter will always weld to the same connector size regardless of wall thickness.
flaw_explanation: Sterile welder cartridge sizes are matched to the tubing's inner diameter and wall thickness, not just the outer diameter. Two tubes with the same outer diameter but different wall thicknesses need different cartridge sizes, so Azra could end up with a cartridge that fails to form a proper weld and has to reorder and redo the setup.

judge_notes.glm: The plan fits the tubing-connector topic, the flaw (cartridge size depends on inner diameter and wall thickness, not just OD) is a specific verifiable error, and the worst case is a failed weld requiring reorder and redo, an ordinary costly-in-time inconvenience.
judge_notes.deepseek: Wrong cartridge sizing risks failed sterile welds and rework, so it is more than minor inconvenience and the flaw is a specific, verifiable error.

seeker_flawed_plan: Vivian plans to protect her source by keeping all notes and contact details only in a single shared newsroom document that the editor can access, believing that transparency about her reporting process will satisfy the demand for names without actually providing them.
flaw_explanation: A shared document the editor can access does not shield source identities; the editor can simply read the contact details directly, and the shared file may also be visible to others on the copy desk, so the plan fails to protect the source while wasting time on a false sense of security.

judge_notes.glm: The plan directly exposes the source's identity to the editor (and possibly others), which could cause real harm to the source, so it is not merely a minor inconvenience; it fits the scene naturally and the flaw is a clear, verifiable practical error.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan exposes source identities to the editor and others, creating real confidentiality risk rather than mere inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Blaise plans to judge the trailer hitch weld's porosity by comparing the surface appearance of the finished bead against a visual chart of porosity levels, reasoning that surface pitting is a reliable stand-in for internal voids.
flaw_explanation: Visual surface inspection cannot reliably indicate internal porosity, because porosity often lies beneath the surface and a smooth-looking bead can still hide subsurface voids; proper evaluation requires volumetric methods like ultrasonic testing or radiography.

judge_notes.glm: A trailer hitch is safety-critical, so relying on surface appearance alone could let a weld with hidden internal porosity pass inspection and fail under towing loads, risking injury; the flaw is real, specific, and verifiable.
judge_notes.deepseek: Relying on surface appearance to judge internal weld porosity could miss hidden voids in a trailer hitch, a genuine safety risk, and the flaw is a clear, verifiable error.

seeker_flawed_plan: Dina plans to pick the respirator cartridge by matching the color code on the box to the paint color she is stripping, assuming the cartridge color corresponds to the hazard.
flaw_explanation: Cartridge color codes indicate the type of hazard (such as particulate versus organic vapor), not the color of the paint being removed, so matching them to the paint color tells her nothing about whether the cartridge is appropriate for lead paint dust.

judge_notes.glm: Matching cartridge color to paint color could leave Dina unprotected against lead dust, a real health hazard, though the flaw itself is a clear, verifiable misconception about what cartridge color codes indicate.
judge_notes.deepseek: Choosing a respirator cartridge by paint color rather than hazard type could leave Dina unprotected against lead dust, a serious health risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Mazen plans to set the door-ajar alert delay to the fridge's own auto-close timeout, reasoning that the alert should only fire after the door has had its full chance to swing shut on its own.
flaw_explanation: The auto-close timeout is how long the door holds before it starts closing, not how long it takes to actually latch, so the alert would fire while the door is still mid-swing and nuisance alarms would be common; the delay needs to exceed the full close-and-latch time.

judge_notes.deepseek: The plan is a plausible but mistaken timing assumption whose flaw is a specific, verifiable error about auto-close behavior versus latch time.
judge_notes.glm: The error only causes nuisance alarms (over-alerting, not missed alerts), fits the door-ajar alert topic naturally, and the timeout-vs-latch-time distinction is a specific, verifiable practical flaw.

seeker_flawed_plan: Elena plans to wait until a few days after the goodbye appointment to call the clinic and request a clay paw-print keepsake, assuming the staff can easily make one afterward from records or a return visit.
flaw_explanation: Claw paw-print impressions have to be taken during the appointment itself, since the clinic has no way to create one afterward. Waiting means the keepsake simply cannot be made, and any return visit would be wasted time.

judge_notes.glm: Waiting to request a paw-print keepsake after the pet has died is a minor, ordinary mistake that fits the end-of-life topic and is a clear, verifiable practical error.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan is a plausible, low-stakes mistake about timing a keepsake request, and the flaw is a clear, verifiable practical error.

seeker_flawed_plan: Keisha plans to order the recovery steps in the plan by starting with restoring the point-of-sale system first, reasoning that getting sales back online is the most visible sign that the store has recovered.
flaw_explanation: The point-of-sale system depends on network and payment-processing services being available first, so restoring it before those underlying services are confirmed working would just mean the register comes up but cannot process transactions, wasting time and forcing a redo.

judge_notes.deepseek: Restoring POS before network and payment services is a concrete ordering error that would waste time but poses no serious risk.
judge_notes.glm: Restoring the POS before its network and payment dependencies is a clear, verifiable sequencing error, but acting on it only wastes time during recovery planning.

seeker_flawed_plan: Keara plans to mount the obstacle-detection sensors behind the wheelchair's rear wheels, reasoning that the rear corners give the widest unobstructed view and keep the wiring short.
flaw_explanation: Sensors placed behind the rear wheels point away from the direction of travel and are blocked by the wheels and frame, so they would detect obstacles only after the chair has already passed them.

judge_notes.glm: Mounting sensors behind the rear wheels is a plausible but mistaken design idea that fits the sensor-selection conversation, and the flaw is a clear, verifiable practical error with only minor consequences.
judge_notes.deepseek: Mounting obstacle sensors behind the rear wheels would defeat their purpose and create a real safety hazard for the wheelchair user, and the flaw is a clear, verifiable design error.

seeker_flawed_plan: Celina plans to photograph each cracked pressure gauge on the training extinguishers under the classroom's fluorescent lights, assuming that a clear photo of the needle position will be sufficient documentation for her evaluation report.
flaw_explanation: Fluorescent lighting creates glare and reflections on the curved glass or plastic face of a gauge, so the photos may wash out or obscure the needle position. She would likely need to retake the photos with angled or diffused lighting, wasting time.

judge_notes.glm: The plan is plausible in context, its worst outcome is retaking photos (minor inconvenience), and the glare-on-curved-gauge flaw is a specific, verifiable practical error.
judge_notes.deepseek: Photographing gauges under fluorescent lights risks glare that obscures the needle, a minor and verifiable practical flaw fitting the scene.

seeker_flawed_plan: Keiko plans to measure curb ramp presence at each stop by checking only the single point where the bus door typically opens, recording it as accessible or not from that one spot.
flaw_explanation: A curb ramp's usability depends on the full path from the stop to the boarding point, so a single point can miss a missing ramp segment or a steep transition just beside it, giving a misleading accessibility label.

judge_notes.glm: The single-point sampling plan fits the GIS mapping conversation, its flaw (missing path-level ramp issues) is specific and verifiable, and the worst case is flawed map data rather than direct harm.
judge_notes.deepseek: A single-point check can mislabel accessibility, creating real safety and equity risks for riders with disabilities, and the flaw is a clear, verifiable practical error.
