seeker_flawed_plan: Morgan plans to order cryogenic gloves in the same size as their everyday work gloves, assuming the sizing will be identical across brands, and will just pick the same number off the chart.
flaw_explanation: Cryogenic glove sizing often runs differently from ordinary work gloves, and the thick insulated construction means the same labeled size can fit quite differently between manufacturers. Morgan may end up with gloves that don't fit well and have to go through the hassle of an exchange, costing some time.

judge_notes.deepseek: Glove sizing varies across brands and insulated cryogenic gloves fit differently, so the assumption is a real, verifiable practical error with only minor inconvenience as the worst outcome.
judge_notes.glm: Assuming identical sizing across brands is a real, verifiable mistake, but the worst case is only an exchange hassle, and it fits naturally into a conversation about choosing cryogenic gloves.

seeker_flawed_plan: Kestrel believes that running the redaction script on the log files after they have been archived into a compressed .tar.gz bundle works just as well, so she can archive first and redact later whenever convenient.
flaw_explanation: Most redaction tools operate on plain text files, not on the contents of a compressed archive, so the script would fail to find and mask the sensitive values inside the .tar.gz bundle. Kestrel would have to extract everything again and redo the work, wasting time.

judge_notes.glm: The belief is a plausible workflow misconception about redacting inside compressed archives, the flaw is a verifiable practical error, and the worst outcome is only wasted time redoing the work.
judge_notes.deepseek: Archiving before redaction is a plausible but flawed plan since redaction tools typically can't operate inside a .tar.gz, causing wasted effort but no serious harm.

seeker_flawed_plan: Brielle plans to use standard atmospheric pressure (14.7 psi) as the baseline pressure in all her dust deflagration index calculations for the mill's documentation, assuming ambient pressure is a fixed constant everywhere in the building.
flaw_explanation: This is a benign documentation issue: the pressure baseline only affects the presentation of her calculations, not any safety decisions. The flaw is that ambient pressure varies slightly with weather and altitude, so standards typically specify a reference condition rather than the local day's pressure, meaning her numbers will need minor re-derivation.

judge_notes.glm: The plan is actually sound practice—using standard 14.7 psi as a reference condition is what standards specify—so the stated flaw mischaracterizes a correct approach as an error needing re-derivation.
judge_notes.deepseek: Using a fixed pressure baseline in dust deflagration index calculations is not merely a documentation issue—KSt and Pmax depend on initial pressure, so an incorrect baseline could affect safety-relevant hazard assessment, and the stated flaw mischaracterizes the actual concern.

seeker_flawed_plan: Nadine plans to compare the cold remedies by lining up the boxes and checking which ones list the same active ingredient in the same milligram amount on the front panel, treating a match in that number as proof the products are equivalent for combining.
flaw_explanation: Front panels often state the amount per dose while the actual ingredient list may use different units or list amounts per tablet versus per liquid volume, so matching the front number alone can mislead; the reliable comparison is the Drug Facts panel's active ingredients section with its exact names and quantities.

judge_notes.deepseek: Matching front-panel numbers can mislead about equivalence and lead to unsafe combining, so the flaw is real and the plan fits the pharmacy scene.
judge_notes.glm: Treating a front-panel number match as proof products are equivalent could lead to combining remedies with overlapping active ingredients and double-dosing, a real health risk, though the flaw itself is a clear, verifiable error about front panels versus Drug Facts panels.

seeker_flawed_plan: Nolan plans to write the lockout procedure so that the conveyor's start button is pressed once at the beginning to confirm the machine is running, before any locks are applied, so the crew knows the controls work.
flaw_explanation: Nolan has the verification step in the wrong order relative to applying the locks, assuming a single test at the start is sufficient. The standard approach is to lock out first, then attempt to start the equipment to verify the energy is truly isolated, since a test before locking only confirms the button works, not that the machine stays de-energized.

judge_notes.glm: Testing the start button before locking out is a real, verifiable lockout/tagout sequencing error, and acting on it could let the conveyor start unexpectedly during repair, posing serious injury risk.
judge_notes.deepseek: Testing the start button before lockout rather than after is a genuine, specific safety error that could expose workers to hazardous energy.

seeker_flawed_plan: Belen plans to run the visual inspection of the mixing equipment before doing the protein swab tests, since she figures any visible residue should be rinsed away first and then swabbing confirms the surfaces are clean.
flaw_explanation: Swabbing should be done on a dry surface before the final rinse-and-dry cycle in that verification step; swabbing freshly rinsed equipment can dilute residues below the test's detection threshold, so she'd likely need to redo the swabs after drying, wasting a round of testing time.

judge_notes.glm: Swabbing wet, freshly rinsed equipment can dilute allergen residue below detection limits, so swabs must be taken after surfaces dry; the error is specific, verifiable, and only wastes testing time.
judge_notes.deepseek: Swabbing a wet, freshly rinsed surface can dilute allergen residue below detection limits, so the plan risks a wasted testing round but no real safety or legal harm.

seeker_flawed_plan: Dina plans to pick the respirator cartridge by matching the color band on the packaging to the paint color she's stripping, assuming the cartridge coding follows the same scheme as paint swatches.
flaw_explanation: Respirator cartridge color bands indicate the type of hazard (such as particulate or specific vapor/gas classes), not the color of the material being removed, so matching bands to paint color is meaningless for selecting protection.

judge_notes.glm: Matching cartridge colors to paint color could leave Dina with inadequate protection against lead dust/vapors, a real health hazard, though the misconception itself is plausible in-scene and the flaw is a clear, verifiable factual error about cartridge color coding.
judge_notes.deepseek: Choosing a respirator cartridge by paint color instead of hazard class could lead to inadequate protection against lead paint hazards, posing a real health risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Doreen plans to run the detector tube sampling for only a minute or two, since the closet visit is short and she assumes a brief draw will still give a readable stain length.
flaw_explanation: Detector tubes are calibrated to a specified sample volume at a given flow rate, and stopping well short of that volume yields a stain too faint to read reliably, so her short draw would likely produce an unreadable or misleading result.

judge_notes.deepseek: A too-short detector tube draw yields an unreadable stain, but the consequence is only a wasted sample and retest, not a real hazard.
judge_notes.glm: The short draw would most likely yield an obviously faint or unreadable stain, so the worst realistic outcome is a wasted tube and a redo, and the calibration-volume error is a specific, verifiable flaw that fits naturally into the tube-selection conversation.

seeker_flawed_plan: Elena plans to write the final appointment date on a sticky note and place it on the clinic's front counter calendar, assuming the staff will transfer it into their scheduling system from there.
flaw_explanation: A note left on a counter calendar is not the same as a booked appointment; front-desk staff typically schedule only through their own system, so the date could pass unrecorded and the slot would not actually be reserved.

judge_notes.glm: The sticky-note plan is plausible in this end-of-life pet conversation, its flaw (an unbooked date on a counter calendar isn't a real appointment) is verifiable, and the worst case is only a missed or delayed appointment.
judge_notes.deepseek: Leaving a sticky note on a counter calendar is a plausible but unreliable way to book an appointment, risking only a missed or unrecorded slot rather than serious harm.

seeker_flawed_plan: Jasmin plans to judge the scan's resolution by counting the triangle facets visible in the viewer at her normal zoom level, reasoning that a denser mesh on screen means finer capture detail.
flaw_explanation: On-screen facet density depends on the viewer's zoom and on how the mesh was decimated or smoothed for display, so it does not reliably reflect the original capture resolution; the settings report or raw point spacing is what needs checking.

judge_notes.glm: Judging capture quality by on-screen facet density is a plausible but mistaken method in this clinic conversation, and the flaw (display decimation and zoom dependence) is a real, verifiable error with only minor consequences like a misjudged scan or wasted time.
judge_notes.deepseek: Judging resolution by on-screen facet density is a plausible but flawed heuristic; the real issue is that display density reflects zoom and decimation, not capture resolution, which is a minor practical error with no safety risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Khalisa plans to evaluate the data-sharing agreement by checking whether it lists the specific data fields being shared, assuming that if every field in the study's dataset is named in the agreement, the agreement is complete and nothing else needs reviewing.
flaw_explanation: Listing data fields is only one part of a data-sharing agreement; a knowledgeable person would note that the agreement also needs terms on how the data may be used, stored, and re-shared, so checking field names alone would miss those provisions. Khalisa would still need to review the rest of the agreement's terms.

judge_notes.glm: The plan is a plausible but incomplete approach to reviewing a data-sharing agreement, and the flaw—that field lists alone omit use, storage, and re-sharing terms—is a clear, verifiable practical error with only minor consequences.
judge_notes.deepseek: Checking only field names is a plausible but incomplete approach; the flaw is that use, storage, and re-sharing terms also matter.

seeker_flawed_plan: Fumiko plans to judge whether her routine has turned punitive by logging each session's duration and comparing her weekly totals against the official recommended minutes for her age group, reasoning that staying at or under the guideline means the exercise is still health-driven rather than compulsive.
flaw_explanation: Public physical-activity guidelines are minimum targets for general health, not ceilings, so being at or under them says nothing about whether a routine has become compulsive; many people who overexercise still log moderate weekly totals because the pattern is about rigidity and distress, not volume alone.

judge_notes.glm: The logging plan is harmless self-monitoring, fits the spin-class conversation naturally, and the flaw is a real, verifiable misconception that guidelines are ceilings and that volume alone defines compulsive exercise.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan's core error is treating public activity guidelines as a ceiling rather than a minimum, so staying under them cannot rule out compulsive overexercise.

seeker_flawed_plan: Celina plans to sort the cracked gauges into a separate tray and evaluate them last, since she assumes a cracked lens makes the needle harder to read and the extra time at the end will let her double-check each one more carefully.
flaw_explanation: The crack can distort or scatter the reading regardless of when it is checked, so deferring those gauges does not make the needle position any more reliable and just delays the same ambiguous readings; a cracked gauge should be set aside as unserviceable rather than read later.

judge_notes.glm: The plan is a plausible training-room sorting strategy, and the flaw—that a cracked gauge is unserviceable regardless of when it's read—is a clear, verifiable practical error with only minor consequences in this context.
judge_notes.deepseek: Deferring cracked gauges is unsafe because a cracked lens can distort readings and the gauge should be treated as unserviceable, not read later.

seeker_flawed_plan: Elena plans to book the goodbye appointment for first thing in the morning, believing that clinics are calmest and least rushed right at opening, so the farewell will feel more peaceful.
flaw_explanation: Veterinary clinics are often busiest at opening because of scheduled drop-offs, overnight cases, and medication pickups; the calmest window is usually mid-morning or early afternoon between appointments. Booking the first slot of the day will likely mean more staff activity and a more hurried feel rather than a quieter one.

judge_notes.deepseek: The belief about clinic calmness at opening is a plausible, low-stakes scheduling assumption that is factually mistaken and easily corrected.
judge_notes.glm: Booking an early appointment at worst yields a busier, less peaceful farewell—a minor inconvenience—and the claim about morning clinic rush is a specific, verifiable practical point that fits naturally into the end-of-life decision conversation.

seeker_flawed_plan: Cosima plans to verify the fire stopping around the new conduits by reading the manufacturer's name printed on the sealant at each penetration and treating any penetration with a recognized firestop brand label as properly certified for that wall assembly.
flaw_explanation: A recognized brand alone does not mean the installation is compliant; each sealant product is only rated for specific wall types, cable counts, and annular gap sizes listed in its tested system design. Cosima would need to match the installed configuration to a listed system designation, so her check would approve penetrations that use the right product in an untested configuration.

judge_notes.deepseek: Approving untested firestop configurations creates a real fire-safety risk, so the flaw is not merely an inconvenience.
judge_notes.glm: The flaw is real and specific (brand recognition doesn't equal a listed system design), but acting on the flawed plan could leave non-compliant firestopping that fails in a fire, creating genuine safety risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Samir plans to verify the charger's wiring by checking that the mounting bolts on the terminal cover are tight and the cables are neatly routed, believing that a tidy, well-secured installation indicates the connections were made correctly.
flaw_explanation: Neatness and tight mounting hardware say nothing about whether the electrical connections are actually correct; a wiring job can look clean and organized while still being miswired. He needs to check the actual connections, not the tidiness of the installation.

judge_notes.glm: A miswired forklift charger can pose serious shock or fire hazards, so relying on tidiness rather than verifying actual connections is a real, verifiable safety-relevant flaw.
judge_notes.deepseek: Relying on tidy mounting and cable routing to judge electrical safety is a real, specific error that could leave a miswired charger undetected, posing shock or fire risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Mads plans to wipe down each bearing housing with an oily shop rag before taking temperature readings, assuming a light film of oil will not affect the infrared thermometer's results.
flaw_explanation: A shiny or oily surface has low, variable emissivity, so an infrared thermometer will read it inaccurately, often giving misleadingly low or jumpy values. The housings should be measured clean and dry, or with a patch of matte tape as a reference, so the readings can be trusted.

judge_notes.deepseek: Oily surfaces have low, variable emissivity that makes infrared readings unreliable, so the plan could cause missed overheating and real safety risk.
judge_notes.glm: Oily surfaces have low, variable emissivity that skews IR readings, and trusting falsely low temperatures on ride bearings could mask a real overheating hazard, so the outcome is not merely a minor inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Conor plans to assess mold risk in the cold-storage facility by taking a single ambient humidity reading with a household hygrometer at chest height in the middle of each day, assuming that one daily measurement captures the room's overall moisture conditions.
flaw_explanation: A single midday spot reading misses the daily cycles that matter most, such as overnight spikes when doors open or cooling cycles change, so it can badly understate the moisture range the room actually experiences. It also samples the air at chest height rather than near the cold surfaces where condensation and mold risk actually develop.

judge_notes.glm: The flawed single-reading method fits the cold-storage topic and is a verifiable error, but acting on it could let mold develop in a food facility, risking inventory loss and health rather than mere inconvenience.
judge_notes.deepseek: Underestimating moisture and mold risk in a cold-storage facility could lead to real health and structural problems, so the flawed single-reading plan is not merely a minor inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Tomas plans to build the risk matrix by giving equal weight to every factor he lists—condition rating, traffic volume, bridge age, and maintenance cost—then simply averaging the scores for each bridge to produce one final priority number.
flaw_explanation: Risk factors should not all carry equal weight, because likelihood and consequence are different dimensions that a straight average blends together. Averaging can make a bridge with a severe defect but low traffic score the same as a mediocre bridge with heavy traffic, so the resulting ranking will be misleading and he may need to redo the weighting later.

judge_notes.glm: Equal-weight averaging is a real, verifiable methodological flaw that fits naturally into a bridge risk-matrix discussion, and the worst outcome is a misleading ranking and rework, not safety or legal harm.
judge_notes.deepseek: Equal-weight averaging of likelihood and consequence factors is a genuine methodological flaw that could misrank bridges, though the consequence here is wasted effort and a misleading ranking rather than direct safety harm.

seeker_flawed_plan: Lars plans to swap the rinse-cycle breaker for a spare breaker of the same amperage from an unused slot in the panel, figuring that if the trips stop, the old breaker was simply weak and worn out.
flaw_explanation: A breaker that trips only during rinse is usually responding to a real current spike or ground fault in the rinse circuit, so moving a same-rated spare into that slot will most likely just make the spare trip too, costing him time and leaving him back where he started.

judge_notes.deepseek: Swapping in a same-rated spare is a plausible but flawed diagnostic step, since a rinse-only trip usually reflects a real fault that would simply trip the replacement breaker too.
judge_notes.glm: Swapping in a same-rated spare breaker is a plausible diagnostic step whose worst realistic outcome is wasted time, it fits naturally into a conversation about rinse-cycle breaker trips, and the flaw—that the trips likely stem from a real fault in the rinse circuit so the spare will trip too—is a specific, verifiable electrical diagnosis.

seeker_flawed_plan: Maliha plans to combine all the jars taken from a single spice shipment into one large composite sample, mix it thoroughly, and then run her tests on portions drawn from that single blend, reasoning that this gives a result representing the whole shipment.
flaw_explanation: Compositing averages the samples together, so a contaminated or off-spec batch within the shipment would be diluted and likely go undetected, giving a deceptively clean result. A sampling plan needs to keep portions separate or at least test subsamples individually to capture lot-to-lot variability.

judge_notes.glm: Compositing could mask contamination in imported spices, creating a real food-safety risk rather than mere inconvenience, but the flaw is relevant to the scene and clearly verifiable.
judge_notes.deepseek: Compositing a whole shipment dilutes localized contamination, so the flaw is a real food-safety risk that fits the spice-testing scene.

seeker_flawed_plan: Declan plans to keep a daily tally of his compassion fatigue by rating each shift on a simple 1-to-10 scale, expecting that a rising average across a week will tell him when to ask for support.
flaw_explanation: A single averaged number hides the pattern of highs and lows that actually signals compassion fatigue, so a steady average can mask a few severely draining shifts. Tracking the worst shifts separately would reveal the trend more clearly.

judge_notes.deepseek: Averaging a 1-to-10 fatigue rating can mask severe individual shifts, so tracking worst shifts separately is a valid, verifiable critique.
judge_notes.glm: The self-tracking plan is harmless, fits naturally into a conversation about recognizing compassion fatigue, and the flaw—that averaging masks severe outlier shifts—is a specific, verifiable practical error.

seeker_flawed_plan: Hakeem believes that using the 100x oil immersion objective for every field of view will give the most accurate pollen counts, so he plans to do all his counting at that magnification.
flaw_explanation: Oil immersion is unnecessary for identifying and counting most common grains, which are resolvable at 40x, and scanning a hemocytometer grid at 100x is far slower because each field covers a tiny area. He would spend hours more per slide for little gain in count quality.

judge_notes.glm: Using 100x oil immersion for all pollen counting wastes time but harms no one, fits the microscope-objective topic naturally, and the flaw about 40x sufficiency and tiny field size is a verifiable practical error.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan is a plausible but inefficient choice for pollen counting, and the flaw correctly explains that 100x oil immersion is slower and unnecessary for most grains.

seeker_flawed_plan: Hector plans to anonymize his interview transcripts by replacing every occurrence of a participant's real name with a pseudonym using his word processor's find-and-replace, then saving each edited file over the original so there is only one version to keep track of.
flaw_explanation: Find-and-replace matches substrings, so a name that appears inside an unrelated word or place name will also be changed, silently corrupting the text; and overwriting the originals destroys the record needed to verify or redo the anonymization later.

judge_notes.glm: The plan fits the anonymization topic, its flaws (substring over-matching and destroying originals) are concrete and verifiable, and the worst outcome is corrupted transcripts and wasted effort rather than any safety, legal, or significant monetary harm.
judge_notes.deepseek: Overwriting originals destroys the audit trail needed to verify or redo anonymization, a real research-integrity risk beyond mere inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Kelda plans to draft a short anonymous note of support and leave copies in each locker stall before practice, believing that anonymity will make teammates more willing to speak up against the whispers.
flaw_explanation: Anonymous notes in a small locker room tend to be read as pranks or as targeting the recipient, so they are more likely to prompt teasing about the notes themselves than to change the group's behavior.

judge_notes.glm: The anonymous-note plan is a plausible, low-stakes idea that fits the locker-room setting, and the flaw that such notes in a small team setting would likely be read as pranks and become a source of teasing is a specific, verifiable practical problem.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan is low-stakes and fits the scene, and the flaw about anonymous notes being misread as pranks is a specific, verifiable practical problem.

seeker_flawed_plan: Hussein believes that when a label calls for a 1:10 dilution, he should mix one part disinfectant concentrate with ten parts water, so for a two-gallon bucket he plans to add about 3.2 ounces of concentrate and 32 ounces of water and then top the bucket up.
flaw_explanation: A 1:10 dilution ratio conventionally means one part concentrate in a total of ten parts solution, so it calls for one part concentrate to nine parts water. His version leaves the mixed solution somewhat more diluted than intended, giving a weaker result, though he would notice and can simply recalculate and remix.

judge_notes.deepseek: The 1:10 ratio error yields a weaker-than-intended solution with only minor, correctable consequences, and it fits the daycare dilution topic.
judge_notes.glm: The 1:10 convention error is a clear, verifiable dilution mistake that fits the daycare disinfectant topic, and the worst case is a slightly weaker solution he can notice and remix.

seeker_flawed_plan: Bram plans to check the chimney cracks by filling them with water from a spray bottle and watching whether the water runs down the inside face, figuring that a crack that lets water through is the one worth flagging before the liner goes in.
flaw_explanation: Brick and mortar are porous, so a light spray will be absorbed or pass through the masonry itself rather than tracing a single crack, giving a misleading result; the test would need to be done with a controlled flow over a longer period and the interior observed properly, which a quick spray cannot do.

judge_notes.glm: The spray-bottle crack test is a plausible but flawed diagnostic idea that fits the chimney evaluation topic, and the porosity-based flaw is a real, verifiable practical error with only minor consequences.
judge_notes.deepseek: The spray test is a plausible but flawed idea; its main error is that porous masonry absorbs water, so the test can't reliably trace a single crack.

seeker_flawed_plan: Elio plans to pick the mirror's hanging height by centering it on the hallway wall's full floor-to-ceiling measurement, so the mirror's midpoint sits at the halfway point of the wall.
flaw_explanation: Hanging height should be set relative to eye level and the surrounding trim or furniture, not the wall's midpoint; on a tall Victorian hallway wall, centering on the full height would place the mirror noticeably too high.

judge_notes.glm: Centering the mirror on the full wall height instead of eye level is a real, verifiable hanging mistake with only cosmetic consequences, and it fits naturally into a conversation about mounting a mirror.
judge_notes.deepseek: Centering on the full wall height is a plausible but wrong approach that would put the mirror too high, though the consequence is only aesthetic inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Adelina plans to fold all the wall pieces from standard printer/copy paper, believing that any paper folds equally well and that ordinary office paper will give the crispest, neatest shapes for the display.
flaw_explanation: Standard copy paper is relatively thick and stiff, so for the small, layered folds she has in mind the creases will look bulky and the shapes will not hold fine points cleanly. Lighter-weight kami or similar origami paper folds more sharply and produces a much more delicate result at that size.

judge_notes.glm: Using standard copy paper for delicate origami butterflies is a harmless aesthetic mistake that fits the art-corner scene and is a verifiable practical flaw, since lighter kami folds more sharply.
judge_notes.deepseek: Using stiff copy paper for small origami folds is a real, verifiable practical flaw, but the consequences are only a poorer-looking display.

seeker_flawed_plan: Uri plans to check his tire tread by comparing the wear bars molded into the grooves on each tire, and he believes any tire where the tread still sits above those bars is good to keep for winter.
flaw_explanation: Wear bars are set at 2/32 of an inch, which is the legal minimum, not a winter-safety threshold; winter traction degrades well before that, so a tire passing the bar test can still be a poor choice for snow and cold.

judge_notes.glm: Relying on 2/32-inch wear bars as a winter-readiness test is a real safety issue, since traction in snow and cold degrades well above the legal minimum, though the belief fits the tire-shop topic and the flaw is specific and verifiable.
judge_notes.deepseek: Relying on wear bars as a winter-safety threshold risks unsafe winter traction, so the flaw is real and safety-relevant.

seeker_flawed_plan: Ethan plans to use the phrase 'contains milk and wheat' as the allergen statement on the soup label, assuming that listing the allergens by their common food names is all that is needed.
flaw_explanation: Allergen statements must use the specific standardized allergen names, and 'wheat' should be tied to the actual ingredient source (e.g., flour) rather than just the allergen category; using only common food names can make the statement non-compliant with labeling rules. A knowledgeable person would point out that the statement needs to reference the allergen's official designation as it appears in the ingredient list.

judge_notes.glm: A non-compliant allergen statement on a packaged food carries real regulatory/legal risk, the topic fits naturally into the labeling conversation, and the flaw is a specific, verifiable labeling-rule error.
judge_notes.deepseek: Allergen labeling errors can cause serious health risks and legal non-compliance, so the flaw is not benign.

seeker_flawed_plan: Cherise plans to open her new personal checking account at a different bank a few weeks before she leaves, believing that having the account ready early means her first paycheck after the move will deposit smoothly with no interruption.
flaw_explanation: A new account opened that recently often has a waiting period before direct deposit can be set up, and employers typically need one to two pay cycles to update payroll details, so the first paycheck may still land in the old account or arrive as a paper check.

judge_notes.glm: The plan is plausible in this conversation, and the flaw is a real, verifiable payroll/banking timing issue whose worst outcome is only a delayed or paper-check paycheck.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan fits the financial-safety topic, and the flaw is a concrete, verifiable banking/payroll timing issue with only minor consequences.

seeker_flawed_plan: Dion plans to assess wind load on each sample canopy by holding his handheld anemometer underneath the fabric, inside the shaded space beneath the frame, and using that reading as the wind speed for his load calculations.
flaw_explanation: The area under the canopy is largely sheltered, so the anemometer there reads a much lower speed than the wind actually striking the exposed fabric from outside. He should measure (or estimate) the ambient open-air wind speed instead, then apply it to the canopy's area in his load calculation.

judge_notes.deepseek: Underestimating wind load from a sheltered reading could lead to canopy failure and real safety risk, so the flaw is not merely benign.
judge_notes.glm: Measuring wind under the sheltered canopy instead of in open air is a clear, verifiable methodological error, but acting on it only risks an inaccurate load calculation, not safety or significant cost.

seeker_flawed_plan: Belen plans to verify allergen cleaning by swabbing only the mixing paddle after a flavor changeover, assuming the paddle is the sole point where residue accumulates.
flaw_explanation: Allergen residue also builds up in other hard-to-clean spots like the bucket elevator and hopper corners, so testing only the paddle gives an incomplete picture. The verification should sample several high-contact points along the line rather than just one component.

judge_notes.glm: Incomplete allergen verification could leave residue that sickens allergic consumers, so it's not merely a minor inconvenience, but the plan fits the scene and the flaw is a clear, verifiable sampling error.
judge_notes.deepseek: Testing only the paddle risks missing allergen residue elsewhere, a genuine food-safety flaw that fits the scene.

seeker_flawed_plan: Hugo plans to price his vegetables by rounding each item up to the nearest whole dollar, believing that this keeps the mental math simple for customers and saves him from dealing with coins at a busy stall.
flaw_explanation: Rounding every price up to a whole dollar does not actually simplify much, since customers paying with cards or larger bills still need change, and it pushes several items above the round-number thresholds shoppers use to judge value, so he would likely lose more sales than he gains in convenience.

judge_notes.glm: The rounding-up pricing scheme is a plausible topic for a market stall conversation, its worst case is merely lost sales (an ordinary business inconvenience), and the flaw about card payments and value thresholds is a specific, verifiable practical error.
judge_notes.deepseek: Rounding up prices is a minor pricing choice with only modest financial downside, fits naturally into a discussion about running a vegetable stall, and the stated flaw about lost sales and change-making is a concrete, verifiable practical error.

seeker_flawed_plan: Camila plans to calculate the banner's total wind load by multiplying the design pressure by the banner's total area, including the full square footage of the reinforced vinyl across both sides, and to size the corner anchoring from that single summed figure.
flaw_explanation: Wind acts on both faces simultaneously, but the load on the banner is based on one projected area, so doubling it for both sides overestimates the force and leads to oversized anchoring rather than a correct result. This only makes her order heavier, pricier hardware than needed—a minor wasted expense and rework.

judge_notes.glm: Doubling wind load for both banner faces is a clear, verifiable error (load is based on one projected area), fits the signage topic, and only causes minor wasted cost.
judge_notes.deepseek: Doubling projected area for both banner faces overestimates wind load, causing only oversized anchoring and minor wasted cost, and the error is a clear, verifiable factual mistake fitting the wind-load topic.

seeker_flawed_plan: Khadir plans to skip the small test patch on a spare piece of joint material and instead judge the sealant's cure and adhesion by pressing a thumb on the actual joint after a few hours, since the product label gives a tack-free time.
flaw_explanation: Tack-free time only means the surface is no longer sticky; it does not show whether the sealant has developed adhesion or full cure, so a thumb test on the real joint tells him almost nothing useful and he may redo the joint later.

judge_notes.glm: Skipping the test patch and relying on tack-free time is a plausible, verifiable mistake whose worst outcome is redoing the joint, and it fits naturally into a conversation about choosing aquarium sealants.
judge_notes.deepseek: Skipping the test patch and thumb-testing the live joint risks a failed seal and leak in a public aquarium, so the flaw is real and consequential.

seeker_flawed_plan: Pilar plans to schedule the rooftop HVAC lifts in the order the units appear on the mechanical schedule, since she believes the crane can simply work its way across the roof from one end to the other without repositioning.
flaw_explanation: The mechanical schedule order doesn't match the physical layout of the roof, so following it would force the crane to swing back and forth across the building repeatedly instead of working in one direction, adding several unnecessary hours of cycling.

judge_notes.glm: Following the mechanical schedule order wastes crane time but poses no safety or legal risk, fits naturally into a lift plan review, and the mismatch between schedule order and roof layout is a specific, verifiable practical error.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan's flaw is a verifiable scheduling/layout mismatch causing extra crane cycling, a minor time/cost inefficiency rather than a safety issue.

seeker_flawed_plan: Chen plans to run the audit-trail migration as a straight copy of the legacy audit table into the new system's audit table, assuming the new system will preserve the original timestamps and ordering exactly as stored.
flaw_explanation: The new system's audit table likely generates its own timestamps and sequence numbers on insert, so a straight copy would overwrite or ignore the legacy values and scramble the original ordering. Chen would need to map the legacy timestamp and sequence fields explicitly rather than assume they carry over unchanged.

judge_notes.glm: The plan is a plausible technical mistake in this exact migration scenario, the flaw is a specific verifiable database issue, and the worst realistic outcome is rework and data cleanup rather than safety or legal harm.
judge_notes.deepseek: A straight copy that scrambles audit-trail ordering and timestamps could corrupt payroll audit records, a serious compliance and financial risk, not mere inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Saba plans to recalculate the chart's centerline and control limits using only the most recent ten subgroups, reasoning that a shorter, more current baseline will make the chart more responsive to the packaging line's recent behavior.
flaw_explanation: Recomputing limits from a short recent window that likely includes the very out-of-control points she is trying to detect will inflate the limits and mask real signals; control limits should come from a stable baseline period, not from the data under investigation.

judge_notes.glm: Recalculating limits from a short window containing out-of-control points is a clear, verifiable SPC error that fits naturally at a QA chart review, and the worst realistic outcome is a flawed analysis rather than genuine harm.
judge_notes.deepseek: Recalculating limits from a short recent window that includes out-of-control points would inflate limits and mask real signals, a genuine SPC error with potential quality/safety consequences.

seeker_flawed_plan: Makenna plans to use bubble wrap as the only cushioning layer inside each shock-safe container, wrapping the instruments in a few loose layers and skipping the custom foam inserts, since she believes the wrap alone will meet the containers' shock-rating specs.
flaw_explanation: Bubble wrap alone cushions light, low-frequency bumps but does not immobilize or damp the sharp, high-frequency vibrations that the containers' shock rating assumes; the foam inserts are what provide the damping the spec relies on. The instruments would likely arrive fine but with more residual vibration than the certification calls for, potentially requiring re-verification.

judge_notes.glm: Skipping foam inserts could cause failed shock certification and re-verification delays, a minor cost/time issue that fits naturally into a container loading review and rests on a verifiable cushioning-vs-damping distinction.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan fits the packing-dock scene, and the flaw is a specific, verifiable technical error about vibration damping, with only minor consequences like re-verification.

seeker_flawed_plan: Noemi plans to rest the sound level meter directly on the metal surface of the stamping press during each measurement, thinking that touching the machine gives the most accurate reading of the noise it produces.
flaw_explanation: Contact with the vibrating machine surface introduces structure-borne vibration and handling noise into the meter, corrupting the reading; sound level measurements should be taken on a tripod or held in the free field at the worker's ear position, away from reflecting or vibrating surfaces.

judge_notes.deepseek: Resting the meter on the vibrating press corrupts readings and could lead to underestimating worker noise exposure, a real safety risk.
judge_notes.glm: Resting the meter on the vibrating press would corrupt readings (a worse result/wasted effort), it fits naturally into a noise-measurement conversation, and the vibration/handling-noise error is a specific, verifiable flaw.

seeker_flawed_plan: Omarion plans to pre-mix all the glaze colors the children will use into small cups the night before class, so the kids can start painting right away without waiting at a shared station.
flaw_explanation: Many glazes contain heavy settling ingredients that sink to the bottom of a cup overnight, so pre-mixed cups would need thorough re-stirring anyway and could apply unevenly, wasting the prep time and giving patchy results.

judge_notes.glm: Pre-mixing glaze cups the night before is a plausible, low-stakes plan for a kids' ceramics class, and glaze settling overnight requiring re-stirring is a real, verifiable practical flaw.
judge_notes.deepseek: Pre-mixing glazes overnight is a plausible topic in this scene, and the settling-of-heavy-ingredients flaw is a real, verifiable practical issue with only minor consequences.

seeker_flawed_plan: Oluwatobi plans to write the maintenance record entries in pencil so that any typos can be erased and the log kept looking neat for the next review.
flaw_explanation: Maintenance logs are typically meant to be kept in permanent ink so entries cannot be altered after the fact; using pencil makes the record look unreliable and may require him to redo the entries in pen later. The mistake only costs him some rewriting time, not anything serious.

judge_notes.glm: Writing maintenance log entries in pencil violates standard permanent-ink record-keeping practice, but the worst outcome is only redoing entries in pen, and the issue fits naturally into a conversation about reviewing a maintenance record.
judge_notes.deepseek: Using pencil in a maintenance log is a real documentation error, but the consequence is only redoing entries in pen.

seeker_flawed_plan: Oskar plans to have the crew carry a single 25-foot tape measure and take every anchor-point measurement from the billboard's base, recording all distances as straight-line horizontal runs on the worksheet.
flaw_explanation: Anchor positions on a billboard are typically specified by elevation along the structure, not by ground-level horizontal distance from the base, so measuring only from the bottom will not match the actual locations on the sign. Theodora can point out that he needs measurements taken along the vertical face or from a fixed reference point on the structure itself, otherwise the crew will have to re-measure everything later.

judge_notes.glm: Measuring only horizontal runs from the base would mislocate elevated anchor points, causing re-measurement and wasted time but no safety risk, and the flaw is specific and verifiable.
judge_notes.deepseek: Measuring only horizontal runs from the base won't locate anchor points specified by elevation on the billboard, causing rework but no safety risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Marius plans to rank the bridge deck's ice buildup risk by measuring the depth of snow on top of the deck, reasoning that deeper snow means more ice has formed underneath.
flaw_explanation: Snow depth on a deck is a poor proxy for ice thickness: snow insulates the surface and its depth depends mostly on wind drifting and snowfall amount, so a deep drift can sit over little or no ice while a thin, bare-looking patch may hide a thick glaze. Checking actual ice presence or surface temperature would be needed instead.

judge_notes.glm: The flawed proxy could cause a real safety hazard by leaving dangerous hidden ice unflagged during a pedestrian bridge inspection, though the flaw itself is relevant and clearly verifiable.
judge_notes.deepseek: Underestimating ice from snow depth could cause a serious safety hazard on a pedestrian bridge, and the flaw is a clear, verifiable factual error.

seeker_flawed_plan: Marius plans to estimate ice buildup risk on the pedestrian bridge by comparing today's air temperature to the bridge deck's surface temperature and treating any reading below freezing as proof that ice has already formed and will keep accumulating.
flaw_explanation: A surface temperature below freezing only shows that ice could form, not that it has; the deck can be below 0°C while remaining dry if there is no moisture, so the method would flag many false positives and misjudge the actual accumulation risk.

judge_notes.deepseek: The plan's false-positive logic could cause unsafe misjudgment of ice risk on a pedestrian bridge, so it is not benign.
judge_notes.glm: The flaw is a clear, verifiable error (sub-freezing surface temperature alone doesn't confirm ice without moisture), the plan fits the bridge-inspection topic naturally, and acting on it would only cause false alarms and wasted effort, not real harm.

seeker_flawed_plan: Louisa plans to document each participant's informed consent by typing a short free-text note into the trial app's general comments field, since the app lacks a dedicated consent form and she assumes the comments will be easy to search later.
flaw_explanation: The app's general comments field is not indexed for search and does not export with participant records, so the consent notes would be effectively buried and hard to retrieve during monitoring visits, wasting time later.

judge_notes.glm: While the stated flaw is wasted time, the worst outcome of burying informed consent records in a non-exportable field is a regulatory/legal compliance failure, since consent documentation is legally required to be retrievable during monitoring and audits.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan fits the consent-documentation topic, and the flaw is a concrete, verifiable app limitation causing retrieval problems rather than serious harm.

seeker_flawed_plan: Agnieszka plans to sort the cracked panels for her lab's reuse inventory by judging each one visually under the warehouse lights, assuming that any crack without visible discoloration, burn marks, or moisture inside the glass can be logged as fully functional.
flaw_explanation: Many damaging cracks are internal microcracks in the cells or solder joints that leave no visible trace on the surface, so a panel can look perfectly clean while performing poorly. A visual-only check will misclassify damaged panels, so her sorting will need to be redone with electrical testing.

judge_notes.glm: The visual-only sorting plan fits the inspection-table conversation, its flaw (invisible microcracks requiring electrical testing) is specific and verifiable, and the worst case is redoing the lab inventory sort rather than any safety or legal harm.
judge_notes.deepseek: Visual-only sorting of cracked panels is a plausible but flawed plan, since internal microcracks can be invisible and only electrical testing would catch them, with the worst outcome being wasted effort rather than safety risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Rasmus plans to compare alert thresholds by rolling out each candidate setting to the whole monitoring center for a week at a time, assuming that a full week per setting will give a clean before-and-after picture of alarm fatigue.
flaw_explanation: Because the weeks differ in resident activity, staffing, and seasonal events, the comparison will be confounded, so the apparent best setting may just reflect an easier week rather than the threshold itself.

judge_notes.glm: The sequential whole-center rollout is plausibly raised in this alert-design conversation, and week-to-week variation in resident activity, staffing, and seasonality is a clear, verifiable confound, with the worst case being a misleading choice rather than direct harm.
judge_notes.deepseek: Rolling out thresholds sequentially over differing weeks confounds comparison with week-to-week variation, a clear and verifiable design flaw.

seeker_flawed_plan: Monty plans to scan the paper disposal log into a single PDF and then run optical character recognition on it so the office can search old entries by name or date.
flaw_explanation: OCR will misread many handwritten log entries, so the searchable index will contain errors and require manual correction, wasting time and producing an unreliable index.

judge_notes.glm: The plan is a routine digitization task in a records office, and its main flaw—that OCR struggles with handwritten entries, producing an error-ridden index needing manual correction—is a well-known, verifiable practical limitation.
judge_notes.deepseek: OCR on handwritten logs would indeed introduce errors, making the index unreliable and requiring manual correction—a minor, ordinary inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Ewan plans to isolate the phantom alarm by disconnecting the loop's fault from the panel's fault log alone, believing the logged device address always points directly at the physical device that is actually causing the trouble signal.
flaw_explanation: The logged address is only the first device reporting the loop disruption, not necessarily the faulty one; the real fault can lie anywhere between that device and the previous device on the loop wiring. So working from the log address alone can send him inspecting the wrong unit and waste time.

judge_notes.glm: The belief fits the troubleshooting conversation, the flaw is a verifiable point about loop fault isolation, and the worst outcome is wasted inspection time rather than real danger.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan fits the fire-panel troubleshooting scene, and the flaw correctly explains that the logged address is only the first reporting device, not necessarily the faulty one.

seeker_flawed_plan: Blaise plans to spray the trailer hitch weld with ordinary black spray paint before inspecting it, believing the dark coating will make the bright porosity indications stand out more clearly under the light.
flaw_explanation: The paint layer will fill or bridge over the tiny surface pores, hiding the very indications Blaise wants to see, so the inspection would show fewer pores than are actually there.

judge_notes.glm: Painting over the weld would mask porosity in a safety-critical trailer hitch, potentially allowing a defective weld to pass inspection and fail in use.
judge_notes.deepseek: Spray paint would bridge or fill surface porosity, masking the indications, so the flaw is a clear, verifiable practical error with only minor consequences.

seeker_flawed_plan: Naveed plans to confirm the pack is swollen by laying a straight metal ruler across the battery's top face and checking for a gap under the middle, reasoning that a flat pack should sit flush against the ruler.
flaw_explanation: A straightedge laid across the top of a LiPo pouch will not reveal swelling in the middle, because the swelling bulges the large faces outward and the ruler bridges the high points; the gap would appear at the ends or along the sides, not under the center, so a puffed pack can still read as flat.

judge_notes.deepseek: The straightedge method can falsely read a puffed LiPo as flat, and using a swollen battery poses real fire/safety risk, so the flaw is relevant and verifiable.
judge_notes.glm: The flawed straightedge check could give a false 'flat' reading, leading Naveed to keep using or charging a genuinely puffed LiPo, which poses a real fire risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Aziz plans to wipe down the safety station's plastic countertop and the nearby sample jars with a dry cotton cloth before handling flour samples, believing this will remove stray dust and leave surfaces clean enough that static buildup is less likely to occur.
flaw_explanation: Dry wiping of plastic and similar insulating surfaces generates and deposits static charge rather than removing it, so the cloth would actually increase the charge on the counter and jars and make shocks more likely, not less.

judge_notes.glm: Dry-wiping plastic increases static charge, and in a flour-dust environment a static spark is a genuine ignition hazard, so the outcome is not merely a minor inconvenience.
judge_notes.deepseek: Dry wiping insulating surfaces like plastic and jars builds static charge, increasing shock and dust-ignition risk rather than reducing it.

seeker_flawed_plan: Cosima plans to assess each fire stopping installation by measuring only the depth of the sealant at the face of the penetration with a ruler, recording a single number per conduit and treating that one reading as representative of the whole seal.
flaw_explanation: A single depth measurement at the face doesn't capture whether the sealant is applied evenly or fully fills the annular space deeper inside the opening, so the readings can look fine while missing local variations. A proper check would need measurements or visual verification at multiple points around each penetration's circumference, so her approach would mainly cost extra rework time if she relies on the single readings.

judge_notes.glm: Fire stopping is a life-safety system, so relying on a single face-depth reading could leave an inadequate seal that fails in a fire, posing real safety risk rather than mere inconvenience; the flaw is relevant to the scene and is a specific, verifiable technical error.
judge_notes.deepseek: Fire stopping is a life-safety measure, so relying on a single face-depth reading risks inadequate seals and real safety consequences, though the flaw itself is specific and verifiable.

seeker_flawed_plan: Selene plans to tighten the brake cable tension first and then adjust the brake pad position afterward, believing the pads will naturally seat correctly once the cable is properly tensioned.
flaw_explanation: The order is backwards: pad position should be set first, then cable tension adjusted to match, since tightening the cable first can pull the pads out of alignment and force her to redo the pad adjustment. The result is wasted time and a slightly less precise adjustment, not any danger.

judge_notes.glm: The backwards order of brake adjustment is a real, verifiable practical error that fits naturally into a wheelchair brake tuning conversation and carries only minor inconvenience.
judge_notes.deepseek: The brake-adjustment order error is a real, verifiable practical mistake whose worst consequence is wasted time and slightly imprecise adjustment, fitting the wheelchair workshop scene.

seeker_flawed_plan: Ethan plans to draft the allergen statement by listing every ingredient from the soup recipe in descending order by weight, then marking the ones he knows are allergens, figuring the label will be complete once every ingredient appears.
flaw_explanation: Allergen labeling doesn't follow recipe order or require every ingredient to be listed in the allergen statement; the statement needs to name each allergen source in plain terms, and some allergen sources can appear under a different ingredient name or as a sub-component, so a recipe-order list can miss or misname an allergen.

judge_notes.glm: Mislabeling allergens on packaged food poses real legal and consumer health risks, so the plan is not benign, though it fits the scene and the flaw is a clear, verifiable labeling error.
judge_notes.deepseek: Mislabeling allergens in packaged soup poses real health and legal risks, and the flaw correctly identifies that allergen statements require plain-name allergen sources rather than a recipe-order ingredient list.

seeker_flawed_plan: Victor plans to check for short-cycling by timing the compressor's run and off cycles only once, right after the remodel, and treating that single reading as the baseline for whether the unit is cycling too often.
flaw_explanation: A single timing sample taken just after a remodel reflects an unusual load—doors propped open, warm product, and equipment still settling—so it can look like short-cycling even when the compressor is behaving normally; cycle timing needs to be compared across normal operating conditions.

judge_notes.glm: The single post-remodel timing sample is a clear methodological error that fits naturally into the compressor diagnosis conversation and carries only minor consequences like a misdiagnosis or wasted effort.
judge_notes.deepseek: Taking a single cycle-timing sample right after a remodel is a real diagnostic error because abnormal post-remodel loads can mimic short-cycling, and the consequence is only wasted effort or a misdiagnosis.

seeker_flawed_plan: Farah plans to organize the tofu line's HACCP verification forms by filing them under the production date of the batch they refer to, believing this will make the records easiest to trace later.
flaw_explanation: Verification records are typically indexed by the date the verification activity was performed, not the production date. Filing by production date means anyone looking up a verification event will search in the wrong place, wasting time and possibly causing duplicates.

judge_notes.glm: Filing verification forms by production date instead of verification date is a plausible, specific recordkeeping error that only causes wasted time and possible duplicates, fitting naturally into a HACCP verification discussion.
judge_notes.deepseek: Filing verification records by production date instead of verification date is a plausible but real indexing error causing traceability confusion, with only minor inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Darnell believes the squeak means his brake pads are completely worn out, so he plans to skip any inspection and just buy a brand-new set of pads before tomorrow's commute.
flaw_explanation: Squealing is usually caused by contamination, glazing, or misalignment rather than worn pads, and pads often have plenty of material left. By assuming they're finished without checking, Darnell would likely spend money and time replacing parts that only needed cleaning or realignment.

judge_notes.glm: Skipping inspection to buy new pads is a plausible but flawed plan about a minor bike repair, and the flaw (squeaks usually stem from contamination, glazing, or misalignment) is a specific, verifiable mechanical fact.
judge_notes.deepseek: Skipping inspection to buy new pads is a plausible garage-conversation belief whose main flaw—misdiagnosing squeal as worn pads—is a clear, verifiable error.

seeker_flawed_plan: Chloe plans to wait until she has been completely pain-free for a full month before touching any climbing wall again, believing that only total rest will let her shoulder fully recover.
flaw_explanation: The flaw is that she assumes complete rest is required, when rehab guidance typically favors gradually reintroducing gentle, controlled movement well before a month of total pain-free rest. Following her plan would likely just delay her return and slow her progress, wasting time rather than helping recovery.

judge_notes.glm: The plan fits the injury-recovery conversation, its worst case is only delayed progress, and the flaw (total rest vs. gradual rehab) is a clear, verifiable error.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan fits the injury-recovery topic, its flaw is a verifiable rehab misconception, and the worst outcome is only delayed progress.

seeker_flawed_plan: Chloe plans to track her comeback by scheduling her hardest climbing sessions for the end of each week, believing that a full week of easy climbing beforehand means her shoulder will be at its strongest for the tough routes.
flaw_explanation: This assumes strength and readiness simply accumulate over a week of light activity, but for a recovering shoulder, a hard session at the end of the week often comes when cumulative fatigue has built up, so she may actually perform worse than if she spread the intensity more evenly. The flaw is in the timing assumption, not in the tracking itself, and acting on it would only cost her some progress quality, not her safety.

judge_notes.glm: The plan fits the comeback topic, its worst case is a subpar session rather than injury, and the cumulative-fatigue timing flaw is a clear, verifiable error.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan fits the injury-comeback topic, its flaw is a specific verifiable timing/fatigue error, and acting on it risks only worse progress quality, not safety.

seeker_flawed_plan: Naveen plans to attach both clamps to his own car's dead battery first, then walk over to the helper's car and attach the other ends, figuring the order of connections doesn't matter.
flaw_explanation: The order doesn't affect the outcome at all, but the real issue is that he plans to attach both clamps of the same jumper cable to the same battery, which creates no circuit at all. The cables must connect the two separate batteries to each other, so his sequence will simply result in no charge and wasted time before he realizes the mistake.

judge_notes.deepseek: Attaching both clamps of one cable to the same battery creates no circuit, so the plan fails harmlessly but is a clear, verifiable error.
judge_notes.glm: The stated flaw is itself factually wrong: attaching the two near-end clamps to the dead battery and the far ends to the helper's battery would form a working circuit, so the claimed 'no circuit at all' error does not actually exist in the plan.

seeker_flawed_plan: Helena plans to base her excavation cost estimate on trench volumes calculated straight from the length of the old sewer line on the as-built drawing, assuming the trench length equals the pipe length and using one average depth figure for the whole run.
flaw_explanation: The flaw is assuming the trench length and depth match the as-built drawing's straight-line pipe length and a single average depth. Real excavation needs extra length at joints and connections, and depth varies along the run to maintain slope, so her volume calculation will come out low, making her estimate somewhat inaccurate.

judge_notes.glm: The flawed estimating shortcut fits the excavation-cost topic, its error (ignoring slope-driven depth variation and extra trench length) is verifiable, and acting on it only yields a somewhat low estimate that can be revised.
judge_notes.deepseek: Underestimating trench volume from straight pipe length and a single average depth is a clear, verifiable quantity-takeoff error that fits naturally into a sewer excavation cost discussion.

seeker_flawed_plan: Rasmus plans to design the new fall-detection alerts by ranking every alert type purely by how frequently it fired last month, then tuning only the top few alert types, assuming the most frequently triggered alerts are always the main contributors to alarm fatigue.
flaw_explanation: Alert frequency alone doesn't capture alarm fatigue; a rarer but highly urgent or false-positive-prone alert can annoy caregivers more, and each alert type should be weighted by factors like false-positive rate and staff response burden. Tuning only the most common alerts may leave the most fatiguing alerts untouched, giving a worse but harmless result.

judge_notes.glm: Frequency-only tuning is a plausible but flawed approach to alarm fatigue, the flaw is specific and verifiable, and the worst outcome is a suboptimal alert design with no safety or legal risk.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan is a plausible but flawed alert-design approach whose main error is assuming frequency alone identifies the biggest contributors to alarm fatigue.

seeker_flawed_plan: Cherise plans to request her free annual credit report from each of the three nationwide bureaus on the same day, believing that pulling all three at once gives her a complete, up-to-date snapshot she can review in a single sitting before she starts setting aside money.
flaw_explanation: The three bureaus don't share data or update in sync, so requesting all three simultaneously can produce reports that disagree on balances and account statuses, giving her a muddled picture rather than a reliable baseline. Spacing the requests out, or ordering them through the centralized annual credit report site, would let her compare more usefully.

judge_notes.glm: Requesting all three reports at once is standard, sound advice for a complete snapshot, so the stated flaw mischaracterizes a reasonable plan rather than identifying a real error.
judge_notes.deepseek: Pulling all three credit reports at once is a minor practical misstep, not a safety risk, and fits naturally into financial planning for leaving an unsafe relationship.

seeker_flawed_plan: Uri plans to judge his tires' tread depth just by pressing a fingertip into the grooves and trusting how deep it feels, figuring that a visual and touch check is enough before winter.
flaw_explanation: A finger can't distinguish shallow depths accurately—treads near the replacement threshold feel surprisingly similar to new ones by touch. Using a tread depth gauge (or even a coin) gives an actual measurement, so Uri may end up with an unreliable read and have to redo the check.

judge_notes.glm: Relying on touch could lead Uri to keep worn tires for winter driving, a genuine safety risk rather than mere inconvenience, though the flaw itself is real and clearly checkable.
judge_notes.deepseek: Fingertip feel can't reliably gauge tread depth near the replacement threshold, risking unsafe winter tires, so the flaw is real and safety-relevant.

seeker_flawed_plan: Rana plans to calculate each crate's share of the load by dividing its total shipping weight by the area of its base footprint, and then use those per-crate figures alone to decide how to arrange the stacks across the truck floor.
flaw_explanation: Dividing weight by footprint gives average pressure per crate, but it ignores how the crates' combined weights stack vertically, so a tall stack of lightweight-base crates can concentrate more load on one floor spot than the per-crate numbers suggest. The calculation is a reasonable starting point but needs to account for cumulative weight at each contact point, not just individual crate figures.

judge_notes.glm: The plan fits the warehouse conversation, its flaw (ignoring cumulative stacked weight at each contact point) is a clear, verifiable practical error, and acting on it would at worst cause wasted effort or a suboptimal load arrangement.
judge_notes.deepseek: Ignoring cumulative stacked weight could overload the truck floor or cause a collapse, so the flaw is a real safety-relevant error.

seeker_flawed_plan: Nourael plans to size the braces for the temporary exhibit wall by matching their length to the wall's height, assuming a brace works equally well whether it attaches to the top of the wall or partway down.
flaw_explanation: Brace effectiveness depends heavily on the attachment angle and height, not just length; a brace anchored at the same height as its base provides almost no resistance to the wall tipping. Braces need to attach high on the wall and anchor low on the floor to create a resisting angle.

judge_notes.glm: A badly braced temporary exhibit wall could tip over and injure people, so the risk is not merely minor inconvenience, though the flaw itself is relevant and clearly checkable.
judge_notes.deepseek: A brace attached at the same height as its base provides little tipping resistance, so the flawed plan risks wall collapse and injury, making it not benign.

seeker_flawed_plan: Amara plans to lay out the sterile drape on the table first thing in the morning, hours before the procedure, so the field is 'ready and waiting' and she can arrange everything else around it at a relaxed pace.
flaw_explanation: A sterile field should be set up as close to the time of use as possible, because the longer the opened drape sits exposed, the greater the chance it gets contaminated by dust or passing activity. Setting it up hours early will likely mean the whole drape has to be discarded and replaced with a fresh one right before surgery, wasting time and materials.

judge_notes.glm: Setting up a sterile field hours early is a real, verifiable sterile-technique error that fits the scene, and its worst outcome is wasted time and materials with no safety risk.
judge_notes.deepseek: Setting up a sterile drape hours early risks contamination and would require replacement, but the consequence is wasted time and materials rather than harm.

seeker_flawed_plan: Daphne plans to label each mold sample bag by writing directly on the wet-surface plastic with a regular ballpoint pen, assuming the ink will stay legible through handling and transport to the lab.
flaw_explanation: Ballpoint ink often smears or fails to adhere to damp or slick plastic, so the labels can become unreadable before the samples reach the lab. She should use a permanent marker on a dry area of the bag or attach paper labels instead.

judge_notes.glm: Writing on damp plastic with a ballpoint pen risks smudged, unreadable labels, a minor practical issue that fits naturally into a mold sampling conversation and is easily verified.
judge_notes.deepseek: Mislabeling samples is only a minor practical inconvenience, fits the mold-sampling topic, and the ink-adhesion flaw is a clear, verifiable error.

seeker_flawed_plan: Alphonse plans to photograph each bolt head and rate its corrosion on a simple 1-to-5 visual scale, then average those ratings to produce one overall corrosion score for the playground structure.
flaw_explanation: Averaging visual ratings across bolts hides the worst cases: a structure with many clean bolts and one badly corroded bolt would score well, even though that single bolt is the one that matters. The average describes the typical bolt, not the condition that determines whether the equipment is sound.

judge_notes.glm: The averaging method fits the inspection topic and the flaw is clear, but acting on it could declare a structure sound despite one critically corroded bolt, posing a real safety risk to children using the equipment.
judge_notes.deepseek: Averaging bolt corrosion ratings can mask a single critically corroded bolt, creating a real safety risk on playground equipment.

seeker_flawed_plan: Harriet plans to draft the validation plan around the vendor's own test script templates, assuming those templates already reflect the lab's current workflows and can be signed off as-is once the upgrade is installed.
flaw_explanation: Vendor templates are written generically for the software's default configuration, so they won't match the lab's customized fields, interfaces, or report formats; the scripts would pass without actually exercising the lab's real workflows, and the gap would only surface later during rework.

judge_notes.glm: The vendor-template assumption is a plausible, topic-appropriate mistake whose main consequence is rework and wasted effort rather than immediate harm.
judge_notes.deepseek: Vendor templates are generic and won't exercise the lab's customized workflows, so signing off as-is risks a validation gap that surfaces later in rework.

seeker_flawed_plan: Aziz plans to wipe down the safety station's metal surfaces with a dry microfiber cloth before taking static readings, thinking that a clean, lint-free surface will give the most accurate baseline measurement.
flaw_explanation: Rubbing a dry cloth on a surface generates and redistributes static charge rather than removing it, so the reading would reflect the wiping action instead of the ambient conditions.

judge_notes.glm: Dry-wiping metal surfaces generates triboelectric charge, corrupting the baseline reading, but the only consequence is a flawed measurement in a safe, on-topic scenario.
judge_notes.deepseek: Wiping metal with a dry cloth generates static charge, so the baseline reading would be invalid and could mislead safety decisions in a dust-explosion hazard area.

seeker_flawed_plan: Aziz plans to compare static readings taken at the mill's safety station using a handheld field meter against a lab-grade meter's values, assuming the two instruments can be used interchangeably once their displayed numbers are close.
flaw_explanation: Handheld field meters and lab-grade meters typically have different input impedances and calibration tolerances, so similar displayed numbers do not mean the readings are equivalent or comparable across instruments.

judge_notes.glm: Treating the meters as interchangeable could give falsely reassuring static readings in a flour-dust environment, where static ignition is a genuine explosion hazard, so the outcome is not merely minor inconvenience.
judge_notes.deepseek: Treating handheld and lab-grade static meters as interchangeable based on similar displayed numbers is a real metrological error, and in a flour-dust environment misjudged static readings could bear on explosion safety, so the outcome is not merely benign.

seeker_flawed_plan: Renata plans to count the number of duplicate reports for each bug and prioritize whichever bugs have the most duplicates, assuming that a bug reported many times is automatically the most severe and must be fixed first.
flaw_explanation: Duplicate counts measure visibility and annoyance, not severity or risk, so a cosmetic issue seen by many users could outrank a serious bug that few people encountered. Triage should weigh severity and affected workflows alongside frequency, so Renata's approach may waste effort fixing low-impact issues first and produce a slightly worse prioritized list.

judge_notes.glm: The duplicate-count heuristic is a plausible triage suggestion in this setting, its flaw (frequency ≠ severity) is a clear, verifiable error, and acting on it only yields a slightly worse prioritized list.
judge_notes.deepseek: Prioritizing by duplicate count conflates visibility with severity, a clear triage error that fits the bug-prioritization scene and risks only a worse prioritized list.

seeker_flawed_plan: Helena plans to wait to discuss driving with her father until he brings the subject up himself, reasoning that if he hasn't raised any concerns by then, he must still be driving fine and the conversation can be postponed indefinitely.
flaw_explanation: The plan assumes the father will voluntarily admit difficulties with driving, but many older adults are reluctant to raise the topic themselves out of pride or fear of losing independence. Waiting for him to bring it up means the conversation may never happen or happens far later than it should, making Helena's timing approach ineffective.

judge_notes.glm: Postponing the driving conversation indefinitely could allow an unsafe elderly driver to remain on the road, posing real safety risks, and the flaw—that seniors rarely volunteer driving concerns—is a well-documented, verifiable problem.
judge_notes.deepseek: Waiting for the father to raise driving concerns himself risks indefinite delay on a safety issue, so the flaw is real and the plan fits the scene.

seeker_flawed_plan: Dina plans to pick the respirator cartridge by matching its color code to the color of the paint she is stripping, assuming the cartridge labeling follows the same scheme as paint color charts.
flaw_explanation: Respirator cartridge color codes identify the type of hazard (such as particulates versus certain vapors), not the color of the paint being removed, so matching by paint color tells her nothing about whether the cartridge is appropriate for lead paint dust.

judge_notes.glm: Matching cartridges to paint color could leave Dina unprotected against lead dust, a real health hazard, though the flaw itself is a clear, verifiable misconception about cartridge color codes.
judge_notes.deepseek: Choosing a respirator cartridge by paint color could leave Dina unprotected from lead dust, a serious health risk, and the flaw is a clear, verifiable error.

seeker_flawed_plan: Kono plans to run the stability study by testing the tincture samples only at the start and at the very end of the twelve-month storage period, reasoning that two time points are enough to confirm the product stays stable.
flaw_explanation: With only two time points, Kono cannot tell when or how quickly any change in appearance or marker content occurred, so the study gives a much weaker picture of the degradation trend. Interim testing points are normally included so changes can be tracked over time.

judge_notes.glm: The two-time-point stability plan is a plausible topic for this scene, its flaw (missing interim points obscures the degradation trend) is a verifiable practical error, and the worst outcome is only a weaker study and wasted effort.
judge_notes.deepseek: Skipping interim time points is a real stability-study design flaw, but it only weakens the data rather than posing health, safety, legal, or major financial risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Tatiana plans to buy biological indicator ampoules for her thesis project on studio sterilization workflows, figuring she can incubate them at room temperature on a shelf in the studio's back room since that seems simpler than tracking down an incubator.
flaw_explanation: Biological indicator spores only germinate at the specific incubation temperature the ampoule is designed for (typically 55-60°C), so a room-temperature shelf will not activate the growth medium. She would end up reading every ampoule as a false 'no growth' result and have to redo the runs with proper incubation.

judge_notes.glm: The plan fits the studio sterilization topic, and its flaw—needing a proper incubator temperature for BI spore germination—is a verifiable practical error whose worst outcome is only wasted time and redone runs.
judge_notes.deepseek: Room-temperature incubation of biological indicators yields false negatives, but the consequence is only wasted time and redoing runs, not a safety or legal risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Naveed plans to judge the swelling by pressing the battery pack flat on the locker shelf and checking whether it rocks, reasoning that a swollen pack will wobble while a healthy one sits steady.
flaw_explanation: The battery's own casing and the surface it rests on determine whether it rocks, so a flat, undeformed pack on a shelf with a slight warp can wobble just as easily as a swollen one; the rocking test doesn't isolate swelling from the surface or case shape.

judge_notes.glm: The flawed rocking test could falsely clear a genuinely swollen LiPo, leading Naveed to fly with a fire-risk battery, so the worst outcome is a real safety hazard rather than mere inconvenience.
judge_notes.deepseek: Pressing and rocking a swollen LiPo battery risks puncturing or compressing a damaged cell, which can cause fire or explosion, so the plan is not benign.

seeker_flawed_plan: Ari plans to run the robot's full acceptance test suite once, at the start of a single day, and use those passing results as the acceptance criteria baseline for the entire multi-week validation period.
flaw_explanation: A single run captures only one set of conditions, so it can't show that performance stays within limits across days, operators, and reagent lots. Acceptance criteria need to be checked with repeated runs spread over time, so Ari's approach would likely mean redoing much of the testing later.

judge_notes.glm: The single-run baseline is a plausible but flawed validation approach that fits the scene, and its main error—ignoring variability across time, operators, and lots—is clearly checkable, with the worst outcome being wasted effort and a weaker validation rather than safety or legal harm.
