judge_notes.deepseek: A single-run baseline is a genuine validation error that would cause rework, but the consequences are limited to wasted time and effort rather than safety or legal harm.

seeker_flawed_plan: Oskar plans to have the crew mark the proposed anchor positions on the billboard's front face from the ground using a laser pointer and binoculars, then verify the marks visually before anyone goes up, figuring this saves a trip up the ladder.
flaw_explanation: The flaw is that a laser dot and pencil marks on a large sign face are nearly impossible to align and read accurately from ground level at that distance and angle, so the marked positions won't reliably match the intended anchor points. The crew will end up climbing up anyway to re-measure, wasting the time the ground-marking step was meant to save.

judge_notes.glm: The ground-marking plan is plausible in this scene, its worst outcome is wasted time from inaccurate marks, and the alignment/reading accuracy problem is a specific, verifiable practical flaw.
judge_notes.deepseek: Ground-level laser marking on a large billboard face is impractical to align and read accurately, so the flaw is real and the worst outcome is wasted time, not safety risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Julian plans to log each hammock's strap condition by measuring the total length of every suspension strap with a cloth tape and comparing it to the original spec, figuring that any stretch or wear will show up as a length difference he can track over time.
flaw_explanation: Strap length is a poor wear indicator because nylon webbing stretches and recovers with load and humidity, so small length changes are normal and won't reliably reveal fraying; the frayed fibers and abrasion are visible on the surface and at stitch lines, which a tape measure won't capture.

judge_notes.glm: Relying on strap length to detect fraying could miss dangerous wear on suspension straps holding a person aloft, creating a real fall/safety risk, though the flaw itself is a clear, verifiable error and fits the inspection conversation naturally.
judge_notes.deepseek: Relying on strap length to detect wear could miss frayed straps and create a real safety hazard for aerial yoga users.

seeker_flawed_plan: Lowell plans to judge the new autoclave cycle by checking whether the indicator tape on the outside of each bundled lab coat turns dark, treating a full color change as proof the load reached sterilizing conditions throughout.
flaw_explanation: External indicator tape only responds to temperature at the surface of the bundle, so it can change color even when the interior of a tightly packed load never reaches the required temperature; only a chemical or biological indicator placed inside the load can show that.

judge_notes.glm: Relying only on external indicator tape is a classic, well-documented sterilization monitoring mistake that fits the autoclave topic, and the worst realistic outcome here is a failed or wasted sterilization cycle rather than serious harm.
judge_notes.deepseek: Relying on external indicator tape can falsely certify sterilization, risking inadequate decontamination of lab coats.

seeker_flawed_plan: Ravi plans to add up all the load values on his calculation sheet by summing the platform weight, the live load, and the equipment load as the final step, after applying the safety factor, so the factor of safety is applied first and then everything is combined into one total.
flaw_explanation: The safety factor should be applied to the combined total load last, not multiplied into individual loads before summing them. Applying it first and then adding everything together gives an inflated result that misstates the design load and will force him to redo the sheet.

judge_notes.glm: The stated flaw is not a real error: multiplying each load by the safety factor and then summing is mathematically identical to summing first and multiplying the total, so the claimed 'inflated result' would not occur.
judge_notes.deepseek: Applying the safety factor to individual loads before summing is a real, verifiable calculation error that would inflate the total and require redoing the sheet, but poses only minor inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Boris plans to draw the smoke-control zone boundaries on the charrette floor plans using the guest-room corridor centerlines as the dividing lines, since that keeps each zone visually tidy and easy to label.
flaw_explanation: Smoke-control zone boundaries must follow the actual smoke barriers and door assemblies, not corridor centerlines; using centerlines will put the boundary in the middle of a corridor rather than at the rated wall or door that actually stops smoke spread, so the zones won't match the physical barrier layout.

judge_notes.glm: The plan is a plausible charrette sketching choice whose flaw (boundaries on corridor centerlines instead of actual smoke barriers) is a clear, verifiable design error with only wasted-effort consequences at this stage.
judge_notes.deepseek: Misplacing smoke-control zone boundaries away from rated barriers is a genuine life-safety error, not mere inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Nefeli plans to set the alert thresholds by averaging the readings from all the underpass sensors together and applying that single average threshold to every sensor, since they are all the same model.
flaw_explanation: Identical sensor models can sit at different elevations and drain geometries, so a shared average threshold will misfire at some locations; each sensor needs its own baseline-based threshold.

judge_notes.glm: A single averaged threshold could cause missed or false flood alerts at an underpass during heavy rain, creating a real safety risk, though the flaw itself is a clear, verifiable engineering error.
judge_notes.deepseek: A shared average threshold could fail to trigger flood alerts at low-elevation underpasses, creating real safety risk, and the elevation/geometry flaw is a clear, verifiable error.

seeker_flawed_plan: Nolan plans to write the lockout procedure so that the conveyor is shut off first and the lock is applied only after the machine has fully come to a stop, since he believes locking out a moving conveyor isn't practical.
flaw_explanation: Standard lockout practice is to apply the lock immediately after shutting off the power, before the machine has a chance to be restarted, not after it stops. Waiting until the conveyor has fully stopped leaves a window where someone could restart it, and it misses the point that the lock secures the energy source rather than the motion itself.

judge_notes.glm: The flawed lockout sequence creates a real safety hazard (restart window during maintenance), fits the conveyor lockout topic naturally, and the error is specific and verifiable.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan creates a real safety hazard by delaying lockout until after the conveyor stops, leaving a restart window, and the flaw is a clear, verifiable error in standard lockout practice.

seeker_flawed_plan: Naveed plans to compare the swollen pack's overall dimensions against the manufacturer's original spec sheet, assuming that if the case measures within a couple of millimeters of the listed size, the swelling is within normal tolerance and the pack can go back into service.
flaw_explanation: The spec sheet lists the dimensions of a new, unswollen pack, so any increase at all already indicates gas buildup; measuring against the original size treats the starting point as a tolerance band rather than a baseline, and the soft case can also bulge in the middle while the outer edges still measure close to spec.

judge_notes.glm: Returning a swollen LiPo to service risks fire, and the flaw is real: any dimensional increase signals gas buildup, and mid-case bulge can hide behind edge measurements.
judge_notes.deepseek: A swollen LiPo pack is a fire hazard, so returning it to service based on a flawed dimension comparison risks real safety harm.

seeker_flawed_plan: Reina plans to total up the cable length for each run by adding the straight-line distance between outlets and then rounding the grand total up to the next whole box size, assuming the extra slack will cover any bends and routing around equipment.
flaw_explanation: Straight-line distances ignore the extra length added by every bend, doorway, and detour around furniture, so the rounded-up total can still fall short once the cable actually follows the walls and floor. Measuring along the intended route instead would give a realistic figure.

judge_notes.glm: Underestimating cable length by using straight-line distances is a real, verifiable practical error, but the worst outcome is mainly wasted time and a second trip for more cable, and it fits naturally into a conversation about planning cable runs for a pop-up clinic.
judge_notes.deepseek: Undersized cable runs in a clinic create real electrical safety and fire risks, so the flaw is not merely an inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Rashida plans to write her report about the manager's unsafe practices by hand in a lined notebook first, believing she must submit only a signed paper copy because she assumes the resort's regional office will not accept emailed complaints.
flaw_explanation: The regional office actually accepts emailed complaints and even encourages them for faster routing. Drafting everything by hand first would just cost her extra time transcribing it, without changing the outcome.

judge_notes.glm: Hand-drafting and assuming email isn't accepted only wastes her time, fits naturally into her reporting dilemma, and the flaw is a specific, verifiable factual error about the office's complaint channels.
judge_notes.deepseek: Handwriting a report first only wastes time since the regional office accepts emailed complaints, a minor inconvenience with no real risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Una plans to apply the grout to the mosaic bench on the same day the china pieces are set, believing this saves time and the pieces will be held firmly enough.
flaw_explanation: Mortar needs to cure for at least about 24 hours before grouting; grouting too soon can shift the pieces or weaken the bond. This only wastes time and materials, as the section would need to be redone.

judge_notes.glm: Grouting before the mortar cures (~24 hours) is a real, verifiable error that would only waste time and materials, and it fits naturally into a conversation about making a mosaic bench safe for public seating.
judge_notes.deepseek: Grouting before the mortar cures is a real, verifiable error that only causes rework and wasted materials, fitting naturally into the mosaic bench conversation.

seeker_flawed_plan: Mikkel plans to do the radio's channel check and volume/squelch test as the very last items on the pre-launch checklist, after everything else on the boat is already done, since he figures the radio checks are quick and can be squeezed in right before departure.
flaw_explanation: The flaw is that the radio checks should come early, not last: if a check reveals a problem like a dead battery or a stuck squelch, doing it last means all the other completed steps may need to be revisited or redone, wasting time. Placing radio checks first lets any radio issue be sorted out while the rest of the checklist proceeds.

judge_notes.glm: Doing radio checks last is a real sequencing error that wastes time if a fault is found, fits naturally into a radio checklist review, and risks only delay.
judge_notes.deepseek: Doing radio checks last risks wasted rework if a fault is found, but the consequence is only minor inconvenience, and the flaw is a clear, verifiable checklist-ordering error fitting the marine radio topic.

seeker_flawed_plan: Doreen plans to select the detector tube with the widest printed measuring range she can find, figuring that a broader range will let her handle any solvent concentration in the shop without switching tubes.
flaw_explanation: Wider-range tubes typically have coarser graduation and lower sensitivity, so a broad-range tube may not resolve the low concentrations she actually needs to document, giving her a less precise result and forcing a repeat test.

judge_notes.glm: Choosing a wide-range tube for low-concentration documentation is a real, verifiable tradeoff (coarser graduations, lower sensitivity), fits the scene naturally, and the worst case is only a wasted or repeated test.
judge_notes.deepseek: Choosing a wide-range tube is a plausible but flawed selection that mainly causes imprecision and repeat testing, not serious harm.

seeker_flawed_plan: Hannelore plans to save the instrument audit trail exports as PDF printouts and then run optical character recognition on the scanned pages, believing the text layer will preserve the original timestamps and sequence exactly as recorded.
flaw_explanation: OCR on printed audit trails can reorder or misread entries and strip the original metadata, so the reconstructed text will not reliably match the source sequence; the archive should retain the native export format rather than a scanned derivative.

judge_notes.glm: In a regulated compliance archive, replacing native audit trail exports with OCR'd scans risks data-integrity non-compliance and regulatory/legal consequences, not just minor inconvenience; the flaw is specific, verifiable, and the plan's core problem.
judge_notes.deepseek: OCR of printed audit trails can corrupt timestamps and sequence and lose metadata, so the plan risks noncompliant, unreliable archival records rather than mere inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Harlan plans to set up the immutable donation log by first enabling versioning on the storage bucket and then uploading the monthly ledger exports, assuming that turning on versioning afterward will also protect the files already uploaded.
flaw_explanation: Versioning only applies to objects uploaded after it is enabled, so the earlier ledger exports would remain unprotected and could be overwritten without retaining prior versions. The order of steps needs to be reversed.

judge_notes.glm: The flaw is a real, verifiable ordering mistake about storage versioning, fits the ledger topic, and the worst case is data loss requiring redoing work rather than safety or legal harm.
judge_notes.deepseek: The versioning-order mistake is a real, verifiable flaw, but its consequence is only unprotected ledger exports, a minor operational inconvenience rather than a serious harm.

seeker_flawed_plan: Bashira plans to record the impact attenuation readings from the field tester immediately after each drop without waiting, assuming the displayed number is the final result once the weight settles.
flaw_explanation: Many field impact testers need a short settling or averaging interval after the drop, and reading the display too early captures a transient value rather than the stabilized result, so the recorded numbers will be slightly off and may need to be redone.

judge_notes.glm: Reading the tester too early only risks slightly inaccurate readings and redoing drops, fits naturally into a surface inspection conversation, and the settling/averaging interval issue is a specific, verifiable practical error.
judge_notes.deepseek: Reading the tester too early yields transient values, a minor accuracy issue with no safety risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Shirin plans to wipe down each concentrator's exterior filters with standard household paper towels and all-purpose surface cleaner before logging the monthly maintenance check, believing this counts as completing the filter-cleaning step.
flaw_explanation: All-purpose cleaner can leave residue on the filter media, and paper towels can shred fibers into the mesh, so the filters are not actually clean. The filter-cleaning step requires rinsing with plain water and air-drying, so her method wastes time and the check would need to be redone.

judge_notes.glm: The flawed cleaning method plausibly arises in this maintenance conversation, its error (residue and fiber shedding vs. rinse-and-air-dry) is specific and verifiable, and the worst outcome is redoing the check, a minor inconvenience.
judge_notes.deepseek: Using all-purpose cleaner and paper towels on concentrator filters is a plausible but incorrect cleaning method whose flaw is specific and verifiable, with only wasted time and rework as consequences.

seeker_flawed_plan: Svea plans to set each sensor's alert threshold by averaging its readings over the past week and adding a fixed margin, assuming that a week of data gives a stable baseline for every sensor.
flaw_explanation: A week is too short and too season-dependent to establish a stable baseline; routine demand changes and weather swings within that window will skew the average, so the margin ends up either too tight or too loose and the thresholds need rework.

judge_notes.glm: The plan fits the sensor-threshold topic and the flaw is a clear, verifiable statistical error, but mis-set thresholds on water-main pressure sensors could mask real pressure anomalies (bursts, leaks), posing more than trivial risk to infrastructure and the public.
judge_notes.deepseek: Averaging a week of sensor data ignores seasonal and demand variability, so the baseline is unstable and thresholds will need rework—an ordinary, low-stakes engineering inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Alvaro plans to evaluate the roof membrane seams purely by visual inspection, marking every seam that looks straight and uniform from a few feet away as adequately bonded and suitable for nearby solar racking attachment points.
flaw_explanation: A seam can look flat and even while having unbonded spots or small gaps that are not visible from a standing position, so visual inspection alone misses defects that a seam probe or similar check would catch. Following this plan, Alvaro would waste survey time marking unsuitable seams and would need to redo the evaluation.

judge_notes.glm: Visual-only seam inspection plausibly arises in this roof survey conversation, its flaw (hidden unbonded spots missed without probing) is verifiable, and the worst outcome is wasted survey time.
judge_notes.deepseek: Visual-only seam inspection can miss unbonded spots, causing wasted survey time and rework but no serious safety or financial harm.

seeker_flawed_plan: Alvaro plans to document seam conditions by taking photos of each seam during a single midday pass and using those images alone to build his evaluation report, since good daylight photos should capture everything he needs.
flaw_explanation: Photos alone miss what a seam evaluation actually relies on, such as probe testing along the seam weld and notes about surface conditions like moisture or debris. He would end up with an incomplete report and have to make a second trip to redo the assessment properly.

judge_notes.glm: Relying only on midday photos for seam evaluation is a plausible but flawed plan that misses probe testing and surface-condition notes, with the worst outcome being a wasted trip and redo.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan is a plausible but flawed shortcut whose main problem is that photos alone cannot substitute for probe testing and surface-condition notes, causing an incomplete report and a redo trip.

seeker_flawed_plan: Giorgio plans to write the runbook's recovery steps in strict chronological order, starting from the moment the outage is detected and walking through each action the team took during the last real incident, so the document reads like a clean narrative.
flaw_explanation: A runbook organized as a timeline of one past incident buries the decision points and recovery branches, so during a different failure responders must read the whole narrative to find the step that applies, wasting time. Runbooks work better structured by system and by symptom or trigger, with steps that can be entered at any point.

judge_notes.glm: Writing a runbook as a chronological narrative of one past incident is a common but flawed approach that buries decision points, and the flaw is clearly explainable and fits naturally into a tabletop exercise discussion about runbook writing.
judge_notes.deepseek: Writing a runbook as a chronological narrative of one past incident is a plausible but flawed approach that buries decision points and branches, though the consequence is only wasted time during recovery.

seeker_flawed_plan: Nadine believes that any over-the-counter cold remedy labeled 'non-drowsy' is always a second-generation antihistamine, so she plans to combine any two products marked 'non-drowsy' without checking whether they share the same active ingredient, expecting the labels alone to guarantee the combination is different enough to be safe together.
flaw_explanation: The 'non-drowsy' label is a marketing phrase, not a guarantee of the active ingredient class, and it says nothing about other components like decongestants or pain relievers. Two 'non-drowsy' products can still contain overlapping active ingredients, so she could end up buying a combination that is redundant or unsuitable and have to make another trip back to the pharmacy.

judge_notes.glm: The belief fits the pharmacy topic naturally, the flaw is a clear verifiable point about 'non-drowsy' being marketing rather than an ingredient-class guarantee, and the stated worst case is only a wasted trip or redundant purchase.
judge_notes.deepseek: Combining overlapping cold remedies can cause dangerous ingredient duplication (e.g., acetaminophen overdose), so the outcome is not merely minor inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Chandra plans to first trace the customer's sacred symbol onto a sheet of ordinary tracing paper, then transfer it onto the skin by pressing the paper onto freshly applied henna paste so the outline lifts off cleanly.
flaw_explanation: Pressing tracing paper onto wet henna paste will smear the paste and pull it off the skin rather than transfer a clean outline, because the paste is wet and tacky and paper does not release an even line; the transfer step needs to happen on dry skin with a dry medium, not onto wet paste.

judge_notes.glm: The flawed transfer method would only ruin a henna design, fits naturally into the henna-booth conversation, and the smear/pull-off problem with wet paste is a clear, verifiable practical error.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan is a plausible henna-transfer idea whose main flaw—pressing paper onto wet paste smears rather than transfers—is a clear, verifiable practical error.

seeker_flawed_plan: Emil plans to tighten the plate pack bolts by simply going around the frame once, bringing each bolt straight to the full specified torque in a single pass.
flaw_explanation: Heat exchanger gaskets need to be compressed gradually and evenly, usually in several passes with increasing torque in a crisscross order. Tightening each bolt to full torque in one pass can leave the plate pack unevenly compressed, so the gasket may not seal properly and the job would need to be redone.

judge_notes.deepseek: Tightening plate pack bolts in one pass to full torque is a real procedural error that risks a leaking gasket and rework, but only minor inconvenience.
judge_notes.glm: Single-pass full-torque tightening is a real, verifiable mistake that would only cause a poor seal and redo work, fitting naturally into a gasket-replacement conversation.

seeker_flawed_plan: Doreen plans to pick the highest-range detector tube available in the closet, reasoning that it will cover the widest span of solvent concentrations and save her from choosing between several tubes.
flaw_explanation: A high-range tube has coarser scale divisions and a higher detection limit, so at the low concentrations she actually expects it may read nothing or give a much less precise value than a low-range tube matched to the expected concentration.

judge_notes.glm: Choosing an overly high-range tube mainly wastes time and yields imprecise or zero readings at low concentrations, a fixable practical error that fits naturally into a detector-tube selection conversation.
judge_notes.deepseek: Choosing a high-range tube for low expected concentrations is a real, verifiable selection error that would at worst yield poor readings, not a safety hazard.

seeker_flawed_plan: Carlos plans to diagnose the pump's problem by looking only for the single tallest peak in the vibration spectrum and assuming that peak's frequency directly identifies the failing component, ignoring all the smaller peaks in the plot.
flaw_explanation: The largest peak is often just running-speed energy that is normal for a centrifugal pump, while the diagnostic signature of a developing fault can appear as much smaller peaks at harmonic or sub-synchronous frequencies. Judging only by tallest peak means he may misidentify the cause or miss an early fault indicator, costing him time but nothing more.

judge_notes.glm: The tallest-peak-only approach is a plausible, checkable diagnostic error that fits the pump-vibration conversation, and per the stated flaw its worst outcome is a misdiagnosis costing time rather than safety or money.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan fits the pump-diagnosis topic, and the flaw is a specific, verifiable spectral-analysis error whose worst consequence is wasted time, not safety risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Helena plans to schedule the conversation with her father for right after dinner, believing he will be most receptive and relaxed at that time of day.
flaw_explanation: Evening is often when an older adult is tired and least able to absorb a difficult conversation, so a morning or midday chat, when he is more alert, usually goes better. Picking the wrong time will not cause harm, but the talk may go poorly and need to be redone.

judge_notes.glm: Choosing a poor conversation time is a mild, verifiable practical mistake that fits naturally into Helena and Moses's discussion about her father's driving.
judge_notes.deepseek: Timing the talk for after dinner is a plausible but flawed choice, since evening fatigue can make the conversation harder, though the consequence is only a poor or repeated talk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Ruben believes that a lightning strike would only damage the most sensitive component in the system, the pump's variable frequency drive, so he plans to skip testing the simpler parts like the relay coil and float switch and troubleshoot the VFD board first.
flaw_explanation: A surge doesn't necessarily target only the most delicate component; ordinary relays, fuses, and control wiring are often damaged by lightning as well, and any of them can interrupt operation. By assuming the VFD is the sole suspect, Ruben may spend hours diagnosing a healthy drive while the actual fault is in a cheap relay or a blown fuse he skipped.

judge_notes.glm: Skipping basic components to test only the VFD wastes time but poses no safety or legal risk, fits naturally in a pump troubleshooting conversation, and the flaw about surges damaging relays and fuses is a clear, verifiable practical error.
judge_notes.deepseek: Skipping simple tests to chase the VFD is a plausible but flawed troubleshooting shortcut that mainly wastes time and money, not safety.

seeker_flawed_plan: Conor plans to identify mold-prone spots in the new cold-storage facility by walking through once with a handheld moisture meter and taking readings only at eye-level on the walls, reasoning that if those spots are dry the rest of the room is fine.
flaw_explanation: Mold risk concentrates at cold thermal bridges and near the floor or ceiling where condensation collects, so a single eye-level pass misses the very locations most likely to stay damp; the meter also reads surface moisture only and cannot reveal hidden moisture behind panels or insulation.

judge_notes.glm: The flawed survey could let mold develop in a food-storage facility, posing real health and product-safety risks, while the flaw itself is a specific, verifiable error about thermal bridges, condensation zones, and hidden moisture.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan's single eye-level moisture-meter pass would miss condensation-prone thermal bridges and floor/ceiling areas, a real and verifiable flaw with genuine mold-risk consequences.

seeker_flawed_plan: Stellan plans to evaluate the low-bid proposals by checking that each contractor's concrete patch material is the cheapest water-based sealer listed in the city's approved products catalog, assuming that any product on that catalog page is interchangeable for garage deck repairs.
flaw_explanation: The approved products catalog groups items by price tier, not by intended use, so a cheap water-based sealer on that page may be rated for walls or sidewalks rather than for traffic-bearing garage decks. Stellan would end up scoring bids against a product specification that does not match the repair application, wasting time and possibly ranking bids slightly wrong.

judge_notes.glm: The plan plausibly fits the procurement scene, its flaw (catalog organized by price tier rather than intended use, so a cheap sealer may not be rated for traffic-bearing decks) is specific and verifiable, and the worst outcome is only wasted time and slightly misranked bids.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan fits the procurement scene, and the flaw is a concrete, verifiable mismatch between catalog price tiers and intended product use.

seeker_flawed_plan: Lowell plans to validate the new autoclave cycle by placing a single chemical indicator strip inside one lab coat's chest pocket for each load, and treating a color change on that strip as proof that the whole load was processed correctly.
flaw_explanation: A chemical indicator strip only confirms conditions at that one spot; it is a pass/fail monitor, not a way to validate a cycle, so a passing strip does not show the coats themselves were adequately processed. A knowledgeable person would explain that proper evaluation needs indicators placed in harder-to-reach spots or a separate validation method, and that a single pocket placement can pass while other parts of the load see different conditions.

judge_notes.glm: The plan fits the topic naturally, and the flaw—that a single chemical indicator is a pass/fail monitor, not cycle validation—is a specific, verifiable error whose worst realistic outcome is inadequately processed coats (a quality/methodology problem rather than a serious safety hazard).
judge_notes.deepseek: A single chemical indicator strip in one pocket cannot validate that the whole load, including the coats themselves, was adequately sterilized.

seeker_flawed_plan: Sanaael plans to write the consent workflow's participant-facing materials at roughly a twelfth-grade reading level, reasoning that this keeps the forms precise and complete while still being understandable to most adults.
flaw_explanation: Plain-language guidance for study materials generally recommends aiming around a sixth- to eighth-grade reading level, since twelfth-grade text excludes many otherwise willing participants. Sanaael's assumption that precision requires high-level wording is off; clarity and accuracy can be preserved with simpler text, and his approach will likely reduce comprehension and participation.

judge_notes.glm: Writing consent materials at a twelfth-grade level is a plausible, low-stakes mistake that directly fits the consent-workflow topic, and the flaw is a verifiable deviation from standard plain-language guidance recommending sixth- to eighth-grade reading levels.
judge_notes.deepseek: Writing consent materials at a twelfth-grade level is a plausible but flawed choice; plain-language guidance recommends sixth- to eighth-grade, and the error is specific and verifiable.

seeker_flawed_plan: Riad plans to check the cracked tile floor by tapping each tile with the plastic handle of a screwdriver and listening for a hollow sound, treating any tile that sounds dull as loose and marking it for the installer.
flaw_explanation: Tapping with a screwdriver handle mostly reveals whether a tile has debonded from the substrate, not whether the floor slab underneath is level or sound enough for a heavy sterilizer; a tile can sound perfectly solid while the substrate beneath it is uneven or cracked, so this check can pass a floor that still needs leveling.

judge_notes.glm: The tap test genuinely detects debonded tiles rather than slab level or structural soundness, fits the floor-inspection topic, and at worst leads to a missed leveling issue during a routine renovation.
judge_notes.deepseek: The tap test can miss an uneven or cracked substrate, risking unsafe installation of a heavy sterilizer, so the flaw is real and consequential.

seeker_flawed_plan: Hiroko plans to confirm that a donated laptop's drive was securely erased by running a file-recovery utility against the drive while it is still mounted and in normal use, reasoning that if nothing recoverable shows up, the wipe must have been thorough.
flaw_explanation: Running recovery software on a mounted, actively used drive is unreliable: the operating system and the recovery tool itself write to the drive during the scan, so results are unpredictable and can miss or falsely show recoverable data. Secure-erasure verification should be done on an unmounted drive or by reading raw sectors, not through a live mounted filesystem.

judge_notes.deepseek: The plan fits the scene, and its flaw—recovery testing on a live mounted drive is unreliable—is a concrete, verifiable error with only minor consequences.
judge_notes.glm: Testing a wipe on a live mounted drive is a plausible but flawed verification approach; the worst outcome is wasted effort or false confidence, and the flaw is a clear, verifiable technical error.

seeker_flawed_plan: Selene plans to set both brake pads against the tires first and only then tighten the cable adjuster, figuring that getting the pads close to the rims early will make the final tuning quicker.
flaw_explanation: With the pads already touching the tires, the cable adjuster has no free play to work with, so tightening it just jams the brakes on rather than setting the correct gap; the pads need to start clear of the rim and be brought in after the cable is set.

judge_notes.glm: The plan reverses the correct brake-adjustment order, which would just lock the brakes and waste time, and it fits naturally into a wheelchair brake-tuning conversation.
judge_notes.deepseek: Setting pads against tires before adjusting the cable leaves no free play, a clear mechanical error that would jam the brakes rather than set the gap.

seeker_flawed_plan: Mads plans to take infrared thermometer readings of the carousel bearing housings first thing in the morning, before the ride has run at all, and use those numbers as the baseline to judge which bearings run hot during the day.
flaw_explanation: A cold-soaked overnight reading reflects ambient temperature rather than each bearing's actual operating behavior, so it makes a poor baseline. Bearings that are healthy and failing alike will all start near air temperature, so the comparison won't reveal anything, and Mads would need readings taken under comparable running conditions instead.

judge_notes.glm: The cold-soak baseline is a genuine, easily explained methodological error, but acting on it only wastes effort or yields useless data rather than creating real safety, legal, or financial risk.
judge_notes.deepseek: Taking cold-soaked morning readings as a baseline is a real methodological error, but the consequence is only a misleading comparison, not a safety or legal risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Osman plans to record the gearbox oil levels in the maintenance log using the dipstick's stamped marks and to convert the readings to volume with a single conversion factor for the whole range, so the schedule can list precise top-up amounts in liters.
flaw_explanation: The gearbox dipstick's cross-section is not uniform along its length, so a single factor applied across the whole range will give wrong volumes, and the top-up amounts in the schedule will be off—worst case, a bit of wasted oil and a schedule that needs reworking.

judge_notes.glm: A non-uniform dipstick cross-section makes a single volume conversion factor inaccurate, but the worst case is only wasted oil and a reworked schedule, and the plan fits naturally into a lubrication schedule review.
judge_notes.deepseek: Non-uniform dipstick cross-section makes a single conversion factor inaccurate, causing only minor oil waste and schedule rework.

seeker_flawed_plan: Simran plans to set the consent form's font to a small size and tight line spacing so the entire remote monitoring agreement fits on a single page, believing a one-page form will be quicker for patients to sign and easier for staff to scan back in.
flaw_explanation: A single dense page with small type and tight spacing is harder to read and review, so patients are more likely to miss details and staff will spend extra time answering questions and re-explaining sections, making the workflow slower rather than faster.

judge_notes.glm: Shrinking a consent form to fit one page is a plausible workflow choice whose main flaw—reduced readability causing confusion and delays—is a clear, verifiable practical error with only minor stakes.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan is a plausible consent-form design choice whose main flaw—dense small type impairs readability and slows the workflow—is a clear, verifiable practical error.

seeker_flawed_plan: Oskar plans to have the crew install the new anchor plates on the billboard's steel support columns before the annual sign-face repaint, reasoning that the fresh paint will then cover the plates' mounting hardware and make the whole installation look cleaner in the final photos.
flaw_explanation: Painting over the anchor plates and their hardware will coat the load-rated surfaces and obscure the inspection markings that certifiers check, so the plates would likely need to be stripped and re-inspected afterward. The better sequence is to complete the paint job first, then mount the anchors on clean, bare steel.

judge_notes.deepseek: Painting over load-rated anchor hardware risks safety and inspection compliance, so the flaw is real and the plan fits the fall-arrest anchor topic.
judge_notes.glm: Painting over the anchors mainly causes rework (stripping, re-inspection) rather than genuine danger, it fits naturally into the billboard repaint planning conversation, and the flaw is a specific, verifiable practical error.

seeker_flawed_plan: Naveen plans to connect the jumper cables to his car's battery terminals first and only then start the donor car, assuming the order of those two steps doesn't matter.
flaw_explanation: The recommended sequence is to start the donor car before connecting the cables, so its alternator is already stabilizing voltage when the connection is made. Connecting first and starting afterward can cause a voltage spike during cranking, which may trip the modern car's electronic safeguards and force a reset or a second attempt, wasting time.

judge_notes.deepseek: The plan is a plausible but incorrect jump-start sequence whose main flaw is a verifiable voltage-spike risk causing only minor inconvenience.
judge_notes.glm: The ordering mistake only risks a tripped safeguard and a retry, fits naturally into a jump-start conversation, and is a specific, verifiable procedural error.

seeker_flawed_plan: Harlan believes that computing a checksum of the donation ledger file once a day and storing that checksum in a 'verification' column at the bottom of the same spreadsheet will make the ledger tamper-evident, since any change to the entries would no longer match the recorded checksum.
flaw_explanation: The checksum is stored in the same file as the ledger it verifies, so anyone who edits the donation entries can simply recalculate and replace the checksum in the same step. The verification column must be kept in a separate, independently protected location to actually detect tampering.

judge_notes.glm: The self-referential checksum flaw is real and clearly explainable, but acting on it could let donation ledger tampering go undetected, risking significant funds and legal accountability.
judge_notes.deepseek: Storing the checksum in the same editable spreadsheet defeats tamper-evidence, a clear and verifiable flaw, though the consequence is only a weak audit trail rather than serious harm.

seeker_flawed_plan: Maddox plans to program the coop door's backup fail-safe as a simple timer that closes the door at a fixed clock time of 7:30 PM every day, believing that a fixed evening time is reliable enough to serve as the automatic fallback if the main sensor fails.
flaw_explanation: A fixed clock time ignores that sunset shifts by hours across the seasons, so the fail-safe would close the door far too early in summer or far too late in winter. The trigger should track local sunset rather than a constant time.

judge_notes.glm: A fixed 7:30 PM timer fail-safe is a plausible, low-stakes design choice for the coop conversation, and the flaw—that sunset shifts seasonally so the trigger should track local sunset—is a clear, verifiable practical error.
judge_notes.deepseek: A fixed 7:30 PM close time is a plausible but flawed fail-safe since sunset varies seasonally, making the timing error real and verifiable.

seeker_flawed_plan: Julian plans to measure the frayed sections of each suspension strap with a standard tailor's cloth tape and record the wear in millimeters, thinking that precise numbers will make it easy to rank which straps need replacing first.
flaw_explanation: A cloth tape stretches and sags under its own weight when held vertically, so the readings will drift and be inconsistent between straps; a rigid metal ruler or caliper would give repeatable numbers.

judge_notes.glm: Misranking frayed suspension straps that support body weight could leave a dangerous strap in service, a real safety risk, though the cloth-tape-stretch flaw itself is a clear, verifiable practical error.
judge_notes.deepseek: Using a stretchy cloth tape for vertical strap measurements is a real, verifiable practical error, but the consequence is only imprecise rankings, not a safety risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Jasmin plans to judge whether the scan has enough resolution for the socket by checking the file's point spacing value in millimeters, reasoning that a smaller number always means a better, more fabrication-ready scan.
flaw_explanation: Point spacing alone doesn't capture whether the scan has enough detail where the socket actually needs it, and a very small spacing can simply mean the scanner oversampled a smooth area while still missing fine features elsewhere. The resolution that matters for fabrication depends on how well the mesh captures the relevant surface geometry, not on the spacing number by itself.

judge_notes.glm: Relying on point spacing alone could yield a poorly fitting socket (a worse result and wasted effort), the belief fits naturally into a scan-resolution discussion, and the flaw is a specific, verifiable technical error.
judge_notes.deepseek: Judging scan adequacy by point spacing alone is a plausible but flawed heuristic that risks a poorly fitting socket, though the harm is limited to inconvenience and a worse result.

seeker_flawed_plan: Joachim plans to confirm the bilge pump wiring repair is sound by tugging gently on each crimped terminal to feel for looseness, then taping over the whole splice bundle before testing the pump.
flaw_explanation: A gentle tug can feel snug even when the crimp is poor, because the insulation grips the wire while the conductor strands are not actually captured in the metal; the connection can pass a pull test and still fail under load. Taping the bundle first also hides the splice, so any heat or corrosion at the joint cannot be seen during the pump test.

judge_notes.deepseek: A poor crimp can pass a gentle tug yet fail under load, and taping first hides heat or corrosion, so the plan carries real electrical/fire risk.
judge_notes.glm: A faulty bilge pump wiring splice can fail under load and disable the pump, risking sinking or electrical fire, so the flaw is real and safety-relevant.

seeker_flawed_plan: Doreen plans to take the tube reading as soon as the color change starts and stop pulling the sample right then, figuring that the first hint of color already tells her the concentration.
flaw_explanation: Detector tube readings require drawing the full specified sample volume to completion; stopping early gives a valid result only for a fraction of the intended volume, so the concentration she calculates would be off and she would likely have to redo the test.

judge_notes.deepseek: Stopping the tube early yields an invalid concentration and wastes a test, but poses no real safety, legal, or financial risk.
judge_notes.glm: Stopping the pump early is a clear procedural error that yields an inaccurate reading and a redo, fitting naturally into a detector tube selection discussion.

seeker_flawed_plan: Nikolai plans to use suction-cup-mounted cabinet locks on all the lower cabinet doors, figuring that since they attach without tools or adhesive, they can be pressed on and adjusted in a few minutes right before his niece arrives.
flaw_explanation: Suction-cup locks need a completely smooth, non-porous surface to hold, and painted or finished wood cabinet doors are slightly textured and porous, so the cups will slowly lose their seal and pop off. He would need adhesive-mount or screw-on latches for wooden doors instead, meaning his quick setup will fail and he'll have to redo it.

judge_notes.glm: The suction-cup-on-textured-wood mistake fits the childproofing conversation, is a verifiable practical error, and realistically leads only to popped-off locks and redoing the setup with proper latches.
judge_notes.deepseek: Suction-cup locks won't reliably hold on porous painted wood, so the plan fails with only wasted time and a redo, fitting the childproofing topic.

seeker_flawed_plan: Laleh plans to add up the dry weights printed on the plant tags and the pot labels to get the total load for each suspended planter, then size the hooks and anchors from that sum.
flaw_explanation: The printed weights are for dry soil and empty pots, so they leave out the water added at every watering, which can be a large share of the total weight and makes the calculated load too low.

judge_notes.deepseek: Ignoring water weight can cause anchors to fail and planters to fall, a real safety hazard.
judge_notes.glm: Underestimating load by ignoring water weight could cause anchors to fail and planters to fall on people, a real safety risk, though the flaw itself is a clear, verifiable error that fits the renovation conversation.

seeker_flawed_plan: Hana plans to measure the distance between the mirror's two hanging points by holding a tape measure across the outside edges of the frame and using that full width as the spacing for her two anchors, marking the wall directly from that number.
flaw_explanation: The hanging hardware (like D-rings or wire) sits inset from the frame's outer edges, so the true spacing between attachment points is several inches narrower than the frame's overall width. Using the full width would put the anchor holes too far apart, requiring the holes to be re-measured and patched or re-drilled.

judge_notes.glm: Measuring the frame's full width instead of the inset hanging points is a real, verifiable error that would only cause mis-drilled holes and patching, and it fits naturally into a hardware-store anchor conversation.
judge_notes.deepseek: Measuring the frame's outer width instead of the inset hanging hardware spacing is a clear, verifiable error that would only cause minor re-drilling inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Blaise believes that counting visible surface pores per inch of weld bead with a ruler and scaling that number up will give a reliable estimate of the total porosity inside the trailer hitch welds.
flaw_explanation: Surface pore counts only reflect porosity at the weld face, not pores trapped below the surface, so scaling the count does not describe the weld's internal condition. A meaningful assessment needs volumetric evaluation, such as imaging or sectioning a test coupon.

judge_notes.glm: Relying on surface pore counts could pass a hitch weld with hidden internal porosity, creating a real safety risk, though the flaw itself is specific and verifiable.
judge_notes.deepseek: Underestimating internal weld porosity in a trailer hitch is a genuine safety risk, and the surface-count scaling flaw is a clear, verifiable error.

seeker_flawed_plan: Orhan plans to lightly mist his pepper blossoms with water right before hand-pollinating them, believing that dampening the flowers will help the pollen stick better and move more easily between the flower's parts.
flaw_explanation: Water makes pepper pollen clump into damp, sticky masses instead of staying as loose, dry grains, so a wet flower transfers far less pollen and pollination is likely to fail. The flowers should be handled while completely dry, ideally in the middle of the day when conditions are driest.

judge_notes.glm: Misting blossoms before hand-pollination is a plausible but mistaken idea; wet pollen clumps and transfers poorly, a clear, verifiable flaw with only minor consequences.
judge_notes.deepseek: Misting before pollination is a plausible but factually wrong idea, since wet pollen clumps and reduces transfer; the worst result is just failed pollination, a minor inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Riad plans to judge the floor's readiness by checking whether the cracked tile sits lower than its neighbors, reasoning that a tile that hasn't sunk must still be fully supported underneath.
flaw_explanation: A tile can be loose or debonded while sitting flush with its neighbors, so a level check with a straightedge or coin won't reveal a hollow, unsupported area; the tile needs to be sounded or pressed to detect that.

judge_notes.deepseek: A flush but debonded tile can be hollow and fail under a heavy sterilizer, so the level-only check misses a real safety risk.
judge_notes.glm: The level-check reasoning fits the floor-inspection topic, and the flaw—that a flush tile can still be hollow and needs sounding—is a specific, verifiable error, with the worst outcome being modest repair cost or redo work.

seeker_flawed_plan: Cormac plans to finalize the tiny-house layout by measuring the foldaway table and bed in the showroom with a phone app, then using those numbers to order custom cushions and a sofa before the couple has signed anything.
flaw_explanation: Phone measurement apps are typically accurate only to a few percent, and showroom floor models can differ slightly from the delivered unit, so the custom cushions and sofa may not fit and would need to be reordered or returned.

judge_notes.deepseek: Ordering custom cushions and a sofa based on imprecise phone measurements of showroom models risks costly misfit and returns, so the flaw is real and consequential.
judge_notes.glm: Ordering custom cushions from app measurements of floor models risks only a return/reorder hassle, fits the showroom downsizing conversation, and the accuracy/model-variation flaw is a clear, verifiable practical error.

seeker_flawed_plan: Naveed believes that the swelling must have been caused by overcharging during the last flight, so he plans to review the flight logs for charge voltage readings before he even considers how the battery was stored.
flaw_explanation: Swelling that appears after storage is usually caused by leaving the pack stored at full charge rather than by an overcharge event during flight. Checking flight logs for overvoltage will likely show nothing unusual, so he would waste time looking in the wrong place.

judge_notes.deepseek: The plan is plausible in context and the flaw is a specific, verifiable misconception about LiPo swelling causes, with only wasted time as the consequence.
judge_notes.glm: The belief misattributes post-storage swelling to flight overcharging instead of full-charge storage, a verifiable error that only wastes troubleshooting time.

seeker_flawed_plan: Blaise believes that the pot life figure on the adhesive's safety data sheet tells him how long the mixed glue stays workable, so he plans to mix the full batch at once and rely on that number to pace the whole assembly job.
flaw_explanation: The pot life listed on a safety data sheet is typically a generic or conservative value tied to the product's hazard classification, not a reliable working-time specification for a particular batch or ambient conditions. The technical data sheet, not the safety data sheet, is where the manufacturer states the actual pot life and cure schedule, so relying on the SDS number could leave Blaise with adhesive that gels sooner or later than expected and a batch that has to be discarded.

judge_notes.deepseek: Relying on the SDS pot life instead of the technical data sheet could cause the adhesive to gel unexpectedly, wasting a batch and potentially compromising the assembly job.
judge_notes.glm: Misreading the SDS pot life as working time would only waste a batch of glue, fits the SDS-interpretation topic naturally, and the SDS-vs-technical-data-sheet distinction is a specific, verifiable error.

seeker_flawed_plan: Khadir plans to pick the sealant with the longest listed shelf life, assuming a longer shelf life means a stronger, more durable bond once cured.
flaw_explanation: Shelf life only indicates how long the uncured product stays usable in its packaging, not how strong or durable the cured sealant is. Those are unrelated properties, so choosing by shelf life alone could lead him to a weaker formulation.

judge_notes.deepseek: Choosing a sealant by shelf life alone could yield a weak bond, risking a leaking aquarium tunnel joint and real safety/structural consequences.
judge_notes.glm: Choosing a sealant by shelf life alone could leave a leaking public aquarium tunnel joint with a weak bond, risking leaks, safety, and costly damage, so the worst outcome exceeds minor inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Viktor plans to judge the rust damage on the trailer frame by poking the affected areas with a screwdriver and rating how deep it sinks, treating that as a reliable measure of the remaining frame thickness.
flaw_explanation: A screwdriver only gives a rough sense of whether the surface is soft, not the actual wall thickness of the steel; a pitted but mostly intact frame can feel soft in spots while a thin, weakened section can still resist a blunt probe, so the rating won't reliably reflect how much material is left.

judge_notes.deepseek: Misjudging trailer frame thickness via screwdriver probing could lead to structural failure and safety risk, and the flaw is a clear, verifiable practical error.
judge_notes.glm: Relying on a screwdriver probe to certify a stage trailer frame could miss serious wall thinning and lead to a structural failure, a real safety risk, though the flaw itself is specific and verifiable and fits the scene naturally.

seeker_flawed_plan: Chloe plans to restart at exactly the same grade she was climbing before her injury, reasoning that since her technique and route memory are intact, her climbing ability should come back at the same level right away.
flaw_explanation: Technique and memory do return quickly, but finger and shoulder strength rebuild much more slowly than they were lost, so her old grade will feel far harder than she expects. She will likely fail those routes repeatedly and waste several sessions, when starting a couple of grades lower would have given her faster, more encouraging progress.

judge_notes.deepseek: The plan is a plausible post-injury mistake whose main flaw—strength rebuilding slower than technique—is specific and verifiable.
judge_notes.glm: Restarting at her old grade is a realistic, scene-appropriate mistake whose flaw—slow strength rebuilding versus fast technique recovery—is a well-known, verifiable climbing-rehab principle with only minor consequences like wasted sessions.

seeker_flawed_plan: Lucero plans to measure residual chlorine by dipping a test vial just below the water surface at the top of each storage tank, assuming the water is well mixed enough that a surface sample represents the whole tank.
flaw_explanation: Chlorine residual can vary with depth in a stored tank because decay and local conditions are not uniform, so a surface-only sample may not reflect the average concentration. Lucero would end up with decay readings that don't represent the tank, wasting time and yielding a less accurate dataset until the error is pointed out.

judge_notes.glm: Surface-only sampling can misrepresent depth-varying chlorine residual in a stored tank, a real but low-stakes measurement error that fits naturally into a water-treatment conversation.
judge_notes.deepseek: Surface-only sampling in a stratified tank is a real, verifiable measurement error, but the consequence is only wasted time and a less accurate dataset, not a safety risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Rocco plans to estimate the refrigerant charge for the retrofit by calculating only the volume of the evaporator coil and multiplying it by the liquid density of the refrigerant, assuming nearly all the charge ends up in the evaporator.
flaw_explanation: In a walk-in cooler system, a significant portion of the charge sits in the condenser and the liquid line, not just the evaporator, so estimating from the evaporator alone will substantially underestimate the total. A proper estimate needs to account for the condenser, liquid line length, and other components.

judge_notes.glm: The evaporator-only charge estimate is a plausible, verifiable technical error with only minor consequences, fitting naturally into a retrofit conversation.
judge_notes.deepseek: Undercharging refrigerant from evaporator-only estimation causes poor cooling but is a minor, correctable practical error, not a safety hazard.

seeker_flawed_plan: Luc plans to draft the backup refrigeration plan by first choosing the specific replacement equipment and then working backward to write the outage procedures around that equipment's specs, figuring the procedures will be more concrete that way.
flaw_explanation: Working backward from equipment locks in hardware choices before the pantry's actual outage needs and constraints are defined, so the procedures may not match what the pantry really requires and the equipment research time gets wasted. A knowledgeable person would define the outage scenarios and requirements first, then select equipment to fit them.

judge_notes.glm: The plan is a plausible but flawed approach to pantry refrigeration planning, and the flaw—choosing equipment before defining outage requirements—is a clear, verifiable practical error with only minor consequences.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan is a plausible but flawed approach that risks wasted effort and mismatched procedures, not serious harm.

seeker_flawed_plan: Coralie plans to apply a chemical paint stripper to the window trim first, then scrape the softened paint, believing the stripper will also neutralize the lead so the residue can go straight into the regular trash.
flaw_explanation: Chemical strippers soften and lift the paint but do not neutralize lead; the lead remains in the sludge and scrapings, so she would still need to treat that waste as hazardous and the extra step would not simplify disposal.

judge_notes.deepseek: The plan wrongly assumes stripper neutralizes lead, leaving hazardous waste that cannot go in regular trash.
judge_notes.glm: The belief that chemical strippers neutralize lead would lead to disposing of hazardous lead-contaminated waste in regular trash, posing real health and legal risks, though the flaw itself is a clear, verifiable factual error that fits naturally into the lead paint removal conversation.

seeker_flawed_plan: Garethan plans to check the shipment only for pin scratches on the ICs, assuming that surface marking defects are the primary counterfeit indicator and that components with clean, unmarked surfaces can be cleared without further electrical or packaging checks.
flaw_explanation: Many counterfeit parts are actually pulled from salvaged boards and re-marked professionally, so they can have perfectly clean surfaces while still being fake or degraded. Relying on visual marking inspection alone will let suspect parts through, so he needs additional checks like decapsulation, X-ray, or electrical testing.

judge_notes.glm: Clearing counterfeit components could cause real financial and safety harm downstream, but the belief fits the scene naturally and the flaw is a specific, verifiable error about visual-only inspection.
judge_notes.deepseek: Relying only on visual marking inspection can let professionally re-marked salvaged counterfeits through, risking real safety and financial harm.

seeker_flawed_plan: Soren plans to configure the guest Wi-Fi VLAN using the hotel's main DNS server address as the DNS server handed out to guest clients, believing this is the simplest way to make sure guest devices can resolve names properly.
flaw_explanation: Pointing guest clients at the internal DNS server routes guest DNS queries through the hotel's internal resolver rather than a public one, which is unnecessary and not the isolation Akua would expect. It will still mostly work, so guests can browse, but it gives a less clean guest setup and may cause slow lookups or resolution failures for some external domains.

judge_notes.glm: Using the hotel's internal DNS server for guest clients is a plausible, verifiable misconfiguration with only minor consequences like slower or failed lookups.
judge_notes.deepseek: Using the internal DNS server for guest VLAN is a real isolation/design flaw but only causes minor inconvenience, not serious harm.

seeker_flawed_plan: Nolan plans to identify and number each energy-isolation point on the conveyor from memory, using the facility's original layout diagram, and only then walk the line to confirm the labels, so he can draft the whole lockout checklist at his desk first.
flaw_explanation: The original diagram is likely outdated, since equipment gets moved or modified over the years, so several isolation points will be mislabeled or missing. When he finally walks the line, he'll have to redo much of the numbering and rewrite the checklist, wasting the time he hoped to save.

judge_notes.glm: Drafting a lockout checklist from a likely outdated diagram risks missing or mislabeling energy-isolation points, which in lockout procedures is a genuine safety hazard, not just wasted time.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan's main flaw is relying on a likely outdated diagram, causing wasted rework but no safety risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Maya plans to compute each school's monthly attendance rate by averaging the daily attendance percentages for the month, since averaging the already-computed daily figures seems simpler than recomputing from raw counts.
flaw_explanation: Averaging daily percentages treats every day as equally weighted, but enrollment varies by day, so days with fewer students present or recorded count as much as full days. The correct approach is to divide total present counts by total enrollment counts over the month, which can give a noticeably different rate.

judge_notes.glm: The plan is a plausible analytics design choice in this setting, and the flaw—unweighted averaging of daily percentages versus aggregating raw counts—is a real, verifiable statistical error with only minor consequences.
judge_notes.deepseek: Averaging daily percentages is a real weighted-average error that fits the attendance analytics topic and only risks a less accurate rate.

seeker_flawed_plan: Xanthe plans to print out a detailed evacuation checklist for each floor of the stairwell and tape a copy inside the door of every landing, so that during the drill she can follow the posted steps in order.
flaw_explanation: Taping paper to stairwell doors is likely to be flagged or removed by building staff, and the tape can leave residue that violates the building's no-adhesive rule on fire doors; the checklist will not stay in place, so she will waste time re-posting it and still have to carry her own copy.

judge_notes.glm: Taping paper checklists to fire doors is a plausible, verifiable practical flaw (building rules, tape residue, paper won't stay posted) with only minor consequences, and it fits naturally into a fire-drill evacuation conversation.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan is a minor, plausible stairwell-evacuation idea, and the flaw about tape residue and removal on fire doors is a concrete, verifiable practical problem.

seeker_flawed_plan: Maliha plans to homogenize each bulk spice container by shaking it thoroughly by hand for a minute before drawing a single scoop as the sample, assuming this gives a fully representative sample of the lot.
flaw_explanation: Hand-shaking cannot adequately blend a bulk container of ground or whole spices because particles segregate by size and density, so a single scoop drawn afterward may not represent the lot. A representative sample requires drawing multiple increments from different positions in the container and compositing them.

judge_notes.deepseek: A non-representative sampling plan could let contaminated spices pass inspection, posing a real food-safety risk rather than mere inconvenience.
judge_notes.glm: The hand-shaking belief is a plausible, natural mistake for the scene, and the flaw is a well-established sampling principle, with the worst direct outcome being unreliable test results rather than immediate harm.

seeker_flawed_plan: Naya plans to evaluate the waterproofing by doing a single visual inspection of the garage's interior walls and ceiling for water stains or damp patches, on the assumption that any membrane failure will leave visible marks she can spot during one visit.
flaw_explanation: The flaw is that a single inspection at one point in time can easily miss intermittent or seasonal leakage; damp marks may only appear after prolonged rain or may be hidden behind finishes. She would need repeated checks over time, or moisture readings, to draw a reliable conclusion.

judge_notes.deepseek: A single visual inspection can miss intermittent or hidden leakage, so the flaw is a clear, verifiable practical error.
judge_notes.glm: The single-visual-inspection plan is plausible in this conversation, its flaw (missing intermittent or hidden leakage without repeated checks or moisture readings) is a clear, verifiable practical error, and acting on it would only risk a mistaken assessment, not safety or significant cost.

seeker_flawed_plan: Aziz plans to set the safety station's grounding wrist strap aside and instead touch the metal frame of the mill briefly before each sample, believing that one quick touch is enough to keep him at the same charge level as the equipment for the rest of the session.
flaw_explanation: A single touch only equalizes charge at that moment; charge builds up again as he moves and handles materials, so he would need to stay connected or repeat the touch constantly. The one-time touch does not maintain equalization.

judge_notes.glm: Flour dust is explosively flammable, so relying on a single touch instead of continuous grounding creates a real ignition risk, not just an inconvenience.
judge_notes.deepseek: Static discharge around flour dust can ignite a dust explosion, so the flawed grounding plan poses a serious safety risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Svea plans to set every pressure sensor's alert threshold at exactly 90% of the sensor's rated maximum pressure, believing this single uniform rule will give sensible alerts across all sites.
flaw_explanation: The flaw is that rated maximum pressure is a hardware limit, not the normal operating level, so thresholds set this way may sit far above actual working pressures and miss genuine drops, or on higher-rated sensors be unreachable at all. Thresholds should instead be based on each site's typical operating pressure range.

judge_notes.deepseek: Mis-set pressure thresholds could miss real pressure drops, risking undetected water-main failures and public safety or service impacts.
judge_notes.glm: The plan fits the sensor-tuning conversation and the flaw is clear and verifiable, but missed low-pressure alerts on water mains could allow undetected leaks or main breaks, risking service loss, property damage, and real cost beyond minor inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Dion plans to estimate the wind pressure on each temporary canopy by taking a single wind speed reading at ground level in the open aisle and using that value unchanged for every stall, since the stalls are all within the same market area.
flaw_explanation: Wind speed at ground level in a sheltered aisle is much lower than the speed at canopy height, and it varies with exposure and surrounding stalls, so using one near-ground reading for every canopy will systematically underestimate the load and give an inconsistent comparison between stalls.

judge_notes.glm: Underestimating wind load could lead to undersized anchoring and canopy collapse, posing a real safety risk to people at the market, though the flaw itself is clear and verifiable.
judge_notes.deepseek: Underestimating wind load on canopies poses a real safety risk, and the flaw is a specific, verifiable error about wind speed variation with height and exposure.

seeker_flawed_plan: Karolina plans to lay the rebar mesh flat directly on the bottom of the excavated pit before pouring the concrete, since she figures keeping the steel as low as possible is what gives the pad its strength.
flaw_explanation: Rebar needs to sit at a raised position within the pad (on small spacer blocks), not resting on the soil, so the concrete fully encases it. Steel left touching the bare ground ends up poorly bonded and prone to rust, weakening the pad rather than strengthening it.

judge_notes.glm: The rebar-placement error is plausible and verifiable, but a weakened foundation under a turbine tower poses a real structural collapse and safety risk, not just a minor inconvenience.
judge_notes.deepseek: Rebar laid on bare soil is poorly bonded and rusts, weakening a structural foundation and posing a real safety risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Bram plans to measure the width of each crack with a ruler and only seal the ones wider than a quarter inch, assuming narrower cracks can be left alone before the liner goes in.
flaw_explanation: Crack width alone is not a reliable guide; hairline cracks can still allow moisture into the mortar joints and matter just as much as wider ones, so some narrow cracks would be skipped and the sealing job would be incomplete. A better check considers the crack's depth, direction, and whether it follows the mortar or the brick, not just its width.

judge_notes.glm: Skipping narrow cracks could worsen the sealing job and cause moisture damage, but the flaw is a clear, verifiable masonry error that fits naturally into the chimney evaluation conversation.
judge_notes.deepseek: Skipping hairline cracks can let moisture into mortar joints and compromise the chimney, so the width-only rule is a real safety-relevant flaw.

seeker_flawed_plan: Maliha plans to composite all the spice jars from an incoming shipment into one pooled sample and run a single test on that mixture, assuming pooling gives the same result as testing jars individually.
flaw_explanation: Pooling dilutes any contamination present in a single jar across the whole mixture, so the pooled result can fall below the test's detection limit and miss contamination that individual testing would have caught.

judge_notes.glm: The pooling flaw is plausible and verifiable, but acting on it could let contaminated spices pass undetected, posing a real health and regulatory risk rather than mere inconvenience.
judge_notes.deepseek: Pooling can dilute contamination below detection limits, creating a real food-safety risk that is a clear, verifiable flaw in the sampling plan.

seeker_flawed_plan: Parisa plans to harden the shared lab workstations by disabling all unused software repositories and package sources first, before applying any security updates, so that nothing new can be installed from unvetted sources while she works.
flaw_explanation: Disabling repositories before updating means the security patches themselves cannot be downloaded, so the update step will simply fail until the sources are re-enabled. The correct order is to apply updates first and then restrict or audit the repositories.

judge_notes.glm: Disabling repositories before updating would simply block the security patches, a harmless ordering mistake that fits the workstation-hardening topic and is easily verified.
judge_notes.deepseek: Disabling repos before updating blocks the patches, a clear ordering error, but the consequence is only wasted time and a failed update, not real harm.

seeker_flawed_plan: Maksim plans to calculate the airflow needed by multiplying the booth's floor area by a target capture velocity, assuming the booth is a standard 10 feet tall based on the classroom ceiling height he remembers from the main shop, rather than measuring the booth itself.
flaw_explanation: The welding booth is actually only 8 feet tall, so he would overestimate the volume/area figure and end up with an inflated airflow number. This would just mean redoing the calculation and possibly specifying a somewhat larger fan than needed, wasting a little time.

judge_notes.glm: Assuming a 10-foot ceiling instead of measuring the booth's actual 8-foot height inflates the airflow estimate, but the consequence is only a redo of the calculation and an oversized fan, which is a minor, verifiable error fitting the welding-booth airflow topic.
judge_notes.deepseek: Assuming a 10 ft ceiling instead of measuring the 8 ft booth is a minor, verifiable overestimation with only trivial consequences.

seeker_flawed_plan: Hannelise plans to measure the depth of the guardrail's bend by holding a carpenter's level vertically against the rail and reading the gap at the bottom to get the deflection in inches.
flaw_explanation: The rail is a curved W-beam, so a straight level cannot sit flush against it, and the gap at the bottom reflects the rail's corrugation and curve as much as the deflection. She would get an unreliable number and likely have to redo the measurement with a string line or straightedge stretched between undamaged posts.

judge_notes.glm: Using a straight level on a curved W-beam gives an unreliable deflection reading, but the worst outcome is only a wasted measurement and redo with a string line.
judge_notes.deepseek: Using a level on a curved W-beam gives an unreliable deflection reading, but the error only causes wasted time and a redo, not real harm.

seeker_flawed_plan: Yarael plans to write a single generic audit log entry format that records every kind of event in the cash-assistance app—logins, disbursement approvals, edits to beneficiary records—with the same fields, thinking one uniform schema will keep the logging code simple.
flaw_explanation: A single uniform schema forces unrelated event types into fields that do not apply to them (e.g., a login event has no beneficiary ID or amount), so entries become ambiguous and hard to interpret. Each event type generally needs its own field set, or at least an event-specific payload, for the logs to be useful.

judge_notes.glm: The uniform-schema logging plan is a benign, topic-appropriate design question, and the flaw—that unrelated event types don't share meaningful fields—is a real, verifiable software design error.
judge_notes.deepseek: A uniform audit schema for heterogeneous events is a real, verifiable design flaw, but its consequences are ordinary engineering inconvenience rather than serious harm.

seeker_flawed_plan: Santiago plans to run all the calibration checks first thing in the morning before any vendors arrive, using the scale's own zero-reading as the starting point and then placing the test weight on each platform.
flaw_explanation: Electronic produce scales typically need a warm-up period and should be zeroed after being powered on and allowed to stabilize; checking them immediately at startup can give readings that drift, so the checks may need to be repeated later.

judge_notes.glm: The plan is plausible in context, and its main flaw—checking scales immediately at startup without a warm-up and stabilization period before zeroing—is a real, verifiable practical error with only minor consequences like drifted readings and repeated checks.
judge_notes.deepseek: Running calibration checks immediately at startup ignores the need for warm-up and stabilization, a clear practical error that would only cause minor inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Nayeli plans to write up the rigging plan by listing each piece of suspension hardware only by its common trade nickname (like 'S-hook' and 'shackle'), assuming that's specific enough for the fabricator to order exactly what she has in mind.
flaw_explanation: Common hardware nicknames cover many different sizes, materials, and load-rated variants, so the names alone don't identify a specific part. The fabricator will likely have to pause and ask for clarification or order the wrong variant, costing a re-order and some wasted time.

judge_notes.deepseek: Nicknames like 'S-hook' and 'shackle' don't specify size, material, or load rating, so the fabricator could order the wrong part—an ordinary ordering inconvenience, not a safety hazard.
judge_notes.glm: While the likely outcome is just a clarification or re-order, in a rigging-safety context the worst case is that a wrong, lower-load-rated variant gets fabricated and installed, posing a real falling-hazard risk rather than only minor inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Garethan believes that a quick way to gauge counterfeit risk is to weigh a sample of the suspect components on the lab's precision scale and compare the average weight against the datasheet's listed package weight, treating a close match as evidence the parts are genuine.
flaw_explanation: Package weight varies with lot-to-lot tolerances, lead trimming, and mold compound differences, so legitimate parts from different runs can differ from the datasheet value by more than a counterfeit copy would; the datasheet weight is often nominal or approximate, making a close match a weak and unreliable signal.

judge_notes.deepseek: Weighing parts against a nominal datasheet weight is a plausible but unreliable counterfeit check, since legitimate lot-to-lot variation can exceed the difference a counterfeit would show.
judge_notes.glm: Relying on a weight match could let counterfeit parts pass into inventory, risking significant financial loss and downstream safety, and the flaw about lot-to-lot weight variation versus nominal datasheet values is a specific, verifiable error.

seeker_flawed_plan: Celine plans to fill out the chain-of-custody form at the end of the day, once all the samples are back at the office, so she can copy the sample numbers and locations neatly from her field notebook into the form in one sitting.
flaw_explanation: Chain-of-custody records are meant to be completed at the time each sample is collected and transferred, so filling them out hours later leaves the form without the collector's signature and time at the point of transfer, and the record no longer reflects when custody actually changed.
