judge_notes.glm: Relying on a diagram-and-visual match to declare wiring safe could mask a real installation error, creating genuine electrical/fire risk rather than mere wasted time, though the flaw itself is clear and verifiable.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan's flaw is real and specific, but relying on a visual/diagram match to confirm safe wiring could leave a genuine electrical hazard undetected, so the outcome is not merely minor inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Lars plans to time the rinse cycle with a stopwatch and compare it against the machine's spec sheet, reasoning that a rinse phase running longer than rated would explain why the breaker trips only then.
flaw_explanation: The spec sheet's rinse time is the programmed duration, not the actual powered run time, so a stopwatch reading taken by ear or by watching the spray will not match it even on a healthy machine and will send him chasing a normal difference.

judge_notes.glm: Timing the rinse against the spec sheet is a safe diagnostic step, fits the dishwasher-tripping conversation, and the flaw that programmed duration differs from actual powered run time is a specific, verifiable error.
judge_notes.deepseek: Timing the rinse with a stopwatch and comparing to the spec sheet is a plausible but flawed diagnostic, since spec rinse time is programmed duration rather than actual powered run time, causing a normal mismatch.

seeker_flawed_plan: Phaedra plans to drill the vent holes into each hollow form only after it has fully dried, reasoning that the clay will be stiff enough then to hold a clean hole without sagging or burring.
flaw_explanation: Drilling fully dry clay is brittle and prone to chipping or cracking around the hole, and any trapped moisture already sealed inside during drying has no escape route; the hole needs to be formed while the clay is still workable, before the piece dries.

judge_notes.glm: Drilling bone-dry clay risks chipping and cracking, and vent holes should be made while the clay is still workable, so the flaw is real, specific, and fits the topic with only minor consequences.
judge_notes.deepseek: Drilling after full drying risks chipping and traps moisture, so the vent should be formed while the clay is still workable.

seeker_flawed_plan: Sorayael plans to compare the ventilation of each crate by holding a strip of lightweight paper at the crate's exterior face and judging airflow by how strongly the strip flutters, then ranking the crates from most to least ventilated.
flaw_explanation: A fluttering strip at the exterior face mainly registers air movement outside the crate, such as drafts in the garage or the person's own motion, not the exchange of air through the crate's openings, so the rankings can reflect the surrounding room rather than the crate's ventilation. A more reliable check would measure airflow at the openings themselves or use a smoke or tracer test to see how readily air moves through the interior.

judge_notes.glm: The paper-strip test is a plausible but flawed ventilation check that fits the scene, and the exterior-face measurement error is a specific, verifiable practical flaw with only minor consequences.
judge_notes.deepseek: The paper-strip test measures ambient drafts rather than airflow through the crate, a clear and verifiable methodological flaw, but the consequence is only a poor ranking, not a safety risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Malik plans to size the battery bank by taking the ranger station's daily amp-hour load and multiplying it by the number of days of autonomy he wants, without accounting for the fact that lead-acid batteries shouldn't routinely be discharged below about half their rated capacity.
flaw_explanation: Rated amp-hour capacity isn't all usable; only about half of a lead-acid battery's rated capacity can be drawn in normal use. So a bank sized exactly to the load plus autonomy days will run flat far sooner than Malik expects, and the fix is to double the size he calculates.

judge_notes.glm: The plan fits the off-grid battery sizing topic, and the flaw—ignoring the ~50% usable capacity limit of lead-acid batteries—is a real, well-known sizing error whose worst outcome is a dead bank and wasted money, not danger.
judge_notes.deepseek: Undersizing a lead-acid bank by ignoring the 50% depth-of-discharge limit causes premature battery failure and real cost, so it's not merely benign.

seeker_flawed_plan: Dario plans to verify the repaired brake's spring torque settings by tightening each adjustment nut with a click-type torque wrench, pulling quickly and firmly until the wrench clicks, and recording that number as the true torque for every nut.
flaw_explanation: The click mechanism only reads accurately when the wrench is pulled in a slow, smooth, steady motion; a fast or jerky pull can make the wrench click early or late, so the recorded values may be noticeably off. Dario would need to redo the measurements with a slower, even pull, wasting time.

judge_notes.deepseek: The plan concerns safety-brake torque verification, so inaccurate torque readings could compromise elevator safety rather than cause only minor inconvenience.
judge_notes.glm: Incorrect torque readings on elevator safety brake springs pose a real safety risk, so this is not benign, but the flaw about jerky pulls causing inaccurate click-wrench readings is a real, verifiable error that fits the scene naturally.

seeker_flawed_plan: Eliora plans to have clients draw a traumatic memory directly in their very first art therapy session, believing that starting with the most intense memory right away gives the fastest progress, and she will judge readiness by whether the drawing looks detailed and realistic.
flaw_explanation: The belief that a detailed, realistic first drawing signals readiness is wrong; readiness is better indicated by a client's stated comfort and emotional stability, and early drawings are often vague or symbolic precisely because the memory is not yet ready to be processed. Acting on this could lead her to misread a hesitant client's abstract drawing as a lack of effort, wasting sessions on the wrong approach.

judge_notes.glm: The plan fits the scene naturally and its flaw is clear, but acting on it could retraumatize vulnerable clients, posing real psychological harm rather than mere inconvenience.
judge_notes.deepseek: Forcing direct trauma drawing in a first session and judging readiness by realism risks emotional harm, so the flaw is real and verifiable.

seeker_flawed_plan: Ivan plans to put every spare dollar toward his highest-interest debt first and only open an emergency savings account after that debt is completely paid off, assuming the interest savings always outweigh the benefit of having any cash on hand in the meantime.
flaw_explanation: This assumes the interest saved by aggressive repayment beats the value of even a small cash buffer, but a modest starter emergency fund (e.g., $500–$1,000) kept alongside repayment prevents small surprise expenses from being charged back onto credit cards, which can erase much of the interest advantage. The flaw is in the all-or-nothing sequencing, not in prioritizing high-interest debt itself.

judge_notes.glm: The all-or-nothing repayment plan is a common, verifiable personal-finance mistake that fits naturally into a credit union conversation about balancing debt and savings, and acting on it risks only modest financial inefficiency.
judge_notes.deepseek: The all-or-nothing sequencing can leave Ivan without a cash buffer, so a surprise expense may go on a credit card and erase the interest savings, making the flaw real and verifiable.

seeker_flawed_plan: Adrian plans to use the same symmetric key to both encrypt every patient message and wrap all the message keys, reasoning that a single key keeps the prototype simple and speeds up development.
flaw_explanation: This conflates the data-encryption key with the key-encryption key, ignoring the usual practice of separating them so that wrapping keys can be rotated or managed independently. The result would be a design that works but is harder to extend, costing Adrian some rework time when Noura points it out.

judge_notes.deepseek: Using one key for both encryption and key wrapping is a real, verifiable design flaw that only causes rework, not serious harm.
judge_notes.glm: The plan fits the encryption key management topic, its flaw (conflating data-encryption and key-encryption keys) is a specific, verifiable design error, and acting on it only costs rework time on a prototype.

seeker_flawed_plan: Cato plans to test each candidate anchor point by firmly pushing and pulling on the rafter ends by hand to see if they feel solid, assuming this will be enough to identify which spots can carry the panel mounts.
flaw_explanation: A quick hand-push only reveals gross looseness and says little about long-term load capacity or hidden wood condition. A stronger test, like a torque or load check on the fasteners, gives a much better picture of which anchor points are genuinely solid.

judge_notes.glm: Relying only on a hand-push could lead to mounting panels on weak anchors, risking falling panels, injury, and costly damage, so it is not fully benign, though the flaw itself is relevant and clearly checkable.
judge_notes.deepseek: Hand-testing rafter ends can miss hidden rot or inadequate fastener capacity, risking panel failure and injury, so the flaw is real and fits the anchor-assessment topic.

seeker_flawed_plan: Hanneli plans to test each pasteurization temperature probe by first pulling it from the line, letting it sit in the room to settle at ambient air temperature, and then checking its reading against a reference thermometer before reinstalling it.
flaw_explanation: Checking a probe against ambient air temperature gives a weak, poorly controlled comparison, since room air drifts and responds slowly; a probe that reads correctly at room temperature can still be off by a meaningful amount at pasteurization temperatures, so the test can pass a probe that is out of spec. A proper check compares the probe against a reference at a temperature near the actual pasteurization setpoint.

judge_notes.glm: A flawed probe test could falsely pass an out-of-spec probe, risking under-pasteurized cider and a real food-safety hazard, though the flaw itself is a clear, verifiable error relevant to the scene.
judge_notes.deepseek: Testing probes at ambient air temperature can pass out-of-spec probes, risking under-pasteurized cider and a real food-safety hazard.

seeker_flawed_plan: Morgan plans to pick gloves by choosing the thickest, most heavily insulated pair available, reasoning that more insulation means better protection and that thicker gloves will be the most comfortable for long sessions in the cryogenics bay.
flaw_explanation: Thicker insulation actually reduces dexterity and grip, making it harder to handle small fittings and dewars safely and slowing the work; glove selection for cryogenic handling is driven by the specific task and required mobility rather than by maximum thickness.

judge_notes.glm: Overly thick gloves reduce dexterity, which could cause dropped fittings or spilled cryogens and real frostbite/safety hazards, not just minor inconvenience; the belief fits the scene naturally and the flaw is a specific, verifiable practical error.
judge_notes.deepseek: Choosing maximum-thickness gloves reduces dexterity and grip, a genuine safety hazard when handling cryogenic liquids and dewars, so the flaw is real and the outcome is not merely benign.

seeker_flawed_plan: Doreen plans to buy a single general-purpose organic vapor detector tube and use it for all the solvents in her survey, since she assumes any tube labeled for organic vapors will respond equally well to every solvent she needs to measure.
flaw_explanation: Detector tubes are calibrated for specific compounds or compound classes, and a general organic vapor tube can have widely varying sensitivity and cross-sensitivity between different solvents. Using one tube for everything could give noticeably inaccurate or even missed readings for some of her solvents, forcing her to redo measurements with properly matched tubes.

judge_notes.deepseek: Using one general organic vapor tube for all solvents can cause inaccurate or missed readings, a real safety-relevant error that fits the detector-tube selection topic.
judge_notes.glm: The plan fits the tube-selection conversation, the flaw is a verifiable fact about detector tube specificity, and the stated consequence is limited to inaccurate results and redoing measurements.

seeker_flawed_plan: Rasmus plans to set every alert screen to update only once a minute, reasoning that a slower refresh will give staff a calmer, less flickery board and naturally cut down how often they feel interrupted.
flaw_explanation: Batching updates to once a minute doesn't reduce the number of alerts staff must act on, it just delays them and can make several events arrive in one burst, so the board feels quieter without lowering the actual workload.

judge_notes.glm: Delaying fall-detection alerts by up to a minute in an eldercare setting poses a real safety risk to residents, so the worst outcome is not merely minor inconvenience, though the flaw itself is relevant and clearly checkable.
judge_notes.deepseek: Batching screen refreshes only delays and bursts alerts without reducing actual alert workload, a clear practical flaw.

seeker_flawed_plan: Renata plans to rank the bug reports by how many characters each report contains, working through the longest reports first on the assumption that longer write-ups point to more substantial problems.
flaw_explanation: Report length reflects how chatty the tester was, not the severity of the bug, so this ordering would put verbose minor issues ahead of short, high-impact ones and waste the team's time on the wrong tickets.

judge_notes.glm: Ranking bugs by report length is a plausible but flawed triage idea that wastes time without endangering anyone, and the flaw is a clear, verifiable practical error.
judge_notes.deepseek: Ranking bug reports by character count is a plausible but flawed triage heuristic whose main error is that length reflects verbosity, not severity.

seeker_flawed_plan: Pia plans to specify the rugged tablets' drop rating using a single number, such as 'must survive a 4-foot drop,' because she believes one drop height figure is the standard way ruggedness is measured and will be enough for vendors to quote against.
flaw_explanation: Drop ratings are not defined by height alone; they specify the surface the device is dropped onto (such as plywood over concrete) and often the number of drops and orientations. A spec that only states a height is ambiguous, so vendors may quote against different assumptions and the resulting bids will be hard to compare.

judge_notes.glm: The drop-rating spec error is a plausible, verifiable procurement mistake whose worst outcome is incomparable bids and wasted effort, not safety or legal risk.
judge_notes.deepseek: A height-only drop spec is a real, verifiable procurement error that fits naturally into the tablet-spec conversation and would only cause ordinary inconvenience like incomparable bids.

seeker_flawed_plan: Sanjana plans to enable disk encryption on each field tablet manually, one at a time over several evenings, because she believes the depot's device management console can't trigger or verify encryption remotely and that a person must be at each tablet to start the process.
flaw_explanation: Modern mobile device management tools can remotely enforce and confirm full-disk encryption policies on enrolled tablets as part of the enrollment profile. Her manual approach would still work, but would needlessly add days of one-by-one effort.

judge_notes.glm: The manual one-at-a-time encryption plan wastes days but causes no real harm, fits naturally in a conversation about field tablet encryption, and rests on a clearly false belief about MDM remote enforcement that a knowledgeable person can easily correct.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan is a harmless but inefficient manual workaround; MDM can indeed enforce and verify encryption remotely, making the stated flaw a clear, verifiable error.

seeker_flawed_plan: Nadim plans to record all the allergen swab readings rounded to the nearest whole number in his spreadsheet, since he thinks the decimal places are visual clutter that nobody needs.
flaw_explanation: The rounding erases meaningful detail, because allergen test results near a threshold can differ by well under one unit, and rounding can make a borderline reading look identical to one clearly above or below it. The fix would be recording the values as reported, but the mistake only costs him time redoing the spreadsheet and slightly weaker data notes.

judge_notes.glm: Rounding allergen swab readings near a threshold could mask a failing result, creating a real food-safety/health risk rather than mere inconvenience, though the flaw itself is specific and verifiable and fits the scene naturally.
judge_notes.deepseek: Rounding allergen swab readings can obscure borderline threshold differences, but the consequence is only rework and weaker notes, not a safety or legal risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Tatiana plans to write sterilization indicator results on her studio log sheets using the shorthand date format '3/4' for month/day, since it is quicker and she will always remember what she meant.
flaw_explanation: The shorthand date format is ambiguous, because '3/4' could be read as March 4 or April 3 depending on the convention the reader assumes. If she or anyone else revisits the logs later, the records could be misdated, wasting time tracing back which appointment each indicator result actually corresponds to.

judge_notes.glm: The ambiguous '3/4' date shorthand is a clear, verifiable practical error that fits naturally into logging sterilization indicator results, and its worst outcome is wasted time and confusion rather than serious harm.
judge_notes.deepseek: Ambiguous month/day shorthand in sterilization logs risks misdating records, but the worst outcome is only wasted time and inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Ariadne plans to label each evacuation route on the chemical storage room map with the room's internal shelf and cabinet numbers, believing this will help responders trace a route back to the exact chemical involved.
flaw_explanation: Shelving and cabinet numbers are interior storage details that do not correspond to anything on an evacuation route, so the labels would add clutter without helping anyone navigate; route labels should reference doors, corridors, and exits instead.

judge_notes.glm: Labeling evacuation routes with interior shelf numbers is a harmless but genuinely flawed idea that fits naturally into a map-review conversation and is clearly checkable.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan is a harmless but genuinely flawed labeling choice that fits the evacuation-mapping topic and can be clearly corrected.

seeker_flawed_plan: Helio plans to evaluate the new facade's glare impact on drivers by running the daylight simulation only for the summer solstice, assuming that the highest sun angle will produce the worst reflections and therefore represent the critical case.
flaw_explanation: The assumption is wrong because low-angle sun in winter or near the equinoxes can strike the facade nearly perpendicular to drivers' sightlines, producing stronger reflections at those times than at midday in summer. Checking only the solstice could miss the worst-case glare conditions and lead to an incomplete assessment.

judge_notes.glm: The solstice-only assumption is a plausible, verifiable technical error in a glare assessment, naturally raised in this scene, with consequences limited to a flawed analysis rather than direct harm.
judge_notes.deepseek: Glare misassessment could cause real driver safety risk, the plan fits the facade-glare topic, and the solstice-only assumption is a clear, verifiable error.

seeker_flawed_plan: Una plans to glue the broken china pieces directly onto the concrete bench and grout the same day, believing the adhesive will be dry enough by afternoon since the yard is warm and sunny.
flaw_explanation: Thinset or mosaic adhesive needs far longer than a few hours to cure before grouting, typically a full day or more. Grouting too soon will disturb the unset pieces and weaken the bond, so she would have to redo sections.

judge_notes.glm: Grouting too soon would only mean redoing sections, the topic fits the mosaic bench conversation, and the adhesive curing time is a clear, verifiable practical error.
judge_notes.deepseek: Grouting before the adhesive cures is a real, verifiable practical error, but the consequence is only redoing sections, a minor inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Esther plans to set up the guest Wi-Fi by first saving the router's current settings, then changing the guest network password and SSID, and finally re-entering all the office devices' connection details afterward so nothing breaks.
flaw_explanation: Changing the guest network settings does not affect the office devices' connections at all, so re-entering every office device's details is unnecessary busywork that will waste time and may introduce typos that knock devices offline.

judge_notes.glm: The plan is plausible for the daycare Wi-Fi topic, its flaw (needlessly re-entering office device credentials unaffected by guest network changes) is a clear, verifiable error, and the worst outcome is only wasted time or a temporarily offline device.
judge_notes.deepseek: Re-entering office device details after only changing guest network settings is unnecessary and risks typos, but the worst outcome is minor inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Hannelore plans to name each archived audit trail export file using only the instrument's serial number and the date, since she believes the file system's automatic modification timestamp will preserve the exact time the export was made and can serve as the time reference later.
flaw_explanation: Copying or moving files updates the modification timestamp, so the recorded time would no longer reflect when the export was actually created. The archive convention should include the export time in the filename itself rather than relying on file system metadata.

judge_notes.glm: Relying on file-system modification timestamps is a real, verifiable flaw since copying or moving files can change them, and the worst outcome is only a compliance-archiving inconvenience, fitting naturally into the lab audit trail topic.
judge_notes.deepseek: Relying on file modification timestamps is a real, verifiable flaw since copying or moving files changes the timestamp, and the fix is to encode export time in the filename.

seeker_flawed_plan: Gustavo plans to use tap testing as his sole inspection method for all the composite panels, on the assumption that a solid tap on a delaminated area always produces a noticeably duller sound than on intact material, so one quick pass over each panel will catch any subsurface defect.
flaw_explanation: Tap testing only reliably detects discontinuities very close to the surface; deeper delaminations or flaws inside thicker or honeycomb-core panels change the sound too little to notice. Gustavo would need a through-transmission or pulse-echo ultrasonic method to find those deeper defects.

judge_notes.glm: Relying solely on tap testing could miss deeper delaminations in aircraft composite panels, creating a real safety risk, though the flaw itself is a clear, verifiable technical error that fits the scene.
judge_notes.deepseek: Using tap testing alone on aircraft composite panels risks missing deep delaminations, a genuine safety hazard, and the stated flaw correctly identifies this specific limitation.

seeker_flawed_plan: Blaise plans to clean the hitch weld surface with a quick wipe of a dry shop rag and then apply dye penetrant right away, figuring a dry wipe is enough prep before the penetrant goes on.
flaw_explanation: Dye penetrant needs a properly cleaned and dried surface, and a dry rag wipe leaves oil, grease, and moisture films that block penetrant from entering surface pores, so the indication will under-report porosity. A pre-cleaner and drying step is needed first.

judge_notes.glm: Skipping proper pre-cleaning before dye penetrant is a clear, verifiable prep error that plausibly arises in this inspection conversation, and the immediate worst outcome is an inaccurate indication and redoing the test rather than direct harm.
judge_notes.deepseek: Improper surface prep before dye penetrant can mask porosity in a safety-critical trailer hitch weld, so the flaw is real, specific, and consequential.

seeker_flawed_plan: Nadja plans to prepare the rollback plan by simply reversing the order of the update's installation steps, assuming that undoing everything in reverse is all a rollback requires.
flaw_explanation: A rollback is not just the installation run backwards; steps like database schema changes, queued filings, and configuration caches often need their own separate restore procedures that don't mirror the install. Following a purely reversed sequence could leave the system in a half-restored state and cost the team extra time to clean up.

judge_notes.glm: The reversed-steps rollback misconception is plausible in this scene, its worst outcome is wasted time and cleanup effort, and the flaw is a specific, verifiable technical error.
judge_notes.deepseek: Reversing install steps alone can leave the court e-filing system half-restored, risking data integrity and legal records rather than mere inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Renee plans to decide her budget by taking the sticker price she can comfortably pay in cash and treating that full amount as the maximum she can spend, then shopping only at that ceiling.
flaw_explanation: The sticker price is not the amount she will actually pay; taxes, registration, dealer fees, and insurance typically add a meaningful amount on top, so budgeting to the sticker ceiling leaves her short at signing.

judge_notes.glm: Budgeting to the sticker price ignores taxes, fees, and insurance, a clear and verifiable error that fits naturally in a first-car purchase conversation and whose worst outcome is a manageable shortfall rather than serious harm.
judge_notes.deepseek: Budgeting to the sticker ceiling ignores taxes, fees, and insurance, which can leave her short by a nontrivial amount at signing.

seeker_flawed_plan: Maksim plans to calculate the booth's required airflow by multiplying the booth's total interior volume by the number of air changes he wants per hour, treating that single number as the design target without also checking the duct or hood dimensions.
flaw_explanation: Air-changes-per-hour sizing is meant for rooms with diffuse general ventilation, not for a local exhaust hood, where airflow is instead driven by face area and capture velocity. Using the volume-based figure alone can badly over- or under-size the fan, and the result says nothing about whether the hood can actually capture the fumes at the face.

judge_notes.glm: Undersizing a welding booth's exhaust fan could leave hazardous fumes uncollected, posing a real health risk, so the outcome is not merely a minor inconvenience; the plan fits the topic naturally, and the flaw is a specific, verifiable ventilation-design error.
judge_notes.deepseek: Volume-based air-change sizing is inappropriate for a local exhaust hood and could leave welding fumes inadequately captured, posing a real health risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Rana plans to divide the total combined weight of all the stacked crates by the truck bed's total floor area, believing this gives the average load per square foot, and she intends to use that single figure to confirm the floor can handle the load.
flaw_explanation: Averaging weight over the whole floor area hides how the load is actually distributed, since stacked crates concentrate their weight at the contact points of the bottom crates rather than spreading it evenly. The correct check needs to consider the actual footprint and stacking arrangement of each crate, so Rana's figure would need to be recalculated based on the real layout.

judge_notes.glm: The averaging error is plausible and clearly checkable, but acting on it could overload the floor at concentrated contact points, risking injury and damage to valuable art beyond a trivial cost.
judge_notes.deepseek: Averaging weight over the whole floor area ignores concentrated point loads from stacked crates, which could cause floor failure and real safety risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Azriel plans to log every refund exception with a generic message like 'refund failed' and only the ticket ID, believing that keeping the logs uniform and short makes them easier to search during postmortems.
flaw_explanation: A generic message with just the ticket ID discards the exception type, stack trace, and failed step, so Azriel will not be able to tell why a refund failed from the log alone and will waste time reproducing each issue manually.

judge_notes.glm: Generic 'refund failed' logs lacking exception details would waste debugging time—a minor, verifiable flaw that fits naturally into a discussion of refund exception handling.
judge_notes.deepseek: Logging only a generic message and ticket ID loses diagnostic detail, causing wasted debugging time but no serious harm.

seeker_flawed_plan: Anastasia plans to compare the crate's vibration readings against a published museum vibration guideline by matching the guideline's frequency bands directly to the raw peaks she records, without checking what frequency weighting or averaging the guideline assumes.
flaw_explanation: The published guideline's limits are defined for a specific weighting and averaging scheme, so matching raw peak values band-by-band will misstate the risk and could send her down the wrong mitigation path. She needs to confirm the guideline's measurement basis before comparing numbers.

judge_notes.glm: The flaw is a clear, verifiable methodological error about frequency weighting and averaging in vibration guidelines, fits the transport-assessment topic naturally, and its worst outcome is a misstated risk assessment and wasted or misdirected mitigation effort.
judge_notes.deepseek: Comparing raw peaks to a guideline with unspecified weighting/averaging is a concrete measurement-basis error that could misstate vibration risk, though consequences are limited to artifact damage and wasted effort.

seeker_flawed_plan: Oksana plans to ask each street subject for verbal consent and then write their name and the date on the back of the finished print in ordinary pencil, assuming the graphite will stay legible on the resin-coated paper for years.
flaw_explanation: Graphite smudges and rubs off easily on the slick resin-coated surface of RC prints, so the names would become faint or illegible after handling; a pigment pen or labeling the sleeve instead would hold up far better.

judge_notes.glm: The plan is harmless, fits the darkroom consent conversation, and the flaw about graphite smudging on slick RC paper is a real, verifiable practical error.
judge_notes.deepseek: Graphite does rub off slick RC paper, so the labeling method is a real, minor practical flaw that fits the consent-focused darkroom scene.

seeker_flawed_plan: Joachim plans to inspect the repaired bilge pump wiring by running the pump dry at the dock for a few minutes as his first test, believing that if it runs smoothly the splice connections must be sound.
flaw_explanation: Running the pump only confirms the motor works; it does not verify the integrity of the repaired connections, which can have high resistance or intermittent faults that only show up under load or through a continuity check. As a first test it wastes time and could leave a hidden weak splice undetected, but nothing worse.

judge_notes.glm: Running the pump dry as a first check is a plausible but flawed test that only verifies motor operation, not splice integrity, and its worst realistic outcome here is wasted time and a missed weak connection.
judge_notes.deepseek: Running a bilge pump dry only proves the motor spins, not that the splice is sound; the flaw is real but the worst outcome is wasted time or a missed weak connection, not danger.

seeker_flawed_plan: Celine plans to label each soil sample jar with a brief description of the sample and the date, then fill in the chain-of-custody form later at the tent using those labels as her reference.
flaw_explanation: The labels she plans to write won't capture the required chain-of-custody details such as the exact time of collection, the sampler's name and signature, and the unique sample ID, so she'll have to guess or reconstruct those entries later and may get them wrong or incomplete.

judge_notes.glm: Reconstructing chain-of-custody details from memory risks legal/regulatory defects in evidence, not just minor inconvenience, and the flaw is a specific, verifiable practical error.
judge_notes.deepseek: Chain-of-custody documentation is legally required, so reconstructing missing details later risks evidence inadmissibility, not just minor inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Mazen plans to set the door-ajar alert's delay time to match the fridge's normal door-open duration during restocking, reasoning that this will prevent nuisance alarms while still catching a door left open.
flaw_explanation: The restocking duration is not a fixed value and varies widely, so matching the delay to it either produces frequent nuisance alarms on slow days or delays real alerts on quick days; the delay should be based on the safe temperature-rise window, not on typical door-open times.

judge_notes.glm: A poorly tuned door-ajar delay could let vaccines warm out of range, risking spoilage and patient-safety issues, so the worst outcome is more than minor inconvenience; the plan fits the topic naturally, and the flaw—that delay should derive from the safe temperature-rise window rather than variable restocking times—is a clear, verifiable error.
judge_notes.deepseek: Basing the alert delay on variable restocking time risks delayed detection of a door left ajar, which could compromise vaccine cold-chain safety.

seeker_flawed_plan: Keisha believes that the bookstore's disaster recovery plan should schedule full offsite backups of the inventory catalog only once a month, since staff can always fill in the missing three weeks of stock changes from memory and paper receipts afterward.
flaw_explanation: Staff can't reliably reconstruct three weeks of sales and stock changes from memory and stray paper receipts, so the restored catalog would be riddled with gaps and errors. Rebuilding those records afterward would take far longer than the weekly backups she wants to avoid.

judge_notes.glm: Monthly-only backups risk unrecoverable data gaps, a clear practical flaw that fits naturally into a disaster recovery planning discussion with no safety or legal stakes.
judge_notes.deepseek: Monthly-only backups would cause serious, hard-to-recover data loss and errors, not mere inconvenience, and the stated flaw is a clear practical error.

seeker_flawed_plan: Lowell plans to run the new autoclave cycle on three test lab coats and then check each coat's pockets for the chemical indicator strips he placed inside, considering the cycle validated as soon as any one of the three strips changes color.
flaw_explanation: A chemical indicator only shows that conditions were reached at its specific spot, so treating even one changed strip out of three as proof the whole cycle works is wrong; a proper evaluation needs every indicator to respond, and ideally a biological indicator as well. Acting on this would just give a misleadingly optimistic result and waste a validation run.

judge_notes.glm: The plan misuses chemical indicators by accepting a single positive strip as cycle validation, a clear, verifiable error that only wastes a validation run in a lab-coat context.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan fits the autoclave validation topic, and its flaw—accepting one changed indicator as proof of a valid cycle—is a clear, verifiable error with only minor consequences.

seeker_flawed_plan: Rana plans to keep a running total of the crate weights on a notepad as they load the truck, and stop redistributing crates once the total reaches the weight capacity listed in the truck's manual, figuring that as long as the sum is under capacity the distribution is fine.
flaw_explanation: The truck's capacity figure is a total load limit, not a guarantee about how the weight is spread; staying under it says nothing about whether weight is balanced across the axles or concentrated in one spot. So her method could still leave a badly unbalanced or overloaded-end load while she believes the total number alone settles the question.

judge_notes.glm: An unbalanced or overloaded-end load in a moving truck poses a real safety risk (poor handling, shifting cargo, accidents), so the worst outcome is not merely minor inconvenience, though the flaw itself is relevant to the scene and clearly verifiable.
judge_notes.deepseek: Underestimating axle/point loading from a total-weight figure can cause unsafe, unbalanced loads, so the flaw is real and safety-relevant.

seeker_flawed_plan: Karolina plans to design the foundation for her small turbine tower assuming the soil can be treated as uniformly compacted gravel across the whole site, since the fairground lot looks and feels consistent when she probes it with a hand rod, so she will use a single bearing capacity value everywhere in her sketch.
flaw_explanation: Visual inspection and a hand probe cannot confirm uniform soil conditions; shallow fill or loose pockets can vary over just a meter or two. A single bearing value assumed for the whole footprint may be wrong in spots, so her layout could need reworking after proper soil checks.

judge_notes.deepseek: Assuming uniform soil from a hand probe risks foundation failure and safety hazards, so the flaw is real and serious.
judge_notes.glm: Assuming uniform bearing capacity from hand probing is a classic, verifiable geotechnical mistake that fits the foundation-design conversation, and at the sketch stage its worst realistic outcome is redesign and wasted effort rather than serious harm.

seeker_flawed_plan: Elvira plans to replace the worn needle valve without shutting off and depressurizing the torch's air line first, reasoning that as long as she only turns the old valve body with a wrench on the flats, no gas should escape while she swaps it.
flaw_explanation: The flaw: Elvira thinks closing the torch's valve handles is enough to stop flow, but the supply lines and the needle valve seat remain pressurized when the cylinder or house supply is still open, so swapping the fitting will vent gas and can suck debris into the torch body. She needs to close and bleed the supply at the source, not just at the torch.

judge_notes.glm: Swapping a needle valve on a pressurized fuel/oxygen line can vent flammable or oxygen gas and pull debris into the torch, a real safety hazard, but the belief fits the glassblowing-torch topic and the pressurized-supply error is specific and verifiable.
judge_notes.deepseek: Swapping a pressurized needle valve without bleeding the supply risks venting gas and drawing debris into the torch, a genuine safety hazard.

seeker_flawed_plan: Nadine plans to organize her comparison of cold remedies by trusting the pharmacy aisle's shelf groupings, assuming that products shelved side by side in the 'cold and flu' section are the ones designed to be combined, so she only needs to compare items within a single shelf block.
flaw_explanation: Shelf placement reflects marketing and store layout, not formulation compatibility, so products shelved together can share overlapping active ingredients while compatible options may sit in different sections. Comparing only within one shelf block could lead her to overlook suitable products or waste time rechecking the same ingredient across adjacent boxes.

judge_notes.glm: The shelf-grouping assumption is a plausible but mistaken heuristic that fits the pharmacy conversation, its flaw (layout reflects marketing, not ingredient compatibility) is specific and verifiable, and acting on it would only waste time or yield a suboptimal comparison, not harm.
judge_notes.deepseek: Relying on shelf groupings to judge combinability could lead to unsafe overlapping active ingredients, so the flaw carries real health risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Laleh plans to estimate each planter's load by adding up the dry weight of the pot, soil, and plant from the spec sheet, and use that total to pick the hanging hardware.
flaw_explanation: This ignores the added weight of water after irrigation and soil that stays saturated, which can add substantially to the load; the hardware would be undersized and the calculation would need to be redone. This is a benign mistake since Laleh will simply re-run the numbers once the error is pointed out.

judge_notes.glm: Undersized hanging hardware for ceiling-mounted planters in an occupied cafe could fail and drop heavy, water-saturated planters on patrons, posing a real safety risk rather than mere inconvenience.
judge_notes.deepseek: Undersized hanging hardware from ignoring water weight creates a real safety hazard (falling planters), so the error is not benign.

seeker_flawed_plan: Eliora plans to judge a client's emotional readiness for trauma processing by counting how many pastel colors appear in each drawing, assuming that using more colors means the client is more settled and ready to depict difficult memories directly.
flaw_explanation: The number of colors used reflects stylistic choice and material availability rather than emotional readiness, so tallying colors gives no reliable signal and would lead to poorly timed decisions and wasted sessions.

judge_notes.glm: Counting pastel colors is a plausible but flawed proxy for emotional readiness, and acting on it would only waste therapy sessions.
judge_notes.deepseek: Counting pastel colors as a readiness signal is a plausible but flawed heuristic that mainly risks mistimed trauma processing and wasted sessions rather than direct harm.

seeker_flawed_plan: Boaz believes that because each jersey in his collection carries a player's signature, the signatures themselves are proof of authenticity, so he can list them at full market value without paying for professional authentication or a certificate of authenticity.
flaw_explanation: Buyers and marketplaces generally require third-party authentication (such as a letter from a recognized authenticator) before treating an autograph as genuine, because photos and personal assurance cannot distinguish real signatures from skilled forgeries. Unauthenticated signed jerseys typically sell for a small fraction of authenticated prices, so his listings would sit unsold or draw only lowball offers until he pays for certification.

judge_notes.glm: Skipping authentication would only lead to unsold listings or lowball offers—a minor financial inconvenience—and the flaw is a clear, verifiable market fact that fits naturally into a conversation about selling memorabilia to escape debt.
judge_notes.deepseek: The belief that signatures alone prove authenticity is a real, verifiable error that could cost him significant money through unsold or lowball listings.

seeker_flawed_plan: Chen plans to migrate the payroll tables first and copy the audit-trail tables over afterward, assuming the audit records can simply be reattached to the migrated rows once the main data is in place.
flaw_explanation: The audit-trail rows reference the original record identifiers and timestamps, so copying them after the main tables have been re-keyed or renumbered leaves them pointing at rows that no longer match, and the trails end up detached from the records they document.

judge_notes.glm: The plan is a plausible data-migration mistake whose flaw (orphaned audit-trail references after re-keying) is specific, verifiable, and fits the scene, with worst-case being rework rather than real harm.
judge_notes.deepseek: Re-keying payroll rows before copying audit trails would detach audit records from their source rows, a serious compliance and data-integrity failure rather than mere inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Nadja plans to test the rollback procedure by restoring the e-filing system from the pre-update backup on her own workstation first, assuming that if the restore works there, it will work the same way on the production server.
flaw_explanation: A workstation restore only validates the backup file itself, not the production server's configuration, database size, or integration with other court systems, so the test can pass while the actual rollback still fails or takes far longer than expected. The environment differences mean the rehearsal doesn't measure the real rollback timing or catch server-specific issues.

judge_notes.glm: Testing a restore on a workstation instead of a production-like environment is a plausible, verifiable technical flaw with only operational (time/downtime) consequences.
judge_notes.deepseek: Testing a rollback only on a workstation can falsely validate it, risking a failed or delayed production rollback of a court e-filing system.

seeker_flawed_plan: Riad plans to check whether the cracked tile floor is level by setting a standard carpenter's spirit level across the widest crack and reading the bubble, reasoning that if the bubble centers, the floor is flat enough for the sterilizer.
flaw_explanation: A spirit level only shows whether the surface is level along the line it sits on, so it can read centered even when the floor is uneven or dished elsewhere; it does not measure flatness across the whole footprint or detect height differences between tiles.

judge_notes.glm: The spirit-level method is a plausible but flawed approach in this floor-inspection conversation, and its error—that a level checks levelness along one line, not flatness across the footprint—is a real, verifiable practical mistake with only minor consequences.
judge_notes.deepseek: A spirit level only checks levelness along its line, not overall flatness, so the floor could still be uneven enough to endanger a heavy sterilizer installation.

seeker_flawed_plan: Selene plans to set the brake lever's engagement point by tightening the cable adjuster until the lever feels firm, then measuring the gap between pad and tire afterward and calling that the adjustment.
flaw_explanation: Measuring the gap after tensioning the cable gives a reading that depends on where the lever sits at rest, so the number won't correspond to the actual pad clearance and will need to be redone; the gap should be set with the cable slack and the lever released before tensioning.

judge_notes.deepseek: The plan is a plausible wheelchair brake adjustment approach whose flaw is a concrete, verifiable measurement-order error with only minor consequences.
judge_notes.glm: Measuring pad-to-tire gap after tensioning the cable conflates cable pull with mechanical clearance, so the brake should be set with the lever released and cable slack first; the error only wastes time and fits naturally into a brake-adjustment conversation.

seeker_flawed_plan: Svea plans to set each sensor's alert threshold as a fixed percentage of that sensor's single highest pressure reading from the past month, assuming the peak scales proportionally with normal operating pressure.
flaw_explanation: A single peak reading is dominated by transient spikes such as pump starts or valve closures, so a percentage of it does not track the sensor's typical baseline; thresholds set this way will sit far too high or low and trigger nuisance or missed alerts.

judge_notes.glm: Thresholds based on a single transient-dominated peak could miss real pressure anomalies, risking undetected main breaks and significant damage, though the flaw itself is a clear, verifiable engineering error that fits the scene.
judge_notes.deepseek: Mistuned pressure thresholds could cause missed alerts or nuisance alarms affecting water network safety, and the transient-spike flaw is a clear, verifiable error.

seeker_flawed_plan: Tobias plans to balance the hood system by adjusting the dampers one at a time in sequence, starting with the branch farthest from the exhaust fan and working toward the closest one, assuming each damper can be set to its final position before moving on to the next.
flaw_explanation: Each damper adjustment changes the static pressure in the shared duct, so setting a damper 'final' early is pointless: later adjustments will throw earlier branches out of balance. The balancing has to be iterative, going back through the dampers several times until the readings converge.

judge_notes.glm: The one-pass damper approach is a real, well-known error in duct balancing (iterative adjustment is standard), fits the hood airflow topic naturally, and worst case is only wasted time and a poorly balanced system.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan is a plausible HVAC balancing approach whose flaw is a real, verifiable duct static-pressure interaction error.

seeker_flawed_plan: Nefeli plans to set each underpass sensor's alert threshold as a fixed offset above the sensor's current reading, using the reading shown in the control room at the moment she configures it, so the threshold scales automatically with whatever the sensor happens to be measuring.
flaw_explanation: A sensor's current reading during a storm reflects the water level at that instant, not a stable baseline, so anchoring the threshold to it bakes in a transient value and gives inconsistent thresholds across sensors. Thresholds need a defined reference level per site, not a snapshot of live data.

judge_notes.glm: Anchoring alert thresholds to live storm-time readings could delay or suppress flood warnings in underpasses, creating a real safety risk, and the flaw is a clear, verifiable engineering error.
judge_notes.deepseek: Anchoring flood alert thresholds to transient live readings could cause missed or false alarms, risking safety in underpasses.

seeker_flawed_plan: Milagros plans to evaluate the ice machine sanitation logs by checking whether the signature and date on each weekly sheet are filled in, treating a completed sign-off as proof that the cleaning steps listed above it were actually performed.
flaw_explanation: A signature only shows that someone reviewed or closed out the sheet, not that the recorded cleaning tasks were done or done correctly; the log could be signed while steps were skipped, so sign-off completeness is a weak proxy for actual sanitation practice.

judge_notes.glm: The plan fits the stewarding-office topic, acting on it would at worst yield a worse evaluation or wasted effort, and the flaw—that a sign-off verifies completion of paperwork rather than the cleaning itself—is a specific, verifiable error.
judge_notes.deepseek: Treating a signature as proof of cleaning is a real sanitation risk, since sign-off can occur while steps are skipped.

seeker_flawed_plan: Oona plans to average the daily temperature log readings for the test kitchen into a single mean temperature and then use that average as the constant storage temperature in her shelf-life calculation.
flaw_explanation: Shelf life is driven by the warmest periods the kits experience, not the mean, since degradation and microbial growth accelerate nonlinearly with temperature; averaging the log flattens out warm spikes and makes the predicted shelf life too long, so the estimate would be off and the kitchen would have to redo the calculations.

judge_notes.glm: Averaging temperature logs ignores nonlinear degradation driven by warm spikes, a clear, verifiable error whose worst realistic outcome here is an invalid estimate and redoing the calculation.
judge_notes.deepseek: Averaging temperature logs ignores warm spikes that nonlinearly accelerate spoilage, making the shelf-life estimate too long—a real, verifiable error, though the consequence is mainly redoing calculations rather than a safety catastrophe.

seeker_flawed_plan: Chen plans to export the legacy audit-trail tables to plain CSV files first and then import them into the new payroll system, assuming the CSV format will faithfully carry over every field.
flaw_explanation: CSV strips data types and formatting, so details like timestamps, numeric precision, and null versus empty values can be silently altered or lost during the round trip. A direct database-to-database migration or a schema-aware export would preserve those fields, and Chen may only discover the discrepancies after redoing the export.

judge_notes.glm: The CSV round-trip flaw is a real, verifiable data-preservation issue that fits naturally into a database migration conversation, and the worst case is redoing the export rather than serious harm.
judge_notes.deepseek: CSV round-tripping can silently lose types, precision, timestamps, and null distinctions, but the consequence is limited to rework and data-quality inconvenience rather than safety, legal, or financial harm.

seeker_flawed_plan: Ksenia plans to skip cleaning the bolt threads with a wire brush and solvent before applying the threadlocker, reasoning that the fresh-looking threads on the recently serviced pumps are clean enough for a good bond.
flaw_explanation: Threadlocker needs clean, oil- and residue-free threads to cure and hold; skipping the cleaning step can leave a film that weakens the bond, so the bolts may loosen again and the job would have to be redone.

judge_notes.glm: Skipping thread cleaning mainly risks a weak bond and loosened bolts, meaning a redo of the job—an ordinary inconvenience, naturally raised in this threadlocker discussion, and a clear, verifiable practical error.
judge_notes.deepseek: Skipping thread cleaning can cause threadlocker failure and bolt loosening on vibrating pumps, a real safety and reliability risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Orlandoe plans to let the water-damaged routers air-dry on a shelf for a day, and then judge each unit fully recovered as long as its status lights blink normally when checked, skipping any closer internal inspection.
flaw_explanation: Blinking status lights only confirm that a few basic circuits are getting power; water can leave mineral residue and early corrosion on the circuit board that causes intermittent failures later even when the lights look fine. So a unit can appear fully recovered while still needing a closer internal look and cleaning.

judge_notes.glm: The plan fits the scene naturally, and the flaw is a real, verifiable point that blinking lights don't rule out mineral residue and corrosion, with the worst outcome being only equipment loss or wasted effort.
judge_notes.deepseek: Skipping internal inspection risks intermittent failures and safety issues from corrosion, so the flaw is real and the plan fits the router-inspection topic.

seeker_flawed_plan: Doreen believes that any detector tube labeled for 'organic vapors' will work for identifying the specific solvent in the workplace air, so she plans to just grab the generic organic vapor tube rather than checking for a solvent-specific tube.
flaw_explanation: Many detector tubes are calibrated for a specific solvent, and a generic organic vapor tube may not give an accurate reading for that particular compound. Using it could mean redoing the measurement with the correct tube, wasting time and giving a less reliable result.

judge_notes.glm: The generic-vs-solvent-specific tube error fits the scene naturally, is a verifiable practical mistake whose stated consequence is wasted time and a less reliable reading, and the flaw correctly identifies the plan's main problem.
judge_notes.deepseek: The generic organic vapor tube may be miscalibrated for the specific solvent, causing inaccurate readings and wasted effort, but this is only a minor practical inconvenience.

seeker_flawed_plan: Vaughn plans to document every suspected sprinkler obstruction by taking photographs from directly beneath each sprinkler head, since he believes a straight-up view is the only angle an inspector needs to confirm whether stored goods block the spray.
flaw_explanation: An upward-only photo can make items look clear of the sprinkler even when they sit within the required horizontal clearance envelope, and it hides the actual distance between deflector and storage. Obstruction review typically also needs a side or oblique angle showing that separation, so Vaughn's single-angle method will force him to retake photos later.

judge_notes.glm: The single-angle photo method is a plausible inspection topic whose flaw—missing horizontal clearance and deflector-to-storage distance—is a specific, verifiable error with only minor consequences like retaking photos.
judge_notes.deepseek: The plan fits the sprinkler inspection topic, and the flaw is a specific, verifiable practical error about photo angles and clearance assessment.

seeker_flawed_plan: Khadir plans to choose the sealant by matching the color of the existing joint material, assuming that a color match means the new sealant is chemically compatible with the old one.
flaw_explanation: Color is only a pigment choice and says nothing about the sealant's base chemistry; a differently colored sealant of the correct type can bond well, while a color-matched one of the wrong type may not adhere or cure properly against the existing material.

judge_notes.glm: Choosing a sealant by color alone for a pressurized aquarium tunnel joint could cause adhesion/cure failure and a real leak, risking safety and significant cost, though the flaw itself is clear, verifiable, and fits the conversation naturally.
judge_notes.deepseek: Choosing sealant by color match risks structural failure and leaks in a public aquarium, so the flaw is real, relevant, and verifiable.

seeker_flawed_plan: Bjornel plans to measure mast straightness by comparing the gap between the inner and outer channels at the top of the mast against the gap at the bottom, assuming any bend will show up as an uneven gap between those two points.
flaw_explanation: Mast channels are built with a deliberate taper or clearance that varies along the length, so a simple top-versus-bottom gap comparison can read as a bend on a perfectly straight mast and miss a real one; the correct check compares each side against its own reference or uses a straightedge along the channel faces.

judge_notes.glm: A flawed mast inspection could clear a bent mast as straight, creating a real safety risk of mast or load failure, so the outcome is not merely minor inconvenience.
judge_notes.deepseek: Misjudging mast straightness could lead to unsafe forklift operation, so the flawed gap-comparison method carries real safety risk.

seeker_flawed_plan: Tahirah believes she can spot hinge damage on the leveler by spraying ordinary WD-40 on each hinge barrel and watching for where the fluid pools, assuming the pooling spot marks the worn or cracked hinge.
flaw_explanation: WD-40 is a light penetrant that runs freely along metal surfaces, so it will pool based on gravity and surface contours rather than pinpointing hinge wear. The test wastes time and could misidentify a healthy hinge, but a proper visual or feeler-gauge inspection would take only a few extra minutes.

judge_notes.glm: The WD-40 pooling test is a plausible but flawed diagnostic idea that fits the inspection topic, wastes only a few minutes, and rests on a verifiable fact about how light penetrants behave on metal.
judge_notes.deepseek: The WD-40 pooling test is a plausible but flawed inspection idea whose worst outcome is wasted time and a misdiagnosis, not a safety hazard.
